text: I love buzzbars
I honestly think this is better than El Toro; the ejector on this with a buzzbar is crazy.
Really don't know what you'd want me to say that hasn't already been said. Absolute gem for this nice local park.

Has to be the most likable coaster in existence. What it's able to do to your body with only 78 feet of height is hard to even comprehend. Row 3 is my favorite spot on Phoenix - the first drop and turnaround aren't anything special here (the back is far better for both) but in this particular row I am always *flying* out of my seat for the rest of it. Thanks to those buzz bars the ejector goes so hard that I have literally banged my knees on the back of the car in front of me. Add in the dopamine hit of watching 20-30 second dispatches like clockwork and this is a special coaster with as much natural charm as the park it headlines.

This ride is so much fun! At first I thought it should not have won the Golden Ticket Award for best wooden coaster, but ever since I rode it back in 2024, I get why it is. The airtime is absolutely spectacular, some of THE STRONGEST I've EVER felt on any ride. The buzz bar restraints make it even better. BY FAR, in my top 25 best coasters I've ever rode, and I would LOVE to visit Knoebels again just to ride it. 10/10

This is the best airtime I've ever felt on a coaster. The layout feels like it was made with the restraints in mind. I never thought i would ever get so high out of my seat it was honestly terrifying. It felt like I could of been ejected out of the ride at any second. I can see why this ride is a bit of an award-winner.

This is probably the coaster I have felt the least secure riding which makes it as good as it is. The loose restraints combine beautifully with all the hill to create airtime moments that constantly throw you out if your seat. I would go so far to say that, if the restraints were any tighter, the ride wouldn't be half as good as it is. It feels like getting pushed down a bumpy road in a grocery cart.

AMAZING ride. First big coaster I've ever really been on and boy was it wonderful. The awesome airtime paired with the incredibly scary restraints, or lack there of, really made this ride a hoot to ride. The tunnel in the beginning really caught me off guard in it's length. The ride itself was rather short but the airtime was incredible especially at the end.
Good ride but it’s only floater and it didn’t blow me away pretty overrated
Just a basic, old wooden coaster that gets way too much praise due to its buzz bars. The airtime isn't what it's made out to be and the layout is simply basic.
The airtime is insane. The last few hills are indescribable. There are no downsides to this coaster. It’s just flat out amazing.

This ride is the definition of small but mighty. The airtime this ride provides is unlike any other coaster mainly because of the restraints the ride has. The PTC Buzz bars provide ample room for riders to get the maximum amount of airtime.
This ride is nothing short of a miracle.

one of the craziest and funniest rollercoaster ever,an airtime machine basically without every type of harness.
i sped all of my rides on it laughing and screaming,the first time was almost scary,i didn't expect that airtime form a coaster realtivly small and not so fast

This crazy coaster is essentially a heavily intoxicated version of Comet at Waldameer. From the start, the ride spares no time, taking you straight into a pitch-dark tunnel. After this surprisingly long element, the coaster rises high into the air, offering cool views of Knoebels. Then, the ride drops down a very fun first drop, into the best airtime that I've ever experienced. Seriously, every single hill feels like it's trying to fling you off of the roller coaster and onto the tracks. Every jump, every hill, every leap offers amazing airtime, thanks to an unrestrictive buzzbar and NO SEATBELT WHATSOEVER. And even better, the ride is super long. I'm surprised that this isn't the record holder for most airtime on any coaster, because Steel Vengeance's ejectors don't have crap on this beast. There is no other ride in the world that produces better airtime than this. Even though I do find it just a bit overrated seeing how airtime is really the only thing this ride has to offer, just the sheer willpower of the out of your seat moments mostly overpowers that. You've been on roller coasters, but you haven't been on Phoenix.

I normally don’t like wooden coasters because of rattle and whiplash. But even after riding 50 coasters this week and having an incredibly sore neck, Phoenix was legit FUN! I have no idea how those restraints are legal — my 13 year old coaster-loving skinny nephew next to me thought he was going to die, as he spent the whole ride practically standing up. I came up so many times and landed on the seat divider in between us.
the golden ticket was right......... kinda 9/10
The most ejector you can get without restraints.
One of the best wooden coasters in the world. The airtime your getting is honestly kind of scary. Amazing coaster that is surprisingly smooth.
Im so proud that this was my first ever coaster at the park I grew up going to so yeah FOR ME this is and always will be the best coaster in the world. and obviously my #1 at knobles
he's green for an amazing reason
Was really excited for this one and just don’t understand the hype after riding it multiple times.
Holy moly, the airtime on Phoenix is INSANE. It's super smooth, and only has a buzz bar.

Last year, I rode Jack Rabbit at Kennywood. The ride gave me a small taste of the insane airtime that buzzbars give you, literally allowing you to fly up from the seat with each airtime pop, but it was too short in length and height to really leave you with much. Phoenix is basically Jack Rabbit if it was much longer, taller, had a better layout, and was smoother. The entire ride you just get thrown in every direction, literally high enough to hit the buzz bar from underneath, getting thrown off by laterals, and that double up double down is just unreal. The seats are comfortable, the tunnel starting off the ride is mad dark and kinda funny, the pacing is excellent, the operations were perfect almost all day leading to minimal waits, and the airtime, airtime, AIRTIME!!! 10/10. Ride it in the back for violent ejector if you want, but I found that I actually preferred the flojector in the front row.

I’m a bigger but not that big guy and the buzz bar almost touched my lap.  I was in my seat for a few of the hills and the ones with airtime it was just a quick pop.  It was fun but def over hyped.  Ravine flyer is the best woodie in Pennsylvania.
A coaster I want to keep riding, but new name is really f**king bad(0.5 points deducted because of the changed name… Monimo RUSH? Please return it to the original name ‘T Express’)
i just went to everland for this ride but please change the name back to T express
Row 17 is the best seat I highly recommend it

I went to Everland just for this ride, and tbh It's not a great theme park. The line was superslow and neverending. The first drop is brutal, and you get insane airtime on the first camelback, then it becomes repetitive but still intense. The problem is that you can't ride it again because the line takes forever. I was in row six, I guess it's better on the back row. I would say that the first 15 seconds of this coaster are probably the most intense I've ever had on any coaster. Does it justify the hassle? It's up to you.

Rode it on the opening year, the ride was glass smooth, the first drop was amazing and the airtimes were incredible. Shame that Everland chose the route of 208 retrack rather than properly taking care of the existing wooden tracks.
The biggest and the most beautiful Intamin prefab. The first drop is insane and it packs some great ejector in other spots as well.
The best wooden coaster out there with the best lap bars I have ever felt
Great ride, better than most, maybe even better than El Toro

lowkey so fun., Went front row, scared to ride, but that first drop packs a punch and somehow I really had so much fun. First big wood coaster ! It was really hot that day though so the slow line wasn't helping. PLEASE either tie your hair up while riding or remove jewellery cause my hair knotted on my necklace and I had to rip it off. It wasn't much but it does show how intense this ride is. epic tho

This is the best roller coaster in Korea. The first drop is amazing and turn around section before mcbr is intense. Balder section after mcbr is repetitive but full of air time. In conclusion, T express is the best ejector air time roller coaster in Korea.
I got blessed to born in South Korea cuz I can ride this when I want to ride this

Rode this 5x today for the first time. First drop looks like it should hurt and doesn't, instead is glass smooth. Second fave wooden after The Voyage. 

Has some hard spots, hasn't been taken care of well. Should consider having wheels for the top and bottom of the track AND outside to stop the coaster from slamming side to side around different turns. Long trains so I actually prefer the front as it propels you up into the airtime. 1.6km long. 18 trains. TONS of fun.

If Everland took better care of their park and added a few other real coasters, they'd be a serious stop in Asia. So much land and so little must do attractions.

The first drop is one of the best I've experienced, definitely the best on a wooden. The intensity is both good and bad. I probably just have an old person neck, but the next minute was pretty much one solid headache. Rode it twice front and towards the back, I would say that was true in both places. Went on a week day in mid-April and the line was less than 20 minutes each time.
This ride is pure perfection. Unbelievable. Beats El Toro by a mile.

This ride has been my #1 ever since my first ride. That first drop cannot be described by words, and the ejector moments are so unbelievably powerful it's the strongest airtime I've ever experienced out of my 200+ credits. T express is not even comparable to El Toro. This ride absolutely smashes it, and I believe it is the absolute perfect coaster in existence. This ride beats Iron Gwazi, Velocicoaster, Fury 325, Maverick and Steel Vengeance for me. If you're even near South Korea, and if you are a thoosie, I absolutely urge you to spend extra for this coaster. Just do it.

It is currently ranked at my number 2 right behind ArieForce One, the first drop is the best in the world, the first cammelback is demented, and it pulls some great g’s although it does loose a lot of steam over the rides long duration, but pacing wasn’t an option in the cons.
The layout is little repetitive which makes the balder section to be boring, but still it is a great coaster
Best coaster i've ridden, it was very intense, everything you would want in a wooden coaster. Layout is very long and good, no dead spots really, a very good coaster.
This coaster is everything you'd hope it to be! Which is to say a perfect mix of Toro/Balder. Also has some truly insane moments hidden in the incredibly long layout.
I remember my last ride on this getting covered in bugs and I wouldn't have traded that for anything

The original dragster was by far the most intense physical feeling I've ever experienced. Imagine the top acceleration of a tesla times three. Your heart and stomach were literally left at the station. I am so sad to see Top Thrill 2 struggling right now, but hope that I get to ride it someday. Still, nothing will compare to the original hydraulic launch. It was SO powerful. I'll be chasing that crazy feeling forever!

This is the greatest 17 seconds of all time and I think most people would agree with me. That launch is just unbelievable and still my favorite one, that speed is something extremely hard to beat and experiencing it on a coaster is just mind boggling. The top hat is a blur of speed, positives, laterals and even some great ejector going over the top. Such a simple coaster but it's an absolute must do experience. A fair amount of people like ka more but the lap bars, lack of a trim making the drop better and smoothness just give this the edge for me.
Launch go zoom

I first rode this in 2019, and 2 more times in 2021. I miss the old Dragster because it was special. The launch was the 1st 100 mph launch I've ever experienced and it was WILD. I will forever miss this version, and I hope to ride TT2 soon. 10/10.

This first launch will forever be missed. Front row rides were always epic, especially at night. The restraints I always found to be quite comfortable since it is just a lap bar. Launch is pretty smooth considering how fast you are going. Going up the top and dropping doesn’t do as much for me as the first launch, but it’s still crazy. You are still flying after the drop. I am very excited to ride Top Thrill 2, but not having that fast launch is concerning. The elements of Top Thrill 2 still look insane, but it might be hard to match the original’s intensity because of a launch that is the definition of breathtaking.
It was so good, going from - 0 to 120 that fast is insane.

The launch and speed absolutely carried this version of the ride. The high acceleration combined with the face flopping velocity made this one heck of an experience. It's a real shame that the mechanical issues were way too overwhelming for the park.

I am excited to ride Top Thrill 2 when it reopens but it will be difficult to top the original. Dragster was amazing. The lap bars gave it such a cool open feeling and the view at the top is great. First launch was special.

Such an intense ride that has an acceleration kick that is hard to find at other theme parks! Loved the restraints, and the station music. Curious to see what will the revised experience bring for the 2024 season.

This ride was stupid awesome. The launch scared the bajeebers out of me. The drop was crazy. it went by so fast, that I was still processing it when I hit the breaks. I loved everything about this masterpiece

As of the day I have written this review, August 15, 2026, it has been FIVE years since my favorite ride ever shut down forever, now making this coaster a distant memory in the past. Now I would make a generic review of it, but this ride deserves something much better, and instead I will tell the story of me and Top Thrill Dragster.

It started off with my first ever visit to Cedar Point back in August 24, 2019. I was new to the coaster community, and vaguely familiar with the rides at that park. When I saw stuff about Dragster initially, I said “NOPE” and thought there’s no way in heck I’d get on that thing. I mean, I rode Millennium that day, but the thought of going 100+ mph on a ride seemed way too much. So I didn’t ride it that trip, I also skipped Wicked Twister as well. Now about the latter, I heard rumors about its removal back in 2019, and I wanted to ride it before it shut down, so I convinced my Dad to return to Cedar Point and ride.

Now how does this relate to TTD? Well early in the morning I was determined to try and face my fears and ride it, until I then got too scared and chickened out of line. We would spend the rest of the day riding the other coasters, including Wicked Twister. It wasn’t until the end of the day, the temptation of getting on TTD seemed to get even greater. Finally, it got to the point where I convinced my Dad that I was ready to face my fears and conquer Top Thrill Dragster. I remember waiting in line, for at least an hour, looking at all the trains coming and going, being so scared and nervous. I knew that it was coming, but I had to turn to God, and face my fears and get on the ride. Finally, our train pulls in, and I get inside the train, seat belt and lap bar down, and ready to ride. We pull up to the launch track, and I hear “arms down, head back, and hold on”. My heart is pumping like crazy, I’ve never been so anxious on a ride in my life like that before, thinking to myself, any moment now. Finally, the train connects to the launch, and we take off…

And that single moment would become a lifelong memory that I will forever cherish. The launch was so raw and powerful, I remember screaming “OOOHH! OH MY GOSH!!!!” The top hat was so big and grand, getting a view of the park up that high, and then spiraling on the way down back to the station. It was arguably the single greatest moment of my entire life. I remember feeling completely shaken after getting off, but absolutely loving it to death. So much that it truly made Cedar Point for me what it was when I was a kid, all because of how much I loved this one coaster: So much that I even begged my Dad to stay another day JUST to ride this again, in which we did. That feeling of accomplishment that day is something I will always remember, as that moment was what truly made me a roller coaster enthusiast, and truly made me believe I could do anything if I could do that. All thanks to God, who helped me face my fears that day and create a lifelong memory I will never experience again 😢.

I have only ever ridden Top Thrill Dragster four times, and each one of those rides I will forever cherish, with my last being June 25, 2021. I hate how something that I loved so much could shut down and disappear forever. Moreso, I hate how something that I loved so much could ruin somebody else’s life, which was the reason this ride closed forever. My deepest condolences go out to the victim whose life was ruined by the accident, and my deepest condolences to this amazing roller coaster that I will never be able to ride ever again 😭. I will never forget the day when it was announced that this coaster would be closed forever, it was a major turning point in my life and made me realize that nothing is safe from being destroyed or removed forever. It might have been the single worst day of my entire life, all the hope and praying just for nothing…

I may ride Top Thrill 2 soon, but it’s a completely different ride experience than this, and tbh, I don’t think it’ll be better than this. Looking back, thinking about how long ago those memories are now as a 17 year old has made me deeply distraught recently, to the point where I have literally cried grown man tears all because of one coaster. But you know what, if one coaster can make a grown man cry, it must be a good coaster, and darnit it was my favorite ride ever 😭. I wish none of this had happened and that this ride would still exist, but it is what it is… All I can say is that I am grateful for my Dad and for God for blessing me this amazing ride and the amazing memories it gave me. I hope someday someone can design and engineer a launch that get just like the hydraulic launch on TTD and use it for a huge stratacoaster that avoids the issues caused by Dragster. Preserve that type of joy for future generations so they don’t have to go through the same grief that I have for four years, and let them experience the same joy I did back in 2019 at 10 years of age. Even though I wish I could’ve ridden it more, I at least got to ride it that many times, let alone more than once, and I hope someday, in heaven, I will be able to ride this beauty again. Until then, Fly High Top Thrill Dragster, my favorite roller coaster ever, up into the heavens in the sky.

R.I.P. 2003-2021 ❤️🏎️🎢

I think they improved it with TT2, but the sheer anticipation of this one was completely off the charts. When you pull out in front row and are about to launch and there is literally of grandstand of people watching you literally felt like the star of the park for a few seconds.

I rode this once back in 2013, never rode it again before it was converted because it was always down. I was so scared back then but I enjoyed it. I really like the twist as you come down. It was just really short, Top Thrill 2 is an upgrade.

RIP the OG Dragster. The best launch of all time. That top hat with those lap bars was absolutely insane. Will be missed. So lucky I got to ride for the first time this just two weeks before it closed forever.

Every time I think about my coaster rankings, I debate this ride in my head.  How can I still have it so high on my list?  I rode it originally back in 2004, which was a time the world barely knew that such levels of thrill were even possible.  Now almost 20 years later and close to 150 more coasters under my belt, how do I still rank this in my top 5?  It simply comes down to that initial adrenaline rush.  The first time I ever rode this, it was an epiphany.  I had ridden other launched coasters at that point--Mr. Freeze is at my home park of SFSL.  But this is a whole other level of insanity.  The launch is just nuts.  Just when you think you can't go any faster it keeps on going.  It is FAST.  The forces make your body react with adrenaline.  It is such a rush.  The hill and the height are barely even a factor compared to the launch.  Is it 1 trick pony?  Perhaps, but it is the best trick I've ever experienced on a coaster.  It is super short?  Of course it is.  But I can't think of a better way to spend 15 seconds with my clothes on.

I miss you so badly. You were the ride that officially turned me into a roller coaster enthusiast. Going 120 mph in 4 seconds and spiraling 420 feet straight down is a feeling you can’t replicate. RIP to the ultimate game changer.
Great launch and tophat. I thought the overall experience Kingda Ka was much better though.
This is the best ride ever created

Very mixed feelings on the old Top Thrill Dragster.

On the one hand, this is the coaster that made me fall in love with rollercoasters. Dad forced me to ride the first year it opened. I was crying tears of misery and despair awaiting my impending death looking at this monstrosity climbing above me as a little kid. Frankly I'm not even sure how I was allowed on given my state. It's all a bit fuzzy. But what I do remember is that feeling from the first launch. By the time the incredibly short ride had ended, I was still crying but they were tears of joy from the insane intensity of this ride, and my Dad was sure smug about the whole thing. Thus sparking a lifelong addiction....

I rode this thing dozens of more times throughout it's lifespan and my opinion on it changed over the years. Lines were always long and half the time I visited the park it was down, and as I grew older and braver, I began to prefer longer coasters over the very short burst of intensity that this ride offered. Still, it will always hold a special place in my heart as the ride that started it all, for me at least.
Too short, but a record breaker none the less
For years this was my number one coaster. With over 1,200 rides on it… and operating it for a season. This coaster has a special place in my heart. RIP OG TTD.

Still the best launch I've experienced.  Yea, it's too short, but I always made this a top priority visiting CP.  Love the location within the park, views are spectacluar from up 400ft.  Launch amazing and I really loved how the park leaned into creating a spectacle out of this ride.  It turned heads all day, every day, even if you have been on it a hundred times.

Top Thrill Dragster's launch was the single most insane moment on any roller coaster I have ever experienced! It's indescribable, the fiery sensation of intensity that hurtling down the far-too-short launch track provoked within your body will never be matched. Getting ripped down that launch track with only a lap bar was heavenly, while the subsequent tophat would actually bring you to heaven before plummeting you back to Earth again. Top Thrill Dragster was only two moments, but those moments were so memorable that the ride's runtime didn't matter. It's a shame Cedar Fair's poor management of the park led to the tragic accident that abruptly ended this coaster's life.
Pretty awesome being so fast, but you feel quite disoriented when you get off!
This launch is powerful! Speed is incredible and it has good floater airtime over the hills. But the real star in this park is another coaster...
The launch was  breathtaking (literally) especially in the first row but the rest of the layout was really boring. The breaks directly after the launch suck

The launch is just mind blowing, the acceleration goes on for soooo long, you literally can’t move in your chair. Bit disappointed there are trim brakes on the first airtime hill  but maybe it’s necessary. The rest of the layout is nothing special (apart from a few near misses) but it’s still fun because you’re doing it all at such speed. It does lack theming around the ride itself.
INSANE LAUNCH, great sense of speed, blending with some underrated airtime as a bonus. World class coaster

The launch is absolutely crazy, rode it before the opening of Falcon’s Flight. The rest is kinda meh but then its true that with that kind of speed (approx 120km/h after launch) you have to make the track long so that the ride doesn’t seem super short but I wish they would add at least a second fun element…I would have taken anything

The former world’s fastest roller coaster certainly lives up to that title and in a way that is perhaps more exhilarating than previous speed record holders. Instead of having the high speed launch go into a short layout, this is one of the longest roller coasters in the world. Which has both pros and cons to that design.


While there is not much for thematics on the ride, Ferrari World chose to use the ride itself as a visual spectacle for guests and riders to watch. With both an observation deck and large windows in the queue providing unobstructed views of the entire ride. Especially with the launch track being right next to the queue area. There is a strict no loose article policy, but the park offers a double sided shelf to store items at no cost to the rider. Prior to boarding goggles are distributed to riders and compared to other rides that require goggles, these were comfortable and did not impede the experience in any way. The trains use a simple seat belt and T-Bar design that is quite open and exposed during the ride.


Immediately Formula Rossa rolls up to the launch with little for thematics, however this launch is incredible. In the front row the launch produces insane wind that highlights how fast you are going. The other rows do lack that experience and it is less impressive, but regardless the acceleration keeps going. Having had the opportunity to experience the three high speed accelerators, Formula Rossa’s launch is the longest accelerating. What sells the launch is it has one extra second of acceleration compared to the original Strata launches. It is not much, but I noticed that slight extension and the launch does reach its peak at the end of the launch track. That being said, this is a tame launch in the sense of intensity. The acceleration is steady and the train tracks smoothly. To best compare it, the launch felt similar to Top Thrill Dragster’s launch, but a bit tamer. In the front I did notice small items were pelting me in the face and the goggles, but in the rows further back that was not a concern.


The hill following the launch is heavily trimmed, it is noticeable yet not uncomfortable and it did not detract from the rest of the layout. The top has a strong floater over the crest and the twist to the left creates strong laterals. The rest of the layout is very drawn out and not intense in the forces, but the speed maintained is impressive. Banking that low to the ground at that speed is exhilarating in a way that not many other rides could do, but it is never too much. The entire layout in the front is a steady blast of wind that does not let up and each hill ranges from near zero-g to mild floater airtime. Even though it lost speed from the brakes it is not reflected in the course and it does feel like it was once the world’s fastest coaster and it may have the highest average speed on any coaster in the world. The final few hills produce good floater airtime and the brakes throw you forward with the sudden acceleration. Perhaps most impressively the ride tracks very smoothly and there is not a rough or shaky moment at any point.


All around an incredible ride experience no matter what but it really shines in the front row. It may be a longer wait for it but I had no issue waiting a few cycles to get that experience. Very little in the world can compare to it.
It is kinda fun but that do not have anything special without speed
Incredible speed, the launch is incredible but it looses alot of speed after the first hill

What can I say it really is fast =) but honestly , the launch really feels like you are being shot from the gun as someone in the comments mentioned. The rest of the layout is kinda boring but you are still thinking about the launch. I was thinking between 4.5 -5 and gave it 5 just because of the moment I experienced on my first row launch.
Fastest Rollercoaster in the World (right now) it is just amazing the launch the intensity and the element of just being so fun just makes me want to re-ride.

That first launch, wow that's awesome. You needed to wear special goggles for a very good reason. It's impossible for the rest of the ride to compete with the launch, so by comparison it feels a little flat, but in reality you're still moving fast, there's some nice sections with a bit of airtime and a smile for anyone brave enough to take on the fastest coaster in the world.

I actually enjoyed this ride a lot more than I thought I would. My favorite roller coaster in the country. It also has the world's best launch. It feels like being shot out of a gun. It's so fast it's ridiculous. It also uses a lot of that speed, which is the layout's main focus. It's a very long ride too and has some unsuspecting floater and laterals. Great ride.

Best launch in the world. I feel people hate on this ride too much for what it lacks or isn’t, and don’t give it enough credit for what it IS. What it isn’t is some random cloned RMC hybrid coaster with 200 seconds of gradual floater airtime. What it IS is the world’s fastest roller coaster, a ride with the best overall pacing in the world, some epic transitions, unrivaled smoothness, and a sense of pure fun and bliss. This is a unique, must-ride experience for anyone. Oh also, the forces and laterals on the turns are genuinely incredible and contribute to the sense of sheer speed.
Just a gr8 ride.

THIS RIDE IS SOOOOO FAST (fastest ride in the world) and it is amazing! The FORCES ARE GREAT, and since it is super fast you SPEEEEED THROUGH EVERY ELEMENT! I love the speed on this ride, but I was kinda expecting it to be faster. Still a great ride tho!
The Launch is absolutelly amazing. It feels like it never ends. The rest of the layout is weaker. The launch makes the ride.

The launch is amazing but after that the ride doesn’t really do anything, which seems like a missed opportunity since they had so much land and money to work with. All it does is turns and nothing else.

As a coaster enthusiast I was thrilled to visit Ferrari World and ride Formula Rossa as my 147th credit. I was not disappointed. The launch is fantastic, the top speed is face warping fast and the turns are more forceful than I expected (sustained 3g in the turns accoarding to my watches measurement). I also got some night rides on Formula Rossa and it was just amazing to do night rides on the coaster that I waited to ride all my life.

The best experience is in the front row. Prepare for some mind-boggling launch and speed.
The layout is drawn out and the train is slowed down just before the first airtime hill - but they have to do this, otherwise the ride would be too extreme. The first few hills offer floating airtime which I love.
God, what just happened, where am I?!

I've ridden a lot of roller coasters and people will ask me if I'm ever scared of a roller coaster. And I never really am. I don't feel anxious when I'm getting strapped in. I don't get nervous going up the lift hill. I never feel like I'm in actual danger. I feel thrilled, but I don't ever feel fear. Or at least that's what I would say if I'd never ridden X2.
I STILL DON’T KNOW WHAT THIS RIDE DOES
I don’t know what just happened, I’m gonna ride it again!

Wow. This thing should 100% be illegal, but I'm so glad it's not at the same time. It is so intense, and it has fantastic transitions from crushing positives to floaty negatives. The only con is that the ride's leg slamming is really bad, oh and it also pulls 3 hour waits because of trash capacity. I can look past the cons though because this is one of the best rides I’ve ever been on. Come out and ride this stupid thing! :)

Too disorienting for you to comprehend the forces you're feeling. Not terribly comfortable. Pretty bad operations. None of this matters because it's one of the only genuinely frightening coasters in existence

This ride is absolutely incredible, I had an idea of what to expect going in and it still shocked me. I hope they can smooth the ride a little, especially that second raven turn is seriously rough. Going up the lift hill overlooking the park at sunset was so picturesque.
I absolutely love this ride and it is not as rough as most people say. If you know how to ride it it is so fun. out of my about 100 coaster credits x2 is #1

X2 actually blew me away, even with all the coasters I’ve ridden, this thing is the most intense of all coasters. It’s more intense than I305, more than El Toro or Kingda Ka. It’s just insane. Unlike a free spin coaster, I felt like my ground point of reference was taken away while the ride was intentionally showing me or not showing me the next drop. My problem with this is that it was so incredibly rough, I felt like a rag doll being beaten with a baseball bat. My legs were flailing all over and my head hurt so bad. I went back the next morning and got another ride and maybe it was running smoother in the morning because I felt no discomfort the 2nd time and it was just as intense.

That first drop will forever be etched and live rent-free in my mind, it is completely out of this world to go down facing the ground, and last minute perform such a quick rotation. This thing feels unreal in the best way possible. Not to mention the fly-to-lies both of which are incredibly disorienting and remarkably fun! The ride definitely loses steam a bit on the turnaround, but it doesn't detract from the ride for me, and neither does the bounciness of the seats and rotation, it wasn't discomfortable in any way, inner or outer seat, as far as I remember.

X2 is INSANE! It's tall, fast, and so crazy that it doesn't even feel like a roller coaster. You reach a blistering 76 mph on a gigantic 20 ton ride vehicle as it simultaneously flips and twists you in ways you would never think are possible. One second you are being slammed down into your seat with wind howling in your face and the next you are floating out of it doing some sort of crazy inversion maneuver. And the last raven turn is crazy intense! My tip is to just keep your head back on the headrest. I love X2 so much and it has a very comfortable spot in my top 5.
Very intense

WHAT IS THIS THING?? One of the most insane roller coaster experiences I’ve ever had. You go over the first drop backwards at first, and then it spins you so you face the ground. Then you have the sensation of being piledriven nearly 200ft towards the ground. It's like willingly choosing to experience trauma and then, for some reason, after it's over, thinking "I wanna do that again."

X2 is the best ride in America if you can put up with a little pain as the cost for a S tier ride. This is not a ride you can relax on it is the most intense ride I have ever been on and while you have to ride defensively I don't believe that is a problem as it is so unique and different that you naturally cannot ride it like any other coaster. It's uniqueness and breakneck pacing make it the best ride I will ever experience until I make it to China/Japan to ride the variants.

Theming wasn't present when I went to the park (as far as I know, there is supposed to be a fire element and music, neither of which were present). This is a very unique ride, and its sheer intensity certainly not for everyone... Sometimes uncomfortable or has rattling, but I enjoy the thrills overall. It is a confusing and crazy experience. When I first went they could only run one train; I believe there was an issue with the other one? (Needed to buy a flash pass to get on the ride)
Headbanger at the very end

A unique coaster experience, for sure, but also a terrible one. The cars rotate so much that it is impossible to ever get your bearings and understand where you are and what is happening. That's not a fun time. I could see this concept working, but X2 ain't it. Rode it once and decided right then to never ride it again. Hated it, but giving it an extra half-star bump for innovation.

as much i love x2 in my opinion i hate how much it rattels at the end it got to the point i lot my freaking shoes like what the heck this is not acceptable for me as a person the height of a person that can litary ride everything that is barley there but can still ride is freaking not acceptable for a person under 13 years old or under and im one of them like that is my problem but i love how intense it is just bring back the audio and fireball please
By far the most insane roller coaster I’ve ever been on. Equal parts intense and terrifying. Best ride at Magic Mountain
This ride gives us a lot of intense moments, feels like flying off the track! But omg that raven turn really feels like a baseball bat just hit my legs. Ow
i loved it. the rotating carts made it so much smoother. i didnt have any comfort issues but it banged my friend's legs up

this ride is fucing insane, it took me like an hour to process everything that just happened. some people say it’s rough, but for me i was last row inside seat and it was not rough… this ride is just insane. I also like the restraints, I hate over the shoulder restraints but these are kinda nice… i didnt get stapled, they don’t have headbanging, and they feel loose and like you might fall out
So intense and crazy ride, it has just been running one train for a long time and it's pretty janky. The layout isn't actually that good compared to the other 4Ds but it's still awesome

Whoever thought to combine Maverick and Millennium Force into one coaster was bonkers, and I don't know why they built it at Kings Dominion of all places, and yet here we are. Intimidator 305 is possibly the most intense roller coaster in the world. Huge positive Gs, enormous giga level speed, and relentless transitions all happen at the same time, and with the wind in your face in the front row, you'll be begging this ride for mercy. Thankfully, there are breaks of airtime between all of the intense moments, which is what makes this ride work, as it does have a little bit of remorse. The new soft collars are even better than the old ones, so my only complaint about this ride is now out the window. This coaster is absolutely ridiculous and will probably get torn down for a more tame B&M or Mack giga in the next 20 years, so let's enjoy it while it's still kicking our asses.
This ride is INTENSE! It takes me to Greyzone city every time. Its my favorite ride in the KD park.

No roller coaster has messed me up more than Pantherian did. I was fortunate enough to ride it over and over on a hot summer evening and afterwards, I was in a daze. You plummet down 300 feet to the ground, lose consciousness, and wake up to your whole body floating out of your seat. Then, the ride tosses you around mercilessly while going 80+ mph. For me, this is one of the craziest successions of roller coaster elements out there. Pantherian offers an absolutely world class ride experience (unless you are unconscious the whole time).

I’m struggling with this review…not just because me sometime talk like caveman and not word well, but because my rides were a tale of two coasters.

My first three rides, literally minutes after gates opened, were a bit of a letdown.  It brought good - but not amazing - speed and intensity.  Airtime was limited, including a trim break that kills what could have been an epic pop.

My last two rides of the day, hours later, were a different story.  I greyed out on the first bank to the right, and the speed took me by surprise, with the wind reaching deafening levels.  I was rocked to the core in a way few coasters do.

I still have reservations about the lack of airtime moments and the layout, but for pure viciousness, it delivered.

I’m going to give this one more thought, provided all that craft beer hasn’t done irreversible damage after all these years.

Now, if you’ll excuse me, I’m going to stare into space and drool for a few hours.

UPDATED:  Giving it the benefit of the doubt.  Upgraded by a half-star.

The only roller coaster I get off wondering how it's legal. It's legitimately scary when you accumulate laps in quick succession and start to wonder if the increasingly strong greying on the first turn is going to lead to a blackout ride. Just an awesome creation that I would imagine will remain the most intense coaster in the world until the day it's gone - good luck finding anything else that feels quite like Pantherian. Also this is very much an old baseball stadium situation where I'd rather just keep calling it I305.

Still cannot believe that both Kings Dominion and Intamin approved this layout. "Let's drop riders 300 feet and then make a hard banked turn at ground level for 270 degrees" is such a ridiculous idea on paper, and yet it's the moment that makes the ride. Following that up with an insane sustained ejector hill followed by several low to the ground rapid transitions is just the cherry on top.

This is one of the most breathtaking layouts ever conceived, but the final third is significantly lessened by a trim. The new theming is a huge improvement, but I'd love to see them commit even further by adding temple ruins throughout the layout on the turns.
Absolutely brutal in the best way possible. So whippy and intense and leaves you out of breath. The only coaster on the planet like it. Insane and awesome
I'd give it 5 stars if it didn't feel like it was actually trying to kill me on that first turn.
Millennium forces cooler brother. Wish it had some air time with the speed. Otherwise unique experience.

Pantherian was the main reason I choose to visit King's Dominion, and it did not disappoint. I rode twice in the morning, and made a point to make it my last ride, where I was able to get 3 rides in. 

Pantherian is relentless from the first drop as it's sustained positive g-forces are unlike anything else I have riden. While not an airtime coaster, there is just enough airtime to allow your vision to return, before whipping you into another sharp turn.

Despite its intensity, this ride is smooth enough that it can be ridden multiple times.

The front row is the best row, as you can really feel the speed.

I finally got to ride the legendary Pantherian a few days ago to see if it delivered on the hype.  Overall, it's an amazing ride.  E-Rock and I got 3 rides early in the morning, which were fun but didn't quite deliver like we expected.  However, we came back later in the day for 2 additional rides and this was immediately after we had just gotten 2 quick rides on Dominator.  These last 2 rides hit WAY harder than the early rides.  It's the first time I ever experienced the "gray out" that a lot of riders talk about.  I've ridden a lot of intense coasters before like Skyrush, Maverick, Nitro, Afterburn and I had never experienced a gray out before.  I have 2 main issues with the ride.  First off, that trim brake on the 2nd hill really kills the air time.  They could have at least moved it to AFTER the hill.  Secondly, the 2nd half of the ride is just a bunch of turns with quick side-to-side transitions between them.  It needs a little more variety.  Throw in a Stengel Dive or an overbanked curve or something.  I've ridden 2 other Giga coasters and Pantherian comes in 2nd for me.  Fury 325 is my favorite and Millennium Force is my least favorite.  There's no denying that Pantherian is super intense and fun, but it doesn't quite make my top 10.
The perfect coaster for anyone that enjoys intensity. First turn is a guaranteed grey every time.

Oh my god. I rode this when I went to KD for a senior trip a month or two back, and before I go back to KD in a couple of days, I want to review this monster before I forget. But, WOW, this thing is insanity. It's very intense, but smooth. I've ridden easily at least 50 coasters, and out of all of those, this is the only one that made me gray out, and I fucking love it. I rode it, knowing I was probably going to gray out, and then the drop came, and there is zero warning beforehand. I got off this ride and literally jumped up and down like a toddler, and I'm a grown ass man. If you can handle the intensity, I STRONGLY recommend riding this beast.

This was my #1 for years, but it's still in my top 10.   I used to always gray out on the first turn, but now I do the "fighter pilot clench."  I clench major muscles - glutes, thighs, abs, biceps.  It works!  My gray-outs are either non-existent or mild.   Anyway, I love the speed and intensity, especially on the snap turns.  The best experience is after dark in front, where the first drop feels twice as big and the speed is magnified.   I just wish they could get rid of the trim on the last airtime hill.  I really miss "Gentlemen, start your engines" from the I-305 days.

Nicknamed “Millennium Forceless”, absolutely one of the most iconic coasters ever built, and certainly Cedar Point’s most iconic coaster (Besides Dragster 😭). When I first rode this in August 2019, this was at one point the tallest and fastest coaster I had ever been on, and it was the first Giga coaster I had ever ridden. I gotta say, it’s pretty good.
While this coaster doesn’t have the same sentimental importance to me as Dragster, and is nowhere near as good as Maverick or SteVe, it’s still one of Cedar Point’s top coasters for sure. It’s got a great location first off, sitting right next to Lake Erie. It also has one of the greatest first drops I have ever experienced on a coaster ever, partly due to its location as well as the sheer size of it. Other than that, the coaster is simply just fun as heck. Smooth, fast, scenic, exhilarating, and just pure fun. I hear people who call this ride forceless, and I disagree. While it pales in comparison in intensity to say, Fury or especially freakin’ I305, it still pulls some good intensity, especially on the first overbank after the drop. The biggest strength of this coaster however is a front row ride, which is one of the r get rarest that I have ever experienced in my entire life. Heck, the first time I rode it in the front, I was shaken from how fast it was, call that forceless! It’s no Fury front row, but it’s still 100% a worthwhile experience. If I had to make a complaint, I personally feel as if the layout is repetitive. I love how immense and sprawling it is, but I wish there was a greater variety of elements and not just a ton of overbanks.
Despite its shortcomings, Millennium Force is still one of the best coasters that I’ve ever ridden in my life. I feel as if in recent years this coaster has fallen in popularity, but you know what, I still think it holds up in the modern industry, and it’s genuinely a great coaster. While it may not be quite as good as Fury or I305, it’s still pretty great, and absolutely has a spot in my top 20. It’s definitely one of the best at Cedar Point, and serves as a pillar and a true icon of the coaster wars and American roller coaster engineering, still holding up a quarter century later. Now, I just hope this classic CP Intamin coaster still operates for years to come, and doesn’t meet the same fate as many other older Intamins (R.I.P. Top Thrill Dragster 😭, and Wicked Twister)

My current #2 (just behind Eejanaika), and the last of the S&S 4D models. In terms of smoothness, they definitely perfected the formula with this installation. My co-rider, who hates rough rides, enjoyed this! Just like Eej, Dinoconda packs unbeatable intensity, forces, and an amazing layout. While I prefer Eej for its brake run finale and feel that its roughness adds to the exciting, visceral experience, Dinoconda is just as extreme and I'd highly recommend it for anyone who finds Eej or X2 too rough! Just be aware of the low capacity of this coaster (why did this and Eej have to be at notoriously slow operations parks?!) and that it will close at the slightest bit of sustained rain.

Now is the only 4D coaster in China, however, the ride runs every 15 mins and will have a "nap" during the noon, which leads the EXTREMELY LOW capacity. Also the coaster is headbanging, especially on the first row of its direction.

The headlining attraction for PortAventura Park is an interesting case for me. Having done all of the B&M Hypers (and enjoying most of them) in the United States and hearing the claims that this is among the best of the bunch had me very interested. The verdict? It is fantastic! I was very pleased with my experience and it is my favorite ride in the park. From outside the park this ride creates a bold impression, it is massive. With its position on a hill it can be seen for miles and with the nature of B&M’s layouts the perfectly profiled hills and turns appear just as massive. In the park it still maintains that aura of scale, towering over Dragon Khan and being visible from all areas in the park. Perhaps even more impressive is how picturesque this coaster looks from within the park. The white and blue track pop against the sky and it is backdropped with a beautiful view of the coast miles away. Entering the attraction PortAventura made sure to take advantage of the stunning location and design by allowing guests to walk right under the ride and get unobstructed views of the surrounding area. Shambhala utilizes the staggered B&M Hyper train design and with the nature of those trains the extremes (front and back) are going to be the most desired seats. I only had the opportunity to ride twice with one ride in the middle and one in the back row. While I enjoyed the ride in the middle, the back row ride is where it performed the best. The lift is a standard hyper coaster lift with some of the best visuals you can get on a coaster. To the left is the beautiful shoreline and to the right is the rest of the park, once again selling the scale of the ride’s height. For the layout, I’ll be describing the back row ride, but the middle row ride was about the same but noticeably weaker. The drop is great as with a prolonged moment of floater air all the way down to the valley which dives into a quick tunnel and turns into a large airtime hill. A great moment of sustained floater airtime is felt across the train and it gets slightly stronger as it crests over. The ampersand turn is both a visually impressive and fun element, however it was not as intense as I had anticipated. Not a bad thing, but a tad underwhelming compared to other Hypers. The speed hill provides a great pop of airtime and the larger hills that follow all deliver quality floater airtime. A block brake follows and while it did slow the train down a little bit, it was not dramatic and the final hill still provided a good amount of air before concluding the ride. When it comes to tracking, the ride was quite smooth and there was not much rattling during the layout. With the smooth experience, solid layout and good airtime hills, it is a wonderful coaster. That being said, my one criticism is that it is a bit tamer than I had anticipated. Similar to the ampersand, I was surprised that there was not any moment of strong positive force that other B&M hypers have. While it is great to have a ride that flows that well, I would have preferred if the valley’s were a bit stronger to complement the airtime. That being said, that is a small criticism and it is still a great coaster and an experience that is worth doing multiple times.
My absolute FAVOURITE coaster of all time. Genuine perfection in a coaster, idc. Speed and airtime > inversion spam and you can't convince me otherwise.

Shambhala is an elegant, floater-air-filled hypercoaster offering wonderful views of the Catalonian seashore and exciting visual interactions with the looper Dragon Khan, which it arches over the top of. The first drop may be the best first drop I've ever ridden; the turnaround is a unique "ampersand" element that feels like an inversion but isn't. Immediately after that is a short speed hill that provides the ride's one pop of ejector air (mostly it is graceful and floaty).
This is also a physically beautiful ride, with the "Himalayan" theming around the station and its sky-blue and white paint job. There's a fake "splashdown" element that is really just for show, but it's a nice visual effect. The trains are lovely and comfortable, with staggered seats bearing B&M clamshell restraints that leave you feeling remarkably free and exposed. Toward the end of the ride, there is a midcourse brake run, and after that there's a turnaround and hill that don't do much. If I have one complaint it's that this ending is a tad anticlimactic.

Loses half a star because of mandated removal of glasses with straps on exactly 1 of my 7 rides (which I still do not understand to this day). Fantastic airtime all around and addictive to reride, and one of the most visually striking roller coasters in Europe. I love how when you're in the Asia area this ride looks like the Himalayas, and when you're in the Europe area this ride looks like the Alps. While the airtime is brilliant and every single hill hits, the dead spots come from the turnaround section and the section after the midcourse. The turnaround, while it looks incredible from offride, drags on quite a lot and I catch myself "waiting" for the next airtime hill to happen. The post-midcourse is followed by a similarly dull turn to the left, and another hill which is taken sliiiiiightly too slowly to leave a real impression. However, everything else is simply awesome, and one of Spain's strongest roller coasters with its plentiful air and spectacular splashdown moment as well.

Shambhala is imposing yet graceful. In the morning, it was almost too gentle before picking up some speed by noon. If you're into floater airtime there might not be a better ride in the world: The first drop is spectacular in the back while every hill has you out of your seat for several seconds. My favourite part is the ejector/flojector speed hill followed by the two hills framing the fake splashdown. The latter can even get you a little wet in the back rows.
The final stretch after the midcourse brake-run is a little underwhelming compared to the rest but it's still decent. 
The layout can be considered a bit repetitive offering one hill after another but I didn't mind too much: Shambhala is pure fun. Although I prefer Silver Stars second half which is more diverse. Unfortunately, Shambhala's throughput is embarrassing. It should be a people eater but sub-par operations hold it back.

Un coaster grandiose, qui au moment de notre ride était encore assez récent donc avec une certaine aura ! 
Une hauteur bluffante, des sieges confortables, et des lap bars qui ne sont pas trop restrictives et permettent de gratter encore plus d'air time ;) 
Un layout qui avec le recul selon moi aurait pu etre plus "Wow !" mais qui n'a rien de déplaisant. 
Ridé 12 fois sur une periode de 2 jours.

One of the most intense rides in the world. The first drop is insane and every hill provides elite airtime, while every turn gives you both whip and positives. The setting is great and the new trains help out quite a bit.
Insane ejector on every hill. The cable lift is so fast! Absolutely took my breath away.

Some of the best rides of my life have been on the back left wing seat at the end of the day on Skyrush. I was concerned this would change with the more comfortable restraints but nope - this past visit it felt like the ride wanted me to go home and was trying to forcibly throw me from my seat. To be clear Skyrush is *very* seat dependent especially with the new lap bars - if you're riding it in the morning on an inside seat it's not the same experience. I also think how it works on different body types has always played a large role in the unusually divisive reactions. It's certainly not a coaster for everyone but I'm one of the hardcore Skyrush stans who adore this ride. Skyrush has so much aura thanks to its gorgeous yellow track towering above the creek setting, and I love the vibes from the location of its station which can be electric on a busy summer evening. I also love an accelerated lift hill and Skyrush's is simply the best, and it's followed by maybe the best first drop ever designed. What the bottom of that drop does to your body in a back wing seat doesn't feel like it should be allowed. From there the ride is pure controlled chaos with a deceptive layout that feels so powerful and very addictive. Sometimes the biggest praise I can give a coaster is when it's hard to recall the exact feeling of riding it because your mind was a little too shocked to fully process the experience. X2 is the best at this but I can't think of another coaster that does it better than Skyrush.
A bit rattly on the wing seats, but its so worth it!!!
One of the best coasters in the world

I got 7 rides on this in one day, and I think it’s somewhat worth the hype for it. The first drop is really good having airtime. There is airtime in almost every hill and the ride is intense. On the wing seats it’s more intense but has more rattle, the middle seats have more airtime and a bit less rattle. I also think the ride is a bit to short, but the ride is still the 2nd best in the park behind wildcat’s revenge.
I've rarely been genuinely scared on a coaster, but the airtime this thing gives had me terrified I was going to fall out of my seat.

Tbh this thing is basically flawless. Yeah it’s short but it does so much in that time that it’s length doesn’t matter too much for me. They recently changed the trains on this, which made this ride slightly weaker as the laterals aren’t as pronounced anymore. But they’re definitely still there, and I still love this thing to bits. The first drop alone makes this thing world-class, as that is one of the most intense (and best) elements I’ve ever experienced. I can’t describe it, you’d have to experience it. Anyways, every element after is a blur of some of the world’s strongest and most sustained airtime, incredibly strong positives, the aforementioned laterals, and some combination of them. All of that over a tiny plot of land on a pond. I can’t praise this ride enough, truly world-class, and somehow not the best ride in the park.

Wow. Skyrush is elite. The first drop is absolutely amazing, and the spaghetti bowl layout is ultra intense and it pulls crazy forces. Skyrush is one of the greatest coasters ive ever ridden, and I dont see that changing anytime soon.
greatest first drop on the planet.

THIS RIDE IS PERFECTION! One of the most intense in the world! The first drop is out of this world, it throws you out of your seat, then, just when you think it's over, it hits the kink and ejects you farther than before! The sustained ejector is crazy, and it has so much positive gs. The airtime over every hill is so sustained, the positives are so crazy, this is the ride of the extreme forces, negative and positive! It is soo insane, I love Skyrush!!!

The new restraints definitely tamed the ride down a tad, but its less so completely removing its teeth and more like only letting the dragon that eats people only eat 1 person per week as a treat. I think that the added comfort and reduced intensity is a plus in the grand scheme of things and lets me ride it more than once per couple hours. The kink on the first drop is still my favorite single moment from any coaster I've been on. I imagine that the general public may ride once or twice per day rather than once and never again now, so I'm sure the park is happy with the changes (whether or not Hershey is ready to work with Intamin on a major ride again is not something I'd get my hopes up for).

The BEST airtime in the world (or at least in Pennsylvania)! I don't know how to explain the ejector on the drop, it's unreal. The airtime is like an outer body experience minus the dying part. Another INTAMIN Stengel masterpiece.

In 2025, I found myself much less in love with Skyrush than I was before. I don’t even really think it was the updated seats that changed my view on it, although I did admittedly love the old design (see my profile picture). It’s simply too rough for me, as much as that pains me to admit. My first ride in years, in a back row wing seat, had me genuinely shocked at how awfully it tracked. During every moment of positives I felt as though I were being shaken like a soda can. On subsequent rides I was able to strategically pick my seat to minimize the roughness, but the magic that had it in my top 5 before was just gone. It’s still got great airtime  and is still an overall excellent ride, but I don’t think I’ll ever like Skyrush as much as I did in 2023.
Because of personal preference just shy from my perfect ten list, but the ragdolling on this is incredible. The lift is fast, the drop is faster, the banks are intense, all around phenomenal.
Not sure why so many people hype this. It was good. But a bit too intense imo and too short.  Still my number 3 at Hershey but would take Wildcats Revenge or Candymonium over this any day.
I-305, but is has better restraints and better airtime.

I must admit that I went on this ride expecting it to be great.  I was honestly hoping that one of the other two Intamins here would be my favorite, but no.  This takes the cake--easily and by a wide margin.  No doubt the best ride in this fantastically coaster rich park.  I had zero issue with the restraints.  They were perfect; open and free and just holding you in by your lap.  I don't know what else anyone would want.  I kind of get that because of the intense airtime this delivers that you could get a bit sore from it, but are people honestly saying they wish the ride didn't deliver the intense ejector air?  That is crazy-talk nonsense.  The coaster community craves ejectors--always.  This delivers like very, very few coasters on the planet.  Plus, the airtime on this isn't just quick jolts, there are sustained moments of it.  I can understand someone saying they don't like the feeling of literally being 100% at the mercy of the lap restraint for fear of their life--because that is literally what is happening on much of this ride, but to me that is what makes this spectacular and one of the greatest coasters on earth.  I don't know of anyone getting off of any B&M hyper saying they felt like they were going to die.  This, though, you can say that and it isn't an exaggeration.  It delivers crazy out of your seat air on the first drop, then immediately transitions into face stretching positives.  I literally could feel my cheeks getting tugged downward.  Then it essentially repeats several more times.  Throw in some crazy tight twists and turns all at incredible speeds and you have a recipe for a world class thrill machine.  Did I mention that this thing is intense?  It is not for the faint of heart.  This is truly one of the finest coasters for the true thrill seekers out there in the coaster world.  My only slight gripe is the "wing" design.   To me it doesn't really add anything, unless you have a "wing" seat.  So, 50% of the riders get zero benefit from this design.  Even when you do get the "wing" seat, it isn't quite the same feeling like B&M's winged coasters.  It is a bit silly, but because of the ride this delivers the seats don't matter much.  Even with one of the regular, inner seats, this delivers thrills far beyond what most other coasters are capable of.  Masterpiece of thrill.

A masterpiece of airtime.  If you hate seats, this ride is for you because you'll barely be in it.  People who like to belly-ache about the restraints on this ride can come meet me at my house anytime for a knife-fight.  But, the earlier, the better.  I'm usually in bed by 9 p.m.

Skyrush is probably the most intense coaster I've been on.  The air time is also the strongest I've experienced (I will ride El Toro soon, so I'll see how that compares!).  There is just no describing the intensity of the ride.  The first drop is arguably the best first drop of any coaster.  The ejector airtime on the hills is indescribable.  You seriously feel like you are going to fly out of the coaster.  The whippy turns also deliver some great forces.  I also love the final hill with the sudden twist from right to left at the top.  Overall, it's simply an amazing ride and currently sits at #4 for me.  I have 2 main complaints about the ride.  First off, the lap bars are very tight and lay at a weird angle.  By the end of the ride, they can be quite uncomfortable.  I've always been able to tolerate them, but I can understand why some people avoid this ride.  I have yet to experience the latest changes to the lap bars, but I hear they are greatly improved.  My second complaint is that the coaster is fairly one-dimensional.  It's all about intensity.  The layout could benefit from a little more variety.  I still think the ride is fantastic and I totally understand why so many people have this as their #1 coaster.

This is an amazing ride definitely one of my top ten roller coasters I’ve been on however the lap bars for me felt very uncomfortable, yes I have heard that the lap bars that I rode on were new and apparently really comfortable it’s just for me they were some of the worst roller coaster restraints I’ve ever felt it’s probably because I’m quite short only a twizzler 😞 like my crotch is still hurting a day after just a little. So if you are a women I recommend it if you are a dude do it at your own risk

A good mix of airtime and positives, and it's really intense. If you've ridden pantherian, it's like that but shorter and with more airtime and less whippiness. The new restraints are quite comfortable, just wish they locked downwards during the ride so they don't crush you as much, but it isn't painful.
Rode this twice, 2 years apart. Both times, super painful. It gets a few stars for its fun intensity; I just only wish I could enjoy it more without hurting.
first drop is a car crash..........that's all I can say 10/10

Skyrush has gone on a journey from unenjoyable to elite that I can't quite track for any other coaster. The new lapbars really allow the strong ejector to shine, and the ride's positioning over the river is excellent. The wing seats (particularly in the back half of the train) definitely have a rattle to them, and the coaster runs sluggish until around 3pm - but it's still definitely the third (?) best hyper coaster in Pennsylvania.

Okay, so you're at Canada's Wonderland and you don't have Fastlane plus. It's like 35 degrees Canadian and you have only one long Queue in you. On your left shoulder AlpenFury, and on your right Leviathan. You are probably going with AlpenFury and that new coaster smell. Bzzzz you are wrong, but thanks for playing. Having just ridden these back to back on a scorching hot day I can tell you that the better coaster is Leviathan (and even more so if you can score a front row seat). Where AlpenFury is twisty and flippy and wiggly in the new-fashioned way, Leviathan is what coasters started out  trying to be - scary. So many coasters  have nice lift hills but then wimp out with an unimpressive fall (now I'm looking at you Steel Curtain and many others) Leviathan delivers and delivers muchly. There is force behind the fall. And the next few pops and drops would each make impressive first hills on other rides. So look, if you want to be twisted and tossed and thrown around like a chew toy, Alpen is a good ride for you and please do choose it so that the line for Leviathan is shorter by at least one rider. Honestly, the scariest part of AlpenFury for me was waiting for my wallet, keys and cell phone that I was forced to put into some mysterious cubby boxes (that floated over the ride and supposedly arrived on the exit side) because of its nothing-in-your-pocket policy.

The first drop, AMAZING, that 300ft drop really packs a punch! However, the layout could use more elements, but that first speed hill gives some amazing lateral airtime! I cannot emphasize more how great the airtime hills on this ride are. The layout is also way too short for a ride of this immense speed. More high-in-the-air elements could work, like the large camelbacks.

While the pace and first drop are great, Leviathan always leaves me wanting a little more.  It's fun overall, but I want a few more elements to make me say "Whoa!!"   It just feels like it should do more with its height and speed.  Back is best for airtimes and the first drop, and the front really magnifies the speed.

Leviathan is a very good ride, while being such a towering and monstrous coaster it does also weave in elements that feel more akin to a traditional hyper, as in the wild 182 foot tall camelback. The intensity in the valleys is very good and the sense of speed during the whole thing is just insane. every single element hits in one way or another, although the trim on the tall camelback was an annoyance. It's a great ride just a shame it ends so early, could have easily extended the layout using Dragon Fyre or more of the parking lot

Me personally, Leviathan is my favorite B&M Giga. It's a burger with ALL of the toppings (except for onions because I don't like onions). It's the best ride at Canada's Wonderland without a doubt, at least until they RMC the Wildebeest (that was not a typo). What can I say? That wind-in-your-face feeling is done best here, especially if you get a front row ride. The first drop is one of the best in North America. Every airtime moment delivers better than Domino's Pizza's delivery services. Or, if you're not American and you're reading this review, something like Panago'$. I don't know any other non-American pizza places BUT I DIGRESS. The message I'm conveying is that it's a good ride with a STELLAR FIRST DROP and GREAT AIRTIME and ODDLY COMFORTABLE RESTRAINTS. SERIOUSLY. The clamshell lap bars always leave a smile on my face. But anyway, this will always be one of my favorite rides, and it's the best ride at the park. Because guess what? ALPENFURY IS OVERRATED! THERE, I SAID IT! IT'S A GLORIFIED WASHING MACHINE! I keep getting off topic. I'll have to end the review before I start talking about some SpongeBob-esque randomness, so... yeah. Leviathan is cool. Ride it. Sorry for talking about pizza so much.

Leviathan is a wonderful attraction in its first half. The drop, first turn, speed hill, and camelback are pure joy. Once the ride hits the return run, however, is where it falls apart from a design standpoint. Leviathan's finale is just a lot of forceless meandering and it says a lot that on all of my rides the most fun element in that back half was the dip in the brake run. Regardless of its lackluster finale, the ride delivers a wonderful sense of speed and a glass smooth ride experience. 8/10.
This thing hauls like CRAZY and the floater!!! This ride is insane
It was very fun.

Leviathan is fantastic- a smooth, flowy layout topped with fantastic moments of floater to flojector airtime. Even if it was topped eventually by Fury 325 of the same ride model and AlpenFury in the same park, the incredible ride experience Leviathan provides remains timeless and top tier.
It is a really good ride!

The first drop and overall speed are great, but...   I was disappointed by the airtimes, which were good but not great.  My first ride in the front was incredible because the speed is magnified.  Other seats, though, left me slightly disappointed, especially in the second half where the ride feels like it loses some steam.

Easily my favorite giga out of the four ive ridden. Rode this back in 2018 when I was 11, so it was hard to remember the experience and rank it for a while. Finally got back to this incredible park last weekend for my first rides on yukon striker and alpenfury. I expected alpenfury to put leviathan to shame, but the opposite happened. Although alpenfury is an incredible ride and definitely the fan favorite, I found myself in line for leviathan much more than alpenfury (partially because of the wait lol, but mainly because of my preference). While Leviathan is a short ride, I believe it is near perfect. The drop, speed hill, and massive camelback in the first half couldnt be executed better. Yes, I don't think the second half is amazing, but it really doesn't need to be. The first half of this ride is just that good. This is the ride I wish Fury 325 could have been. Leviathan uses it's speed in the first half for incredible ejector and floater hills, while Fury using it for boring turns. I am sure when I ride Pantherian, it will steal the title from leviathan for best giga, but for now Leviathan clears by a mile.
Probably the most slept on giga coaster. It is amazing and I love the drop. Perfect.
This is my favorite ride at Canadas wonderland this ride goes real high and fast

It's certainly no Fury 325, but Leviathan is a formidable B&M giga in its own right. The first drop is excellent and the elements are very flowy and sweeping; makes an epic first impression at the front entrance of the park!
Really fun B&M giga that is super smooth and has tons of airtime. Front row is definitely the best but the back is fun too.
Masterpiece
Exactly what I said for Behemoth.
Great pacing and fun floater but the forces aren’t that strong.

This one might not reach Fury 325 levels of excitement but it's easily my second favorite B&M giga and way better than Orion.  The first drop is fantastic, especially in the front since it feels like you drop for a while.  If it was as good in the first half as it is the rest of the ride it would be elite.  The first half has the awesome drop and then the turnaround into the hand chopper moment is amazing.  It definitely turns into a floater airtime hill coaster after that but I really enjoy these like most of the hyper B&Ms.  Out of both days, it easily had the best capacity with the fast pass and definitely was the shortest wait of the big four for both days.  I almost put it as my favorite at the park but AlpenFury is pretty tough to beat.  4.5/5 stars

Leviathan is a fantastic giga coaster that delivers a smooth, fast, and highly enjoyable experience from start to finish. Its greatest strength is its incredible sense of speed, as the ride constantly feels like it is flying through the layout while maintaining a graceful and controlled pace. The first drop is especially impressive, providing surprisingly strong forces that catch riders off guard and set the tone for the rest of the ride. The airtime throughout the layout is excellent, with several moments of floating sensation that balance out the speed and intensity.

The restraints are also some of the best on any coaster, providing comfort and security while allowing riders to fully enjoy the elements without feeling restricted. The smoothness of the track combined with the massive scale of the ride creates a truly premium coaster experience. However, Leviathan does have a few weaknesses, with the biggest being its short duration. The ride is over before you know it, and the incredible speed makes you wish there were more elements after the final turnaround. In many ways, Leviathan feels like a smaller, more family-friendly version of Fury 325 — a "baby Fury" that captures some of the same speed, flow, and graceful airtime while offering its own unique experience. Even with its shorter length, Leviathan remains an elite coaster and one of Canada's best.

Leviathan is a great coaster. The first drop is incredible, the whole ride is super smooth, and the speed is awesome. All the airtime hills hit, especially the banked speed hill. I just wish it was a little bit longer, like one more moment of airtime or something. But that's just minor. Leviathan is a must-ride coaster in Canada!

Leviathan is my favorite coaster and has been ever since I first road it it was my first above 200 foot coaster to get over my fear of coasters the entire ride is some of b&m best work truly my favorite coaster

i hate to say this, but i was pretty disappointed by Leviathan. it was definitely fun, but i found myself wanting to marathon Behemoth instead. the drop didn't feel as long as other gigas, the pacing was off, and the layout was a bit dull for me. i was really hoping to give this ride another go during my 2026 visit, but it was closed nearly the entire day for high winds, preventing me from riding. unfortunately, as of now, this is just not my favorite.
A ride this good can never be long enough.  Excellent airtime, great pace, and the freedom provided the upper-body with these restraints make for a fantastic ride. Front row for sure.

I did not expect to love Expedition GeForce as much as I did. It's honestly a nearly perfect ride in my opinion. I like the simplistic theming, but I have to admit that the bigFM sponsorship is a bit out of place. Smells Like Teen Spirit played in the station once so I can't complain too much. Moving on to the layout, the first drop starts off with great airtime in the back rows and then has wicket lateral G forces. It's one of my favorite first drops in the world, better than Kondaa's first drop in my opinion and that's thanks to the added whip in the 7th car. Kondaa only has 6 cars for reference. The first airtime hill is more powerful up front, throwing you out of your seat. It's the first ejector moment on the ride and it's not even the most powerful airtime you get on the ride. The overbanked turn has a bit of force to it and the following airtime hill is insane no matter where you sit. It has super sustained ejector airtime, some of the most powerful airtime I've ever felt. The twister section is a nice change of pace and you even get some positive float on the turn into the straight downwards track. The switchback has nice lateral G forces and a bit of airtime. The return leg has quicker, yet still sustained ejector airtime. It's once again really powerful. There was a very mild rattle but nothing bad, especially for its size and age. Silver Star's rattle in the back rows is way worse. Even Thunder Dolphin, which is the same model but newer and with brand new trains rattles more. The trains are rather comfy, being the first (or second) gen Intamin Megacoaster trains, but they are slow to check, having both seatbelt (they are the slow part to check but they are necessary giving the extremely freeing lap bars) and lap bars. They ran two trains for most of the day and the coaster was a near walk-on for most of the day, but they removed the second train for the last hour, which lead to abysmal waits for the front row as they let people with fast passes go wherever they want and they almost always choose the front. They thankfully let them go every two trains. The wait for the back was still bad given the hard to verify trains and single train operations. This lead to a train being sent out every 5 minutes in the last hour. I still managed to get 10 rides on Expedition GeForce in just one day, which puts it neck and neck with Goudurix as my most ridden coaster in a single day.
