Loaded with good floater airtime, and the airtimes are solid on every part of the train.  Great twisting first drop, and the speed is consistent throughout. (It feels faster than 75 mph.) Capacity stinks with one train, but fortunately there were no lines for my visit.  A couple of the valleys have some mildly uncomfortable Gs, but overall this is a speedy airtime machine that's held up very well over the years.

I absolutely love this masterpiece of a rollercoaster. The first drop is out of this world, the six ejector airtime moments are awesome and the pacing the ride has is perfect. Apart from Kondaa or maybe Hyperion I'd have difficulty naming a rollercoaster with better airtime. So much so, that I say the rides on this redefined the term ejector airtime for me. The back row has the best seats but you can ride it pretty much anywhere and you'll have a load of fun. This defines a world class rollercoaster for me which Expedition GeForce despite its 24 year existence still is. It is the best German rollercoaster by far. A must ride for every coaster enthusiast.
Except the single-train operations and 2 dead spots in the layout, the most forceful and intense coaster in europe for me and that for a 25 yr old coaster. A must-ride

Expedition GeForce is an airtime machine with non-stop ejectors and snappy elements. 
The first drop is awesome especially the "overcorrection" which is great on the front row. 
There are issues; The annoying lap bar, the distinct rattle, lack of foot space, lack of theming, and slow operations.
However, it's still a fantastic ride.
So close to being a 5 star ride. Such an interesting layout for a ride of its age, where every hill and turn hits. It suffers from uncomfortable restraints, distracting from the amazing ejector.

Probably the most overrated coaster I've ridden. I found the restraints were uncomfortable on my thighs and was expecting more from the layout. It does have some excellent ejector airtime at the end of the layout, but the rest of the layout just seemed quite dull with the overbanks (which weren't very forceful). At least with Millenium Force it has the size to make the elements a lot grander. Definitely disappointing, and that queue is awful with just 1 train.

I have often heard geforce is overrated.I loved it, may because I just expected a more aggressive version of Silver Star, but it turned out to be my number 3 in Germany so far (behind Voltron and Taron. I am missing Kärnan though). Every hill except the one into the brakes delivers ejectors (that last one still is floaty). Stronger in the front (just the drop is better in the back) 
I found the cars to be a bit small or at least the seating position is extremely restrictive regarding airtime. But with a bit of belly inflationär can get some wiggleroom in the restraints. 
Unfortunately between the great airtime moments the coaster seems to just go around some pointless turns to bleed off speed. Having ridden Kondaa, I can see where thy got their inspiration from and what they improved. 

Even after 25years GeForce still packs a punch

It surprised me even if I knew it was a good ride. 
Surprisingly smooth for its age. The airtimes and ejectors are great. 
Even better at the front IMO.
It's a relentless ride that deserves its good reputation.
Rode it 10 times in a day. 
Loved every ride.
I liked this old gen Intamin a lot because it's packed with airtime and it's very intense. The coaster is also very fast.
Very nice Intamin with a lot of airtime and ejectors. The negatives were also great. The wait time was pretty long because of the fact they only used one train at a time. Great coaster!

despite being outclassed by a lot of newer intamins Expedition GeForce remains one of the best coasters in europe for it's insane twisted first drop nice long terrain layout and airtime moments but the middle section is rather underwhelming
Best coaster for sustained ejector airtime and amazing first drop..drop has great laterals but I wish there was more intense lats through the ride. Regardless its great for airtime
Overrated IMO, but still good.

I think there are enough long reviews already. I especially find the first drop and the S-shaped hill awesome. The pace is perfect and you get a ton of ejector. It has one huge downside for me: I’m a bit taller than most people, so the lap bar rests on my thighs and presses on the muscle with every hill (ouch).
That first drop! Awesome!

Possibly the best coaster I've ridden for strong sustained ejector airtime. It starts off with an insane drop and then goes through an ejector filled layout, the turns aren't too interesting but it goes through them with enough speed to not bore you. Insane that a ride as old as this has held up so well to time. Unfortunately the park it's in doesn't do it any justice, 6 minute dispatches on one train, rude and slow staff. But besides that this is an incredible roller coaster.

I've heard again and again from others that they still rate this coaster extremely high, but I personally just don't see it. I really dislike everything surrounding the ride: The ride ops are incredibly bored and insanely slow, it feels like 7 minutes between every single dispatch. Instead of using the second train the park just cheaps out and exclusively uses 1 train. During the ride itself, the combination of seat belt and lap bar just hurts a bit, it's not comfortable. And the theming is not just non-existent, it's actually actively bad because the ride is sponsored by a dumb radio station and a recording of one of their annoying radio jockeys talking nonsense is played on every single dispatch. And the exit is literally an ugly construction container stuffed with cheap scammy "insert 2€ to almost but not actually get the stuffed animal" gambling machines. So the overall feeling surrounding this ride is just depressing, being near this ride just feels sad and cheap. And the ride itself is also imho not that outstanding, it's just a really nice drop and an airtime hill right after, some irrelevant elements in the middle and then 4 more airtime hills. In general, holiday park is sadly one of the worst theme parks I've ever visited. If you're doing the much much much much better Phantasialand / Europa Park / etc. that are a few hours away, maybe stop by holiday park once for at most half a day or not at all, because Expedition Geforce is still the only standout attraction here, everything else except the log flume is much worse than this.
absolute thrill of a ride. was not expecting it to go around most of the park and the drop was stellar

This ride has the strongest sustained airtime I have ever experienced. For a solid thirty minutes after my final ride, my thighs hurt. The only downside is that there weren't as many moments of positive forces as I was expecting.
Great ride! Could use some oil.
Absolute world class ride with great airtime and an insane first drop, severely held back by the operations and the uncomfortable lap bars.

C'est une bonne machine old school !
Je trouve que les Airtimes et la First Drop sont meilleurs que ceux de Kondaa.
Dommage que le débit soit catastrophique. 
Il y a un peu de vibrations au Last et les lap bar font un peu mal au moment des camelbacks finaux .

Let's start with the downsides for once: Aside from the non-existing theming it's a shame that Expedition GeForce only runs on one train with pretty average operations. Therefore the queue can grow longer than it needs to be. Luckily, even on busier days the queue seems to shrink a lot throughout the day. The ride itself is a classic with its signature twisted drop that, unfortunately, is only really worldclass on the left side of the train. Interestingly enough, I thought it was best experienced not in the last row but somewhere between rows 10-12: In the back row I was pulled down quite fast whereas the other rows in the back half had me out of my seat for a few more seconds. At least that was what it felt like. The rest of the layout is not exactly rich in variety but delivers some of the best drawn-out ejector airtime I've experienced. Every single one of those hills hits, while some of the valleys - especially the one following the first camelback - pull strong positive Gs. Sprinkle in one or two head choppers and you've got yourself a breathtaking experience that only suffers a little from its rather uneventful section in the middle where it's mostly turns. What GeForce lacks in excitement at the half-way point, it makes up for with a strong finale. It's definitely a coaster that's worth the trip, especially as it's still quite smooth for its age. Front row is great too but if you're using the fast pass, I'd recommend picking second row: It's just 1 credit instead of 2 but doesn't really change the experience due to the slightly elevated seating position. I wouldn't be mad if they were able to change the trains for some newer and more comfortable ones, though.

Breathtaking ride and arguably the most unique coaster this company has ever made. Feels like it has a different gear than almost any coaster I've ever been on - thanks in large part to its setting. Every element accentuates a singular thesis behind the design of the ride, which makes it more psychologically potent than all of RMC's other coasters that may be longer or have more airtime elements that don't add up to anything as memorable as Outlaw Run.
Night rides on this elevated it to elite status for me. Avoid even rows if you can.

I chose "harness" as a con because there's no option for "seat belt," and the insanely small belts on this ride suck. That said, Outlaw Run is a lunatic ride that I love with my whole heart. Avoid the wheel seats and the roughness goes away. Ride it in the front at night for the ideal experience. It is an unbelievable night ride—in league with Beast and Voyage.
95/100,  a little short but very fun and intense. This is my first RMC and it makes me excited for Steel Vengeance. The double barrel roll finale is the best and most memorable part.

Geez I love this ride. Still not the best at the park though, which goes to show how good SDC is. Anyways, this ride is a bit rough at times, but man I don't care. It rips through thst course so fast you can barely feel the roughness, and the first ever coaster to invert I ever rode. And it goes upside not once, not twice, but three times. But yeah, good hangtime on the end, good airtime, and an excellent first drop

If it were Ibox, Outlaw Run would be in my top 15, but considering its roughness on wheel seats, I have to put it back. Besides the rough ride, Outlaw run offers great pacing, sharp ejectiors, and three hangtime-filled inversions.

This is an amazing roller coaster. It flies through the woods of Silver Dollar City delivering ejector air, powerful inversions, and relentless speed. As far as wooden coasters go it ran very smooth too.
My favorite wooden coaster of all time!

Why isn’t this ride talked about at all?! It’s SO good and has one of the best first drops out there.  The roughness of the track adds so much to the intensity of the ride.  Every moment hits and the hangtime in the finale is insane.  This is in my top ten and I love it to death.  One of the most underrated RMC creations!
An amazing, fast paced RMC Topper Track masterpiece!
Would be great if it wasn’t so rough.

HOLY CRAP. I recently rode outlaw run and ITS MY FAVORITE RIDE AT SDC. Sure while the back row is ROUGH AS HELL and please avoid wheel seats for your spine, it’s a wild ride. AND MAKE SURE TO RIDE IT IN NIGHT. Probably 2nd fav night ride next to velisicoaster. Or however you spell it. Overall 9.5 out of 10. EASILY one of my favs and I don’t mind that it’s rough.
Wow… just wow 😮

This is much more well-balanced than basically any RMC I've been on. I appreciate the way the ride continues to shift its focus between airtime and laterals, and while the finale doesn't hit hard, I feel like it adds rather than detracts from a ride package that's powerful and diverse but not too crazy. A front row ride gets it just inside my top 20.
This is a very aggressive coaster with strong ejectors. It does have a rattle and a pothole on the first drop that are worse the further back you go. However, it's still a great coaster.
Almost perfect but the bottom of the first drop is so rough.
Great ride, and on the right seats it’s incredible. Row 11 rides best, 1 rides second best. Avoid wheel seats.
Best ride at silver dollar city IMO. (Edit, uh no its not)

Even though its short, I still love this ride. it uses the terrain for a huge wave turn and even the ending being a double barrel roll going upward, slowing down giving you more hangtime. This also has one of my favorite first drops, Im young and I left the park early since my parents were tired but I wouldn't be shocked if at night this is a great night ride.
Great coaster, but too short. Very good first drop and inversions, very quick and intense. Would be better if it was longer and had some more airtime moments. Preferred it over time traveler
A little uncomfortable for taller people due to the shin guards, but a perfect ride nonetheless

Great job RMC! I love the layout but over the years, it has been getting rougher. I went in about 6 different rows and it was fun but after doing that, I came off with a bit of a headache. For me though, the first drop and double barrel roll just make this ride a must do!

This is by far the most underrated RMC. I have a bias towards wooden coasters, but this has some of the strongest airtime on any of them in general. Combine that with a good roughness, a beautiful setting, and fun inversions,  you end up with a top 20 coaster.

This ride shocked me in every way. The pacing is unmatched for any wooden coaster and after 13 years it still runs super smooth. The ejector is also surreal, this ride will really leave you speechless.

Helix, in my humble opinion, is just about as close to perfect as a ride can be. This layout is just unbelievable in it's diversity, you experience pretty much every type of force imaginable, crushing positives, lateral whip, floaty hangtime and utterly addictive airtime, Helix has it all, and in perfect proportions as well. The positives are focussed on the mid-ride helix and the crazy intense Norwegian loop, both those moments give me the tingling in your feet sensation in a big way. The first corkscrew and the inverted top hat shine for their hangtime, they are traversed at the perfect speed to float through them. The zero g roll into the hard left turn are really whippy and the left transition really throws you quite aggressively, and the final heartline roll also pulls you through at a great speed. Then there's the airtime, oh man the AIRTIME, there's a few great moments but that final massive ejector hill might just be my favourite element on any coaster, it sends you every single time. I know many complain about the launches, and it's true they aren't very powerful, but i just don't care, they give the ride the speed it needs for that awesome layout to shine, they're simply there for a purpose, just like a lift hill. What a stunning location for a coaster too, the way it winds up and down the hillside, utilising the terrain so well, is awesome, and there's some stunning views to be had on the ride too. To top it off, it runs pretty smooth, just a hint of a Mack rattle but nothing to be bothered by, operations are awesome, and it always seems to have the best staff running it, everyone in Sweden is lovely anyway but the Helix teams always stand out. I adore this ride and I adore the park that made it happen, Helix and Liseberg never fail to wow me

Helix was for me one of those ride experiences that change how you view and value coasters. This Mack masterpiece has something I'd never seen before in any of my (at that time) over 150 creds: it's a coaster that has both the airtime, layout, hangtime and general quality of a top tier ride, but also some very intense positive G-forces more common on inverts or rides with less out-of-your-seat moments. After riding Helix, now positive G's are on my list of things a good coaster should do, else I feel underwhelmed. That's the key factor of this ride. It's not superbly good at anything in particular, but it offers a long experience with some mild floater on the first drop, beautiful hangtime (first corkscrew, one of the zero-G-rolls, the top hat and the heartline roll) and three ejectors, two of which are really good (though I've seen better). And on top of all that, almost every single valley and turn, even the ones before the first launch, pull strong G's. Virtually every inch of track is sheer adrenaline. That alone accounts for the existence of some minor "dead spots" before the second launch, as well as both launches themselves. It's not that those moments are necesarily bad, but in contrast with the superb pacing of the rest of the ride, they stand out as forceless. Before riding, I'd say the launches provide the speed needed, they're there for that and can't be criticized (they certainly can't, in that regard), but if they were strong launches, this already 10/10 coaster may even become my number 1. Another minor negative I'd like to comment are the other three inversions I didn't mention, which don't really provide: not much hangtime nor whip there (although the Norwegian loop has some high and sustained positive G's). Also, the theming is completely lacking and IMAscore's soundtrack isn't quite up there with their best ones. The location on the hillside and over the pathways is incredible, though. Great views of the coaster from plenty of spots. And Thank You, Liseberg, for that awesome Virtual Queue. It enabled me to get 6 rides on this masterpiece on my day of visit, without hardly having to wait for any of them.

The perfect coaster imo. Layout is excellently crafted along the hillside, all elements follow each other perfectly. Then this ride has excellent airtime, hangtime, whip and positives, all I want in a coaster. The camelback after the inside tophat is blissful with its combination of airtime and views. The first and final inversion offer awesome hangtime. The zero-G roll into the lefthanded turn give insane whip and the Norwegian loop and helix are pretty intense in terms of positives. Just the most well-rounded coaster layout ever. I love Helix so, so much and it is currently my number 1 in the world.

I'm Swedish and I can say that this is without a doubt Sweden's best roller coaster!

Helix has everything a roller coaster should contain. Two launchers, 7 inversions and airtime, and it's a long ride. I love that this coaster start straight away with a drop out of the station and right after that there is a loop, instead of it being a lift hill. Which means something is happening om this rollercoaster all the time, there really is no time to breathe. And since this is located on the mountain inside Liseberg, it uses the terrain very well and it feels significantly taller than what the track itself is. My absolute favorite part of the whole ride is the last airtime hill! You just feel how you fly out of the seat when you ride it. Balder's Airtime is insanely good, but the last airtime hill on helix is ​​better than all the airtime on Balder!

I understand people who say that you don't feel the launchers on Helix. It's not like you're pushed back into the seat forcefully if you say that. But when I rode it last time, I at least felt that you were pushed back a little bit in the seat. So they aren't completely forceless and didn't ruin the ride for me. I strongly recommend trying to sit both front and back. At the front you get the best view when riding, while at the back you get a much more intense and exciting riding experience. You sit very comfortably in the train. The seats are comfortable and the stafety bar around the waist is the same. You feel very safe when you simply ride. The ride itself is very soft and nice, I must say. Many people say that Helix has become shaky in recent years. And it's not really strange at all, since it has been operating at Liseberg since 2014. But I didn't experience it shaking in any way and it was just incredibly comfortable to ride in every way! One thing I also like about Helix is ​​that it is neither the tallest nor the fastest rollercoaster. Without them being the best experience. Which is also what Liseberg wanted from the beginning. and they really succeeded!

So even though the launches may not be the best and it has become shaky in last couple of years, it doesn't matter for me, because Helix is ​​so perfect on everything else. Both the airtime and hangtime are spectacular during the whole ride.
I would definitely say that this is one of the best roller coasters in Europe!
A clear 10/10 from me!!

Helix is an excellent coaster with an amazing location on the side of a hill. The views you get of the park and the city are amazing. The coaster has the really comfortable mack restrains which are very good. The ride starts with a very good first drop out of the station. The rest of the layout has amazing inversions and ejector airtime moments. The only con about this ride is that the launches are not strong, but the rest is perfect.
peak
Its fun but overrated
I liked the boosts so much and the inversion at the start of the ride I also think the whole theme and music was very good there where a bit que time but it was all worth it

i finally after 12 years got to experience this coaster. it just has an incredible, long layout with 7 inversions, two launches and a hell of an station theme song. the only thing i can complain about is how weak the launches are.

Helix is maybe not the most intense coaster but more than makes up for that in it’s wonderful fast pace including a drop and inversion right out of the station and it’s one of the few coasters I’ve ridden where it just seems to never end (in a good way).

WOW. I've heard MANY great things about Helix and I was afraid it would dissapoint me so much. That didn't happen, but it surpised me! This coaster has an INCREDIBLE layout and all forces are well presented through a layout which lasts forever. The location of this ride is also one if its many selling points. Helix is also really smooth and, unlike many modern-day coasters, it does have several sections with really strong positives. Bit of a bummer that the ride and queue are not really themed, but despite that, it still means Helix makes it into my top 3. What an incredible masterpiece!!

Front row on Helix is incredible. You really feel every element. The airtime provided on the ride is outstanding and each inversion provides something. Many of the rolls really whip you side to side. The rides integration into its terrain creates a super unique ride experience that is certainly one of the best in the world.
Probably the most well balanced layout on a coaster of this size
helix is my wife
Beautiful not much more i can say

I am a new coaster enthusiast and i have not ridden many roller coasters before but this was for sure the best one i have ridden, was a little bit dissapointed in the second launch tho but it was still a true masterpiece.
A terrain-hugging masterpiece. With two launches and seven inversions, it uses the hillside perfectly. The night rides, with the park lit up below you, are some of the best in the world.
Helix was great, but not perfect, if Helix had intamin blitz launches like (Taron ) or ( Velocicoaster ) then it would be perfect
Helix is excellent. The launches are weak and the back row has a minor rattle. However, the layout is excellent with strong airtime moments, dives off the cliff face, and an incredible soundtrack.
This coaster was the first big roller coaster. It made me to a coaster enthusiast. It’s fantastic

This coaster doesn't take a break. Leaving the station, you immediately hit your first inversion, and thats a great first look for whats to come. Amazingly built onto the mountain of Liseberg. Unfortunately the lap bar gets very tight during the ride, but eh, still an amazing ride.

Helix offers, what I believe, to be one of the most complete roller coaster experiences out there. Also, the ambient queue soundtrack might just be the best piece of audio to bless my ears. 
Ride at night!!!

I over hyped tis coaster for myself and was left a little disappointed. It's a solid coaster but if you take it off the hillside then it's not great. I enjoyed the layout even with a couple of dead areas and the queue line is also very fun. The 2nd half of the layout was my favorite and 100% can be ridden all day

WHAT THE HELL IS THIS DOING IN A SWEDISH ZOO?!??

So much fun. My favourite RMC in Europe. I have no idea how Untamed ranks above Wildfire, this is SO much better and more varied.

Operations are slow, but even on a sunny Saturday in June the wait was only 10 minutes.

One point of warning: Wildfire doesn’t always open when the park opens, and I was confronted with a “this ride is closed for today” sign, which nearly gave me (and some other enthusiasts) a heart attack. It was just left from the previous night and doesn’t mean the ride is down!

Maybe as perfect as a wooden coaster can be. It is butter smooth unlike the American RMC woodies. The layout really mixes things up. Great airtime both sideways and standard, whippy inversions, and probably my favorite stall to date. The location is stunning and the use of terrain is perfect. I lapped it over and over and never got tired of it.

Blew me away. Can't wait to reride Untamed this summer and properly compare them both. I got 16 rides on this masterpiece, and every time I liked it even more. Yeah, the pacing towards the end isn't the best, but it keeps going anyway, it's not a significant issue. The main cons I found on Wildfire were the train design and the capacity. The lap bar isn't the best, but the major problem comes from the rigid seat walls. They didn't offer as much freedom as I'd have liked to fully enjoy those laterals and whip. If Wildfire had new-gen intamin trains, it would be my N.2 (or maybe even top 1). On the other hand, the ops were quite a nightmare. True, I didn't have to queue for long (I got 16 rides, with spare time to do the kiddy creds and the cable car). However, it was frustrating to see such slow, one-train-ops, with several free seats on every dispatch. If properly operated, waits should have been 3-5 minutes the day I was there (rather than 10-15). Now, that being said, Wildfire is a solid 10/10, an awesome rollercoaster in a far-flung zoo. It does lack some higher positive G's, but precisely that is what allowed me to get 16 rerides on one day. There's plenty of airtime, but it's mixed with laterals and achieved through many different elements – unlike classic airtime machines, which just have straight hill after straight hill. The Zero-G-Rolls are fun, and although they're not the highlights of the ride, they do provide a nice change in forces and elements that perfectly round up the layout. The stall left me a bit dissapointed, though, as I had great expectations for this worldwide beloved coaster element and it seems I'm not really into stalls. Inversions with no hangtime, whip or positive G's aren't my thing; floating upside down isn't as amazing as I thought. However, right after the stall comes one of my favourite elements of all times: that insane outer banked turn pulls crazy laterals entering and exiting, with great whip, and then it agressively ejects you out of your seat while flying at 90º and with gorgeous views towards the water. Breathtaking. And in that regard, the obvious fact I didn't mention yet: stunning location!! Overall, Wildfire is an awesome roller coaster full of aggresive air and turns that is, on itself, worth a visit to this ginormous zoo.
Its very good althouhg the other half is a little bit boring

the views on the top is crazy with first just a turn and then it yeets you up an small hill and down an crazy first drop. the first 0g stall after the drop give crazy hang time and then it shoots you down and in to an insane wave turn. its an world class rmc wooden coaster located in a zoo, thats crazy. since its located in an random zoo it is an big attraction and draws big crowds but it absolutely doesnt help that they run on 1 TRAIN!!! With atleast 40-50 minutes qeue they send them super duper slow like come on man. the second half is a lot slower but who really  cares man it is just pure fun. the second and final roll was kinda rough and i did barely fit in the restraints as a 6 foot guy. Its an incredible coaster but please just add another train.

The location and view at the top are unmatched and then it interacts with the terrain well. The drop is good and then my favorite weightless inversion after that is amazing with a typical insane fast twisty layout following. My only gripe is it takes forever to find at the back of the park and they were really slow operations with one train.

Wildfire is an excellent RMC. The views from the top are stunning and the first drop is outstanding. The tunnel whilst being blasted with wood smoke was a highlight. There's a rattle near the back but nothing major. There are pacing issues toward the end but it's not that bad.
Its first drop and build up is awesome and i like the long stall but it kinda falls of after a bit and its not that long, also when i rode it in front row it had amazing views

Wildfire is very smooth for a pseudo wooden coaster. The first half is fast and whippy. The second half isn't as fast or intense but it doesn't ruin the pacing badly. The lap bars are better than Zadra's since the shin guard doesn't come as close to your legs. The back row offers better airtime and in the front you get a better sense of speed. Best part is the first drop.
Great trip to Kolmarden just to ride this, and it didnt disappoint. The first drop gives great ejector in the back and the scenery is amazing.

First few elements are world-class. Incredible first drop with ejector airtime, stall which gives decent hangtime and has amazing whip going in and out of it, and the wave turn with ejector airtime and laterals. Then Wildfire loses some power but still charges through its elements. Location is incredibly beautiful as well, right by the lake.

Located deep in the zoo near Norkopping Sweden lies one of the greatest masterpiece is created by Rocky Mount construction. This ride has an insane first drop as you crest over a small hill after a crows nest and then you are in for a treat. My favorite part is the overbank wave turn as you faced the lake my goodness what is this doing in the zoo? This was my highlight on my trip to Europe definitely go on this if you have the opportunity to go to Europe because this is a can’t miss coaster one of the best wooden coasters out there

The way this ride hugs the scenery is out of this world. Masterpiece of a wooden coaster. The inversions are incredible, and the airtime moments are really solid. It's also surprisingly forceful otherwise and runs really well. It's probably also the most beautiful coaster I've ever seen

The setting alone is worth the trip. Plummeting down a cliffside on an RMC wooden coaster is an unforgettable experience. It’s smooth, fast, and features some of the best inversions found on any wooden track.
The ride is pretty fun. Great inversions, but speed is the best thing. Natural placement might be the best of the world, but the built scenery is kinda poor for this type of coaster.
The best roller coaster in Europe. Truly a masterpiece, a must ride for all coaster enthusiast

I really enjoy the Zero-G-Stall after the first drop, the banked airtime hill and the first heartline roll. Overall the whole ride is very intense and a lot of fun with lots of elements. I really hate the 2 very well done head-chop effects (after the first drop and through the small hut) ;-) The last 2 rows are recommended in order to have ejector airtime during the first drop. The location in the park with the ride through the rocks and the woods is absolutely stunning.
Really good ride, but a bit overrated.

A very good Topper Track Ride, that is embedded in the beautiful landscape of the swedish forest. The first drop with the 270° turn is iconic an gives wonderful ejector airtime in the back rows. It runs smoothly, the first 3/4 of the ride is world class. Loses over some Hills in the second half a bit too much speed, especially on the last airtime hill. But the three inversions are really good.

Unpopular opinion but this is better than Zadra, plus it never has a queue. And people who say the second half is slow haven’t tried it once it’s fully warmed up. I was greyed out for half the ride during the end of the day.

The coaster is something else, the ride up giving an excellent view over the surrounding area and the little spin around before the first drop is icing on the cake in this regard. To get the most out of the first drop, you should absolutely sit in the back but the front is also fun if you want the sense of speed. The inversions are a lot of fun; especially since this was my first time doing inversions with just a lap restraint. If you are there for the zoo, Wildfire is one hell of a bonus but if you are there for Wildfire, you will find low waiting times and skilled staff. Their display of broken phones is also a nice touch to remind you to leave your personals in the locker or with less brave friends.

This coaster, located inside a zoo in the middle of nowhere in Sweden, has no business being this good 😅

Besides the difficulty of access I can't think of any meaningful con.

When it is crowded the queue takes like 10m, the harness is fairly comfortable, the ride length is pretty good, and I think it is one of the smoothest ride I ever had, no throwing around, no banging against stuff, just a nice ride.
A must ride for thrill seekers
It's one of the best coasters in the world! The hangtime on the first inversion is INSANE! But it is a bit rough, but it isn't too bad!

The best part about this ride is the lap bar. The lap bar makes this roller coaster a million times better. Most of the time I was on the ride, I felt like I was going to fly up and backwards out of my seat. The first time I went on I was scared of the non inverting loop. But the last time I went, the least crazy element was the entry into the loop.

Australias best coaster. Its got powerful ejector and some strong positive gs. All of this is experienced with an extremely freeing lap bar and seat design. My only cons for this coaster are its capacity (dispatches on white christmas for me took around 3 mins) and the occasional dead spot, though I think that the complaints for this ride's pacing are overblown. I get that the stengel dive doesnt do much, and neither does the helix when its running slower, but still, the ride at least feels like it flows in most sections of the ride, and for me, never feels sluggish and keeps its intensity fairly well. My favourite elements are the first drop in the back row (powerful sustained ejector with laterals), the big camelback (nearly 3 secs of ejector airtime), the non inverting loop (whip with airtime) and the final 3 bunny hills (i felt airtime in my throat). And then theres the backwards row. God damn. Just go and ride this thing. The combination of powerful forces with a freeing seat and restraint design, as well as immaculate smoothness make this the best coaster in aus.

This ride is crazily good. The twisted drop is breathtaking and the camelback after the drop gives sustained strong floater. The non-inverting loop whips you so hard and delivers strong ejector especially in the front and back rows. The hills at the finale give you great airtime. Transitions are all very whippy. The helix and the valleys give strong positive gs. The ride is also very comfortable with the Mack lap bars. Pacing is relentless. The only downside of the ride is the capacity. Overall, a smooth long ride packed with great moments and spectacular airtime.
DC Rivals is a phenomenal hyper coaster and i would recommend it to anyone- the backwards seat is insane and is the craziest coaster experience I've had!
Amazing ride.

DC Rivals is a masterpiece of a Coaster, however it really lacks theming. Add onboard audio and enclose the first third of the lift hill and it would be a 5 Star easy. The rest of the Coaster is great, but I would have loved to see some overbanks in it or something like that. Maybe a Wave Turn?

The dc rivals hypercoaster is actually one of the best coasters I’ve ridden, with an incredible first drop, amazing speed, and especially the first camelback hill, which delivers unbelievable airtime. The back rows have the most airtime and make the ride even more exciting. One downside is the lack of theming, and the middle section has a few dead spots where the pacing slows down. However, the final bunny hops completely redeem the ride and end it on a high note. Overall, I’d give it a 9/10 and highly recommend it to any thrill seeker.

Great coaster overall with a few dead spots, especially in the middle of the ride a bit after the non-inverting loop. It also, unsurprisingly, features little to no theming whatsoever, but parks featuring Warner Bros. themed rides usually have a very small budget to put towards theming.

Amazing. Best coaster in Australia. Will rank it again when I ride it backwards. 
The first drop is definitely the highlight/scariest part of the ride. Afterwards, however is so much fun.

Finally, a Mack hyper coaster that doesn’t vibrate! This is an excellent ride. The first drop in the back (10) row is absolutely gargantuan, you don’t touch your seat for the entire descent. The first camelback delivers sustained airtime, and the inverted loop is a fantastic element (especially once the train has warmed up) that you don’t see nearly enough on other coasters.
The rest of the layout is fairly basic, but it still offers some great airtime moments that almost turn into ejector airtime once the train is running hot.
Despite all these positives, it’s disappointing to see average crowds and only one train operating. But what’s even more frustrating is seeing those two backwards seats empty all day long. Then again, at $20 per person, per ride, it’s not exactly surprising…
Especially considering that I tried to buy a seat at 4:08pm and was told it was too late to ride backwards, even though the park didn’t close until 5:00pm and the queue for the backwards seats was completely empty.
Anyway, thanks to Mack Rides, but no thanks to Movie World
Backwards is awesome

my ride count on this master piece is around 32 when i wrote my review and my first time on it was in 2020 amazing ejector airtime fun non inverting loop world class drop would be better if it had a longer ride time though comfortable Mack lap bars 9/10

I always ask for the back on this masterpiece of a coaster to experience that first drop over and over. Definitely one of the best first drops on a coaster in the world. The whip on the non inverting loop is insane. Also the bunny hills at the end provide massive ejector like the first drop. Masterpiece by Mack Rides. Best ride in all of Australia

Very good hyper. I appreciate Mach's creativity putting different elements into hypers instead of just camelback after camelback. The combination of the twisted first drop, massive airtime hill, and camelback is elite. After that, the ride dies a little bit with the helixes, but still throws in a lateral ejector pop somewhere in there. Luckily, it redeems itself at the end with the incredibly powerful bunny hills. Riding those last bunny hills backwards is a crazy experience. While it has its flaws, this is still an elite coaster and I'll take it over any B&M hyper.
First drop backwards **chefs kiss

DC rivals is an outstanding coaster. The first drop is phenomenal, yanking riders over the first crest into an 89 degree drop that aggresively twists to the right before it is halfway through. This is one of the best first drops I have experienced and provides massive ejector airtime (especially in the back row). 

Rivals imediately tears through the next elements, a huge camel back airtime hill followed by a towering non-inverting loop. The later rips riders downward to the left as they exit the loop (I experienced strong laterals,  followed by a decent pop of airtime; there was genuinely a sensation of been thrown out of my seat). 

Many criticise the proceeding elements (i.e., the overbank turns and stengel dives, S-curves, and the helix) for a lack of intensity and their combined effect in reducing the rides breakneck pacing. Whilst I agree that the first few elements are the stand outs (and that DC Rivals knocks the intensity down a notch) my experience throughout the mid course was one of graceful speed and nice pops of airtime (the coaster offers a wonderful sensation of flight). I will also argue that the stengal dive into the helix offers one of the best ejector moments on the ride and the helix itself pulls some decent positives. Therefore, whilst not perfect, I thourghly enjoyed the middle section of the ride.

Rivals concludes in intense fashion, shooting you up out of your seat as the train attacks a series of bunny hills, before slamming into the break run. Overall, the experience is top tier and left me with a massive smile on my face. The presentation is also beautiful, with the purple track winding throughout the queensland mangroves (the giant Joker face at the crest of the drop is also a nice touch). There is not a bad seat on the train (though the backwards row is the most intense) and the experience will have you coming back for more (and more and more and more).
It was a really good ride and I loved it.

Love the first drop, Mack does a great job with the first drops on their Hyper Coaster Model. The Non-Inverting Loop and Camelback are great elements. I will say the middle section of the layout is quite boring but the finale makes up for it providing solid ejector airtime.
already a masterpiece forwards, but the backwards seat is a top 5 coaster experience of all time
DC rivals is the best coaster i've ridden. The airtime and first drop are world class.
A good first drop, with sustained airtime throughout the ride. It’s can be more intense however.

My current #1 as of now! The first airtime ejector camel-back is PERFECT, very sustained. The non-inverting loop is whippy and floaty as can be, too. Then there is the the twister section, which is good normally but freakin' amazing in the backwards seat! Then there are 2 demented airtime s hills, a twisted airtime hill and a hop into the breaks. Airtime and whip perfection!
First drop is isane! Thereafter fast as hell!!!
So good, just smooth with good features, though they could remove the helix at the end or put it after the airtime hills.
AT NIGHT >>>>>>>>

Taron certainly is an amazing coaster but I think the theming and the speed are carrying the whole ride, 'cause it's not that intense and it has only 3 real airtime spots in his 1.3 km lay out... weak if you ask me. Tho the duration and the launches also stand out on this coaster and it's still a #4 for me.
It's almost perfect and the immersion is unparalleled for a coaster of this size, but - for me - the layout itself lacks a bit of airtime and is a tad too repetitive with too few iconic moments.

Taron is one of the best coasters of Europe in my opinion. The theming is outstanding like almost every ride at Phantasialand. Both of the launches are great: the first one has a bit more kick to it, while the second launch feels like you fly past it. Taron has a reckless pace after each launch, but on the end of each half, you start slowing down a bit. The smoothness of the track makes the experience of Taron even more amazing!

Great world class coaster but pretty overrated in my opinion. I love the theming and immersion of it but it just didn’t really hit for me as it wasn’t intense and had weak airtime at best. I think if it did more with its layout it would be higher for me. I’ll have to go back to Phantasialand and get a night ride cuz I’ve heard those are amazing.

Such a special ride
Goes to show you don’t need inversions to deliver  an amazing experience. I was so impressed with the lay out, the pacing and the smoothness.
A truly well executed coaster.

What a fantastic ride! The theming is arguably the best in the world, the capacity and comfort are among the best and the experience is just superb. It has some amazing moments, but in my honest opinion it really lacks inversions.
Very very great surprise ! All those turns are strong and intense, I absolutely loved it !!!

Taron became my favorite ride when I rode it for the first time...very fun, obviously the most fun part are the launches, especially the second. It's not overly intense and that's good for me. It's also smooth and the surroinding area is stunning, my favorite in phantasialand and one of my favorites ever.
Great multilaunch coaster with amazing theming, there is really no negatives.

Taron is absolutely fantastic, it has some great ejector and a few with whip, it almost reminds me of a more thrilling version of SWSD Manta or Mecalodon, which is a big compliment coming from me, mind you! That said, I have to say I think it is a biiit overhyped, at least compared to what I tend to like the most in coasters, it doesn't have the strength or sustainability of other world-class coasters in its ejector, but it does have a suddenness which i commend it for! and if you're one to enjoy theming and immersion, the way it weaves around klugheim is just beautiful! it's not something i too strongly value in my rankings, but that certainly adds to the experience! overall, a top tier coaster still deserving 5 stars, even if i rate it slightly below most people!

In my opinion a totally flawless ride, i seemed the enjoy every single moment on the ride and never felt like any took away from the pacing. The twisted ejector airtime hill, the second launch and the first twist out of the tunnel are some of my favorite ride elements of all time. And the theming is just absolutely insane and adds onto what is already an amazing coaster.
Just a stupendous ride. Tonnes of near misses. Fast. Intense. Ejector at times. Just a masterpiece

What an amazing rollercoaster, everything about it is just FAN-TAS-TIC. The launches are very strong, especcialy the second is such a big surprise. Because there is just so much theming you're going past and trough you have no idea where you're going, wich is something I love about it. Every turn and hill is just so strong. And the theming is just out of this world, when you enter the area it feels like a different world. Everything is themed to the max and I am a big fan of it.

The layout is a twisted mess, which is what makes it so awesome.  You never know what's coming next.  The launches are great, and the theming throughout is so immersive.  There are a few little dead spots, but the rest of the layout makes up for them.  Excellent ride ops keep the line moving.

You can only indicate three pros? That's disappointing! I would like to mark ten pros... One of the best roller coasters out there, without a doubt. It's not the most challenging of them all, but this is a masterpiece. A LOT of people can get on it, because it feels so comfortable and safe. Some people like other coasters more because more people don't dare to get on it, but I then you only rate to brag. Top class roller coaster!
Taron has the most unexpected elements and combined with the theming make it the ultimate ride which still holds up to this day.

WHAT A NOISE! That second launch is something special with the noise. Taron's location and theming are incredible. The ride itself is really good, but a little lacking if you compare it to another Intamin launch coaster like Velocicoaster or Maverick. Not as much airtime as I would like, and not a huge amount of variety in the elements. But it makes up for that with the radical location with the beautiful rock faces you fly through.

its perfect. the launches are amazing and the layout is just so well done, it goes through its layout with such a good speed and the moment it starts to lose its speed it throws the second launch at you which is amazing. the theming also is just very well done with klugheim.
Woah, this was amazing. Both launches were super quick and got me out of my seat, so thrilling and such a good coaster

Taron is an amazing launch coaster with amazing theming which makes this ride much better. The launches are the highlights in my opinion, especially the second one which is incredibly fast. The rest of the layout has some great turns and amazing airtime moments. The only thing I miss are inversions, I think they would make this ride even better.
Amazing layout with good near-misses and a powerful second launch.
Rode this a while ago was mid felt slow and the second half was no different then the first

Taron is a great Intamin Blitz, it has 2 powerfull launches which launches you to an intense 113 kmph, the ride is also pretty smooth, for those thin people (like me) the lap bar prob wont touch fully your lap, I could squeeze my hand between the bar and my lap, since the restraint has a point where it doesn't come down further, because of this, the first turn yanked my body to the side, which kinda hurt a bit, but the rest of the coaster is great! :D

5 stars. Hands down one of the best coasters ever. The theming is spectacular. The lauches are awesome, the second one is really next level. The sound is so good. The layout is awesome and so unique underground and thorugh the mountain structures

Amazing first row experience, especially when not holding on to the harness and just let yourself really “fly” with the ride. It’s really a fun ride, the theming is super immersive and adds to the whole hype and experience. Good set up of the lockers with the wristbands.
Amazing ride with lots of airtime and inversions.

Was really excited for this and was very dissapointed. Theming is great, but that's the only pro (Also how you start the coaster was very unexpected and cool).

Now to the bad part. It didn't feel like flying, it felt more like falling. You are pushed really hard into the harness, which is very uncomfortable. I didn't really see anything and was very disorientated. It's on the list of my worst coasters and I really thought I would like it. Nothing for me I guess. (It was also not Fun at all, it was just boring)

1 Star for F.L.Y.
Super underrated and just a really fun experience
It looks great, but the ride itself is a huge disappointment, I barely felt anything, imagine if the trains were more like Flying Dinosaur or even just inverted, would be much better experience.

The theming is wonderfully immersive, and the layout is so good.  The designers of this ride understand that seat position, poor restraints and too much intensity create discomfort on fliers.  Most fliers hurt my rib cage, but FLY seats are nicely angled to lessen the G forces on the chest.  Also, the intensity is perfect.  There's just enough intensity to make it fun but not too much to where the forces would be uncomfortable.  My first ride was in the front, and the flying sensation was so cool.  The only slight discomfort was near the end when my neck was fatigued from holding my head up.  Overall, just a great coaster experience.

I was a bit disappointed by this ride, even if I know that its strenght is mostly the theme rather than the thrill. Weirdly, I'm not the biggest fan of its theme, it feels too vintage for me, but of course that's just me, and it's undoubtly stunning and well done. Its biggest problem is the lack of comfort for me: I didn't know how to put my head, if I try to keep it forward it ends up hurting my neck and shoulders. So that wasn't a pleasant experience for me.

F.L.Y. is a unique work of art. I thought that Klügheim was already very immersive until they opened Rookburgh. This area is just unbelievable. When i first walked in, i genuinely didn't have any words for it. They thought about every single detail. The soundscape, the buildings, the hotel that's part of the coaster and area (something where Phantasialand is very good that) and even the little puffs of smoke coming from the sewers. It's a whole new world you step in. But, the coaster, it is smooth and so much fun because of the unique feature of hanging on your stomach under the track. It creates very cool inversions and elements where you really feel like your flying through all of the mentioned details. Another 5 stars for me in Phantasialand.
That is my top1 rollercoaster.

This coaster is a work of art. The ride and the area is the best I've ever seen in a theme park. The way you get on and off is so clever and the pre launch section is just amazing. The station and soundtrack is beautiful like the area around it. It's soooo smooth and the launches are so fun and the two inversions are so cool. The airtime moments give you some amazing floater airtime which makes you feel like you are flying and the ride just lasts forever. Immaculate ride. Nothing to fault it is flawless and worth going to the park alone for. It's just mind boggling in an incredible way. 👌

This ride is one of the best Vekoma's I've ever ridden. The theming is extraordinary, especially troughout the queue. The layout itself is very fluid and smooth. I also find FLY to be quite intense and fast. The views on this ride are amazing aswell. All in one, this coaster makes for an amazing and unique experience!
Great Theming, Great queue, great airtime, great everything
It's just a awesome Coaster.

Best flying coaster I've ridden! Worlds above Galactica at Alton Towers. I enjoyed the pre-ride section and the transition from sitting upright to flying. Very smooth and a lot of fun. For me would be made better by some bigger drops. Theming is incredible in this area.
One of kind in the world. Not too intense so that younger guests wouldn‘t ride it but not too tame for the Thoosies. Nice floater airtime and if you‘re lucky even ejector.

F.L.Y. felt very different from any other B&M flyer I'd done. While the B&Ms focus on forces on your back with the pretzel loop, F.L.Y. has forces on your chest, and a TON of it. It's a really different feeling that I really enjoyed. And in the front you also get quite a few "ejector" moments. Getting forces on your back cresting a hill is such an unique feeling and also something only F.L.Y. can do, so that also felt incredibly special! I still prefer Tatsu to it as a flyer, but F.L.Y. is absolutely fantastic for what it is!
Long wait time

F.L.Y. is simply put one of the most fun coasters I've ridden. I wasn't too huge on the flying position but the interactions, the (very underrated) layout and infinite amount of visuals absolutely make up for it. The second half of the coaster is just incredible with great airtime, surprisingly intense moments and a really fun corkscrew just make me want to come back for more. And ofcourse, the theming is arguably the best in the world. They left no space empty, everywhere you look there's something to see and it all looks incredible.

This is a great ride with a layout that's both unique and intense. The launches aren't too powerful, but maybe that's for the best in this position. The first launch also gets faster near the end, which kind of compensates for the lack of initial power. The inversions and airtime pops are floaty and just feel insane in this position. It also just looks cool flying around such a well themed land and interacting with the pathways. The pre-launch section also looks great. As for which row I prefer, it has to be row 1, as the airtime is more pronounced here. The back is also great. The lading system is also really efficient despite the lockers and metal detectors. Hey, Tokyo Dome City and especially Fuji-Q Highland, it's actually possible to be efficient with lockers and metal detectors, why not implement the same procedures as Phatasialand? My only nudge is that it's not the most comfortable thing in the world. My second ride on April 9th was perfectly fine, but my first ride was after lunch and the restraint just pressed against it on the positive G moments, and my only ride during my second day at the park was good, but the lap bar crushed my thighs a little bit my the end. A ride that needs to be ridden in specific conditions to really be top notch just can't make it up to my top 3. Number 5 is where it's at for now.
Update July 2024: Well, I have to say that everything that I said about discomfort doesn't stand anymore. I mean it can press on your stomach a little bit but it's fine. I really enjoyed it more this time and it was hauling through it's layout on my ride in row 1.
Update October 2024: I still really like this coaster, but I wasn't as impressed with it as I was in July. I prefer Black Mamba to F.L.Y. now actually. F.L.Y. is just not as dynamic or well paced as Taron or Black Mamba to be in my top 2 coasters in the park.

I thought I'd love this ride but found it very disappointing. It was impossible to fully enjoy because the harness and positioning is so uncomfortable. I also didn't live the layout. There's a lot of positive G which made the discomfort worse. 
With flying coasters I like to feel like I'm soaring through the air. This one just felt all too compact and not very graceful.

This is so smooth! You feel like you're flying, and you don't want it to end. They managed to make a 3 minute ride not drag on and super smooth!!! Impressive with the space they had to work with definitely the best coaster I've ever gone on! The flying element is unique and amazing.

FLY is a truly magical ride with some of the best theming. It's innovative design and wonderfully crafted layout set out a magical ride experience. The timeless steampunk theme reverberates around Rookborough like a saintly voice and seeing the modern trains fly around the track is a magical experience. Overall it has earned it's place amongst the world's best and is the perfect example of how theming can turn a great ride into a world-class ride!

I managed to get 5 rides on this during my recent trip to Phantasialand and I have to say, what an experience. I must say, however, I got off my first ride with a lot of discomfort in my legs, due to the feeling they were slipping out of the restraints, and fighting the G's to keep them in a natural position. Letting my legs relax on subsequent rides felt so much better and properly allowed me to enjoy the experience of soaring over Rookburgh.

After having 1 ride in the front, and 3 in the very back, I am in two minds about which experience was better. The front gives you the best flying sensation on any coaster (I've ridden Tatsu, Flying Dinosaur, and Superman) and has amazing visuals. The second launch also feels more forceful in the front.

The back completely whips you around each corner and found myself greying out a couple of times, especially after the launches. It's much more of a whippy/intense experience that I found to be the perfect compliment after riding in the front.

Currently in my top 3!

F.L.Y. is an amazing coaster, it location in the Rookburgh area is amazing and adds a lot to this area. The queue is well themed and I also like the darkride scenes. The coaster is not about crazy intense elements, but just about flying through the area and get amazing views. You really feels like you are flying and not on track. The coaster is also really long. This coaster is just a masterpiece with amazing theming. The seating position can be a bit uncomfortable but it is not too bad.

Maybe the best flying coaster in the world, set in a steampunk world with beautiful theming. Super comfortable overall, although the airtime is noticeably weaker in the back row. You’re also only pulled along slowly afterward, so hope for one of the front rows—you can’t choose your seat. The ride ops aren’t the best.

I LOVED Iron Rattler far more than I expected. I thought it would serve as more of a legacy prototype for newer RMC's, but it was far more complete and modern than I anticipated.  It's my personal #3-ranked RMC with only Steel Vengeance and Iron Gwazi ahead of it. While it doesn't have the intensity of those two rides (and not much else does), it's in that next tier. And the way it weaves so many killer RMC elements into the topography of the quarry setting is what sets it apart from Wildcat's Revenge, ArieForce, and Twisted Timbers, in my opinion. There is an ever-so-slight slow down on top of the quarry wall which is well documented by others, but it hardly impacts the experience. Everything else was really good to great. The first drop is as advertised, only outdone by SteVe and IG. The single inversion is perfectly placed and executed. And the dark tunnel and final drop off the quarry wall close the ride experience out in a distinct and quite remarkable fashion. With it's reputation well-known and a number of RMC's under my belt already, it's hard to believe how pleasantly surprised I was by this ride. I largely had a sense of what was coming and Iron Rattler still overdelivered for me.
It's a crying shame that these trains were never built again. RMC all these years later still stands to learn a thing or two about comfort from Gerstlauer, of all companies.

That dive off the quarry wall in the second half is worth the price of admission by itself. Intense and ejector-filled. I camped out by Iron Rattler  and marathoned it for an entire day. 11/10 experience.

Iron Rattler is one of a kind. First, you’ve got arguably the best drop in the world. Then, the rest of the layout is pure perfection.

The way the ride interacts with the quarry wall is a masterpiece in terrain coaster design. You get not one, but TWO “jump offs” the quarry. The second one (before the tunnel) is one of the best sustained airtime hills I’ve ever experienced. 

Biggest downside is length. And the train can lose a bit of speed up on the quarry wall, but this isn’t an issue on a hot day or later in the afternoon/evening.

This coaster holds a special place in my heart being one of the first I've ever ridden. I used to be afraid of coasters, but this coaster helped me demolish that fear. And after four years and 84 more coasters, Iron Rattler still holds its own in my top 5 (#3 to be exact, below Cannibal and Taron in first). Everyone claims that the highlight of the ride is the drop of the quarry wall, but I disagree. For me, it's the first drop in the back row (and yes, you can pick a row). The drop off the quarry wall is great, giving sustained ejector airtime that tries to rip you out of your seat, and you keep falling for what feels like forever. However, the drop does the same thing WHILE turning to the left. So, you are thrown out of your seat and midair you are yanked to the side, and that is a sensation unbeaten. Plus, it's the first drop so you keep falling as well. But the main selling point of this coaster is its location. It dives on and off of the quarry wall which makes it a terrain coaster, and the interactions on top and with the wall (especially the drop off of it) is insane. While the terrain might not be that of Taron or Velocicoaster, it is the best terrain I've ever seen on a Six Flags Coaster. Now, the reason I didn't give it five stars is because of the dead spots. Literally every review you will ever hear talks about the section on the quarry wall. It CRAWLS over those elements and, while still fun, is out of flow with the rest of the fast-paced ride. Otherwise, it's a great ride and pretty decent theming for a Six Flags coaster (but SFFT is pretty good at theming in general). With 4.5 stars, this coaster is an absolute must do if you are anywhere near San Antonio.

Features two of the best elements on any coaster: the first drop and the quarry wall dive. Its setting is awesome. Ride this later in the day because in the morning it absolutely crawls on top of the quarry wall.

I've been on Iron Rattler 146 times. I would be lying if I said it never got a bit old, especially on slower days, as I am pretty much completely used to the forces. However, on night rides after a hot Texas day, this ride still manages to shake me up. That should tell why it deserves such high praise.
hands down best drop on any RMC!!!

Iron rattler is my favorite ride in all of Texas right now. It has a great first drop that can take you by surprise if you don’t expect the turn. It has also good airtimes moments, and the drop of the quarry wall in the back car can eject you out of your seat. I also slightly prefer these trains compared to the more modern RMC trains, they have slightly more room

The first drop is without a doubt the best first drop in the world and the second drop off the cliff is one of the best airtime moments ever. If they made this longer it would easily be top 15 maybe even top 10
I loved it sooooo much it is my favorite roller coaster I have ever been on
It is the best coaster in tx and my fav ever. Just wish it was longer
Best ride in the park and in Texas (that I've been on)
oh my god. holy crap. that's all I can say. absolutely blew my mind. wonderful.
This is a fantastic coaster. It plays better with the quarry wall than any other ride in the park. It’s full of amazing airtime. Crazy whippy. Only minor critique is that it’s over pretty quick.

This is a really fun ride. It is packed full with intense airtime. It has an insane first drop. It’s a little short but not that bad. The trains and lap bars feel so freeing and no hint of pain at all much better than other RMC trains I’ve rode.
Long fun airtime

Love the way it interacts with quarry wall. It’s not only a fun ride to look at it is also an amazing ride. Amazing airtime the whole way through, people said it ran slow but I rode it 3 hours after park opened and it was not running slow what so ever. Then I rode it around 7 and it was running way faster. I also love the dive into the pitch black tunnel at the end.

Iron Rattler is a really great RMC!! The location on the quarry wall is one-of-a-kind, and the layout itself is really well done. It's slightly less intense than the other RMCs I've been on (Wildcat's Revenge & Iron Gwazi) but that does not take away from how much I like this ride. The first drop and the other drop over the quarry are both amazing and give great airtime. The ride is smooth, fast, fun, and thrilling from start to finish, and I wish I could have ridden it more than once. I would marathon this all day if I could. It's currently my #3 favorite coaster because it's so peak.

Its a good ride, but it was super disappointing. People hype this ride as the best coaster in Texas but I cannot call it top 3 in the state. Main cons is the slow quarry crawl in middle of the ride, which is not something you should have on a short ride like this. It does have 3 good moments, being the twisted first drop (which was overrated), the roll near the middle, and the ejector dive at the end (That was also overrated).

I really loved this ride. It has a crazy first drop and works really well with the terrain. It has some fun airtime moments after the roll, before the quarry drop, one of the best airtime moments I’ve ever ridden. The ride also has a cool tunnel with a gently banked turn in complete darkness before a smooth but snappy turn into the brakes.
This was lot of fun, and surprising at times. A bit short maybe, but smooth and thrilling.

I think Iron Rattler is a very good ride! I like the drop, it really whips you down it. The first ejector hill gives the crazy ejector and the two drops down the quarry are super cool! The Zero-G Roll is super floaty too and always gets me out of my seat! I like some of the things on top of the quarry like the first hill is super good but the real moment is the ejector hill off the quarry! It is so good, it pulls you all the way down and you just go all the way out of your seat! Then the tunnel gives a good sense of speed and is pitch black until you get your last pop of airtime and go into the brake run. Overall this is a great coaster and definitely is in my top 5 overall!

Iron Rattler has an outstanding steep first drop in a memorable setting. It contains also a wonderful air time inversion. The section on the cliff looks slow paced in the POVs, but in the real life it is pretty fun too. The drop from the cliff is again superb but unfortunately the ride ends too soon after that.
This was the last roller coaster I rode with an appendix.
Made me fall back in love with rollercoasters.
Awesome attraction. Decently themed, super fun and smooth, still a great ride even though they got rid of the launch

Special coaster that once rode like one of the best in the world but that's not the case anymore. Now it feels like watching your favorite athlete after they've exited their prime - the affection will always be there but there's an awkwardness hanging around. Lightning Rod has taken too many body blows between the loss of the launch and all the steel modifcations that have fortified the back half but haven't addressed the pothole between the wave turn (which is taken too slowly) and the outward banked hill. Thankfully the remaining layout has enough speed for some flashes of brilliance - the quad down can still reach that out of control bliss - and it's a testament to how singular Lightning Rod is that I still love going back to it even if that feeling involves a heavy dose of nostalgia.

I’d like to preface this review by saying I only had the opportunity to ride Lightning Rod on cold, rainy days. I could very well be severely underselling the ride. 
However, I was still disappointed by the ride’s length and terrible wood sections that should be replaced ASAP. I also found it to lack the bite many newer RMCs have, and I believe this may be a bit overhyped due to its legacy status. I did really enjoy the first few elements and the overrated but still awesome “quad-down”, but I found the middle of layout was just okay, not something you can afford to do with such a short layout. 
As it nears a decade of operation, in my opinion Lightning Rod has fallen from grace to newer competition.

Though I never experienced Lightning Rod with the launch, the Lift Hill version is nothing short of elite. Sporting a beautiful setting, incredible first drop, insane terrain layout, and one of the all-time greatest finales with the insane Quad Down, Lightning Rod is easily world-class. Not to mention, it's loaded with extreme ejector airtime- an RMC staple.
Before riding this, I was definitely overrating this coaster but after riding this it shut me up and proved that it was the coaster people were obsessing over!  Easily the best coaster at Dollywood!
IM SO MAD THEY REMOVED THE LAUNCH but anyways this coaster is amazing

text: Shame they had to remove the launch but it was for the better.

I rode this coaster on my 23rd birthday and it was absolutely crazy! Of course it does suck that I never got to ride the launched version, but with a layout like this, who cares if there's no launch? The airtime was absolutely bonkers, especially that quad down finale everyone's been telling me about! Now that's how you celebrate a birthday!

Kinda sad that the launch isn't there. but still, that is the most powerful airtime i've ever felt on a coaster. not only that, but it uses the mountain to it's advantage, and not as an obstacle. one of the best coasters ever

This ride rips! I never got a chance to experience it with the launch but as a lover of the smoky mountains I still really enjoyed the views from the lift hill. The pre drop leads to a great first drop and the ride never lets up from there. The bank turns are tight and forceful as you wind through the smokies in a ride full of incredible airtime moments. Lightning Rod is a relentless airtime machine that crescendos into an all time great element with the quad down that leaves you walking off saying holy shit, that was awesome. An amazing ride from start to finish.
This was an amazing ride! This was for sure the best ride I have ever ridden! The first drop was awesome. It would be cool if I experienced the launch, but it's ok. Amazing ride.

This is the roller coaster that made me an enthusiast back in 2019. Coming back in 2025 I was very worried that the coaster that started it all would fall in my rankings. Although the removal of the launch was quite disappointing, and certainly didn't help improve the ride, it did not hurt the overall ride experience. I am happy to say that the lightning rod that I fell in love with six years ago remains to this day inside my top 10. The only problem with this ride is the transition from I-box to topper track which is pretty jarring. The park should have just replaced all of the wood rather than frankensteining the ride.
Just good at best post launch removal.
Literally can't find anything wrong with it except the removed launch

this thing is so good. i rode this twice with the launch and its really sad to see it with a lift hill. but the launch was fantastic, the quad down was stellar, and the ride was glass smooth! I rode it in the back and there wasn't really any shuffling throughout the experience!
Amazing airtime its ejector the whole ride the first drop is great and it flys through its layout small vibration but other then that its absolutely amazing

One of the cool things about Lightning Rod is that it spends no time being chill after the chain lift as it has a mini drop before the actual drop that tricks you into thinking you will descend the full hill, but you just go down a small amount. You then are pulled back up a small bit, and only then do you go down (I remember the entire train being fooled by this), this time taking in great speed that is honestly so ridiculously fast that it feels like you are in a centrifuge rather than a roller coaster. After this, the coaster never lets up as it throws you side to side, chucks you out of your seat, and plunges you through many other intense elements. The quad down finale is the best ending ever. My only problem with this amazing coaster is that it is too short. An extra minute would have been amazing. Other than that, this is one of the best coasters at the park, behind only Thunderhead for me.
My second favorite RMC behind steel vengeance, awesome quad down, the first drop, wave turn, outer banks, and even the pre drop are all awesome

Wow this ride is unbelievable, I could ride this a million times and would not get bored. When you are on this it is so special to see the landscape and it is on a hill that is so cool. When you go into the downwards quad down it is one of the most iconic moments on. A rollercoaster. It is so fun.
Not my favorite RMC. Some rough spots throughout the ride. Still very fun!
Nice ride but idk why they don’t want to fully IBOX the track cuz I think it would be one of my favorite rmcs bc it has a lot of rattle which was kinda annoying

My first ride, I wasn't 100% sold on its greatness. After a few back-to-back night rides, however, it launched its way up my favorite coasters of all time rankings. The air is crazy, ejector style. Literally on the border of downright frightening and/or painful. Truly on the edge of what our bodies can withstand and still enjoy. The most intense ejector air ever, by a wide, wide margin. Crazy fun. The launch up the hill is...interesting, not necessarily spectacular, just different--it does give a decent air pop over the top. Then the 90 degree banked turns at the top of the hills were truly disorienting--especially at night. Then the return trip home down the mountain. Truly epic. Air, then air, then air, then air again. The whole time you are getting faster and faster and more and more intense. Good times for sure. Great coaster for sure. Truly a world class thrill machine.  

Update:  I rode this a few months back with my Dad.  The line was pretty silly all day.  We didn't get to ride this until about an hour before close.  We rode it I think 3 maybe 4 times in a row as the line kept getting shorter and shorter as we approached closing time.  It no longer launches up the lift hill--to me it didn't take anything at all away from the overall ride experience as the launch didn't do a ton to begin with.  The 90-degree banked turns at the top of the hills are still crazy and awesome.  The trip home back down the mountain is still the money maker for this coaster and makes it truly one of the best on the planet.  The ejectors are still as great as ever.  Still one of the best.
Hyped this up way too much, but it’s still a great ride. Was lucky enough to get a ride right as the park was closing. Next level night ride!
Wicked cyclone's crack cocaine infused step brother
Very aggressive airtime the entire ride. Very fun. I marathoned this coaster at my visit and i loved every second of it. Great coaster
Not as good as Lightning Run
This ride deserves to be higher than 37 Storm Chaser is a great RMC coaster in a dumb park

Don’t get me wrong, I love this ride. Out of my weak credit count of 40, it came in at number four, which seems high on the surface, but that means it’s barely in my top 10% of coasters. I thought this would be my number one or two. It was definitely overhyped for me, and I have heard that it runs on different wheels depending on the year, but I don’t know it just wasn’t it. The airtime was strong floater at best and I expected to be flying through the double up, but it felt like I was riding down the drop on Woodstock Express. Just slow and disappointing.
