went on a dead day and rode storm chaser 20 times in a row with its amazing airtime but those Rmc restraints gave me tons of bruises on my legs.

The ride is perfectly paced and super intense. The barrel roll drop, the first sustained ejector hill, the hard banked first overbank, and the twin twisted airtime hills give an explosive start to the ride. The ride tones down a little bit with the second overbank, smaller airtime hill, and zero-g roll. But the finale ends it with a bang: The trick-track double up followed immediately by a double down. This is the most intense sequence of airtime I've ever experienced. Storm Chaser's only downfall is the lack of theming, scenery, or foliage. The ride is very boring to look at. The RMC trains aren't the best, without anything to hang on to, and can get uncomfortable with rerides. Otherwise, a perfect coaster with excellent pacing, forces, and an insane finale.

For a "bottom tier" I-Box RMC it's still leagues better than most other thrill coasters out there despite its moderate size. Wind Chaser manages to pack all the signature RMC elements into a relatively compact layout that does putter out just before the final break run.

This ride has some of the strongest and most violent airtime of any coaster.  While the pacing is a bit off at times, the the ejector is as stronger as any other coaster and has one of if not the single strongest moment of airtime on any coaster with the first pop of the trick track double up. There’s other coasters with more to them and a few with similar airtime, but this rides pure strength is what gives it a spot in my top 10.

wind chaser was a pretty solid ride, the first drop with the barrel roll is one of my favorite inversions and i wanna know what twisted timbers is like with the same element. the inversions were smooth and baisically the whole ride is and the layout is really good and can probably be copied for more smaller parks. i think they shouldve kept the other side of twisted twins and made it duel. also why cant all rmc coasters have lapbars like lightning rod and have handle bars, also every time i rode this i got stapled every time.

While this roller coaster may not exceed Lightning Run in overall preference, it nonetheless stands as an exceptional compact RMC. It consistently delivers substantial airtime, an engaging and distinctive initial drop, and enjoyable low-to-the-ground elements.

A small but mighty RMC, there’s plenty of funky airtime and floaty inversions. Some poor soul didn’t secure their phone and it almost immediately flew off towards the stratosphere, so that should tell you about the forces. Shame they only converted one track though.

I really like this ride, it packs such a great punch for how small it is. If you love great ejector moments you would love this ride and on top of that it is super reridable because each row gives a different experience on the first drop varying the whip/hangtime on the first drop. Me personally I like the front the best because it gives the strongest forces and gives an amazing drop. My one grievance with this ride is that the last run of airtime hills hits really hard and can sometimes hurt really bad if the seatbelt or restraint is in a weird spot. Other than that though this ride is a knock out of the park for Kentucky Kingdom.
Feels like a baseline RMC hybrid to me. Doesn't stand out from the others but always delivers the punch.

Top-tier element variety, and every element is seeping with quality. Great pacing on top of that. Shockingly intense and forceful without beating you up. Graduates to an elite coaster once it’s warmed up. Worth the price of admission alone!
it will always be Storm Chaser

Awesome RMC. I enjoyed the first drop more than I excepted. The inversions were great and there was great ejector airtime. Pretty smooth. Overall a very good ride, would be better if it was taller, but for its height it’s awesome.

This ride is nothing more but exhilarating. Airtime, smoothness! Yet, the buckle to the lap bar is somewhat discomforting if you don't position it right. Overall, A great coaster with a good amount of airtime

One of RMC's best rides EVER! The airtime is absolutely incredible from start to finish, the barrel roll downdrop is just as amazing as the one on Twisted Timbers. The airtime is simply the best thing about this ride. I'd only ever rode this ride as Storm Chaser, and it was such a fun coaster, and I'd absolutely return to Kentucky Kingdom for it. 10/10
It has amazing ejector airtime. A insanely intense first drop. And good pacing exeot for the end. But beware of the rattle.

UPDATED REVIEW: I GOT A HALF DUEL!!! Props to the crew running this thing on 7/29/24! They were actively telling guests that we had a very limited time window to catch the other train on the lift hill. This built a ton of anticipation and it meant both trains got one duel per run which isn’t bad! And yes, I can confirm that this thing was meant to duel. It was NEXT LEVEL!! Between watching the other train fly along next to you and getting shot out of your seat is just incredible. Twisted Colossus is JAM-PACKED with solid ejector airtime. The first drop, the wave-turn high-five, and EVERY SINGLE HILL will ABSOLUTELY LAUNCH YOU out of your seat!!! If this is the airtime on what is supposedly a “lower-tier” RMC, I cannot imagine what it’s like on something like Iron Gwazi. Aside from the endless heavenly airtime, the inversions are very fun. I would describe the stall as pure inverted air, while the zero-g roll is exactly what the name implies. This thing is also SILKY SMOOTH. Smoothest coaster I’ve ever ridden. IF I HAVE ONE PIECE OF ADVICE, I would say set your expectations right. If you go in expecting a duel, you may be very disappointed. I would go in and just try to appreciate the layout and airtime for what it is. Believe me, I did that the very first time I rode it and it did wonders. Overall, an ABSOLUTELY AMAZING work of art and a must-do at SFMM!!!
I have nothing bad I can say about this coaster. Literally zero complaints. I wish everybody in the world can ride this coaster at least once, then there will be World Peace.
I love twisted colossus and it is such a great ride that greatly fills its spot.But the shin guards on the lap bars take away from the ejector airtime.

Wow. Twisted Colossus is great. It's great. My first ride on it this past Christmas was one of the best i've ever experienced. I finally got that coveted dueling ride and it made this ride skyrocket up my rankings. The headchopper moments, the airtime, the interactions with the other train. All of it is just one of the craziest experiences you can get on a coaster. It might not be the tallest or fastest ride but is still amazing. This ride currently (as of 2/1/25) is at my #2 spot in my rankings. It was also my first RMC and was a truly incredible experience. Go ride it at Six Flags Magic Mountain. you won't regret it.
Really fun airtime machine.  You are out of your seat for at least half the ride (excluding the lifthills and brake run).  I don't care about dueling too much.

New to the enthusiast community, this is the ride that made me join it! This means that I don’t have much comparison to go off of, but it’s definitely my favorite of all the coasters I’ve been on. Consider this a casual review from an outsider’s perspective, I guess. I still don’t have much knowledge tbh, but these are some things I immediately noticed:
- The ejector airtime moments were very fun (my mom was genuinely afraid of flying out of her seat at some points).
- My mother’s back appreciated the smoothness. I’ve heard good things about RMC’s smoothness and am excited to try more of their stuff!
- Going around twice makes it a pretty long ride! There was almost no wait while we were there so it was a treat to just walk straight on and finally feel like a coaster was long enough, as there are a lot of rides I enjoy but feel are much too short.
I do wish they did more theming in the queue, though, as I’m a sucker for steampunk, and the lap bars were a bit uncomfortable. I also really wish we had gotten a duel, especially since my friends somehow ended up in a different train.

Although I only got a half duel, I honestly wasn't expecting Twisted Colossus's single layouts to be as good as they were, and I thought they would be disappointing without the duels, but I was dead wrong. These single layouts without the dueling are still absolutely fantastic. The airtime was absolutely insane and the best I've ever experienced on a coaster, even better than Ghostrider, and even without the other train the hand choppers with the structure were still great. Even though I am disappointed with the reliability of this ride causing me to only get a half duel, the single layouts were still so strong that I think this is one of the best coasters in California even without the dueling, and had I got a full duel it would probably be my #1.
This ride is very close to my heart, the first drop has some of the best airtime ever, and is is ejector city, I really just wished it duels, I only ever have gotten one half duel

Twisted Colossus is a great ride, but unfortunately with the additions of West Coast Racers and Wonder Woman Flight of Courage it now serves no purpose in Magic Mountain's lineup. The now have two other coasters that do exactly what this ride does but better. I also think that this ride didn't live up to the expectations I had, especially because I have never dueled on Twisted Colossus in my life. If you think about it, that's just kind of sad because it's a ride that's meant to duel. I also don't like the gimmick of "two rides in one" because the two laps are very similar and pointless if you don't duel. It also just causes me discomfort and motion sickness. I also absolutely hate the 2nd lift hill, it ruins all the excitement you get from the first lap. Even though I've been talking negatively about the ride, I can still acknowledge that it's a great coaster and has plenty of great moments. The drops on both sides are really good, the step up into the turnaround gives good airtime, the stall is fun, the zero-g roll is whippy, the camelback is strong. On paper this is a great ride and it is a great ride. I just wish it had been executed better so that it would get pushed to that next level of quality that it was supposed to be in.

This is, without question, the best ride at Magic Mountain and it's not close. Twisted Colossus is only 120 feet tall, and especially with Goliath right behind it, this thing looks tiny---but trust me, as soon as you fly over the drop, you will be able to tell which is better. The drop is actually one of my favorites ever---you get so much airtime even though its only 116 feet, and the sense of speed is unreal. The so-called 'high-five banks' are cool too, but I can only imagine how cool they would become if you were dueling. The ejectors, the airtime hills, and especially the top gun stall are absolutely incredible. The top gun stall especially is unbelievable. Also, my one con of SteVe is that the restraints are uncomfortable for me, but despite Twisted Colossus having the same type of restraints, they are bigger and fit me better, making them far more comfortable. Honestly one of the most comfy restraints in the park imo. Best ride at SFMM for sure. However, the reason I put 'reliability' as a con is because this thing was MEANT to duel and they really need to find a way to make it duel more often. I lapped this coaster four times before close hoping for a duel (and props to the ops, they were trying as hard as they could to get us duels), but a few idiots trying to pull their phones out and being slow putting their things away ensured that wouldn't happen. Still, getting to go through the layout twice is awesome, and I really hope SFMM modifies the ride just slightly to ensure a duel every time. I even have some ideas of how they could do that. Overall this is a spectacular ride, and if you don't ride this at MM you haven't been. Trust me.
This is the best coaster I have ever been on, great airtime, great inversions, duels more often than before now too

Wicked Cyclone is an RMC recreation of the old wooden Cyclone coaster that is one of the best rides you’ll have at a park. It is loosely themed to storm chasers and has a great twisting layout that delivers banked turns, stalls, outward hills, and a steep and thrilling first drop that dictates the pace of the entire ride. It is relentless from start to finish with many hills ejecting you from your seat. I recommend riding in the front and back seats to get the best experiences. The lap bar is all that’s needed. This ride is deserving of its praise!

I feel like this RMC has the most room for improvement if I can get over there again and give it a proper sunny day of lapping this thing when it's running hot.  4.5/5 stars

I fear that I have a one-sided love for Twisted Timbers. I love this coaster, but it does not feel the same way about me. I was violently thrown around like a ragdoll and got a pretty nasty bruise on my elbow. So what did I do? Run back in line to ride it a second time, of course! The rain was pouring, but I was determined to ride Twisted Timbers in the front row. Somehow my second ride was even more unpredictable than the first, with rain obscuring my vision and pelting me, the ejector airtime felt even more ridiculous. Twisted Timbers used all its might to throw me out of my seat, and would have surely succeeded if not for the restraint. Clearly, this ride is not for everyone, but I loved it. It may not have the 305ft drop of Pantherian, but it surely feels more out-of-control and ridiculous. Strongest ejector airtime I've ever experienced! I would rank it higher, but it's just a little too intense and the trains are not the most comfortable. Still easily five stars though.

This is the most overrated ride I have ever ridden and I gave this ride a chance with 15 rides over 4 days. The first drop is great with a weird but awesome mix of airtime and hang time and the first speed hill and 180 degree overbanked turn are also good, but after that this ride sucks. There is nothing interesting happening, it’s just the same ejector hill one after another and two terrible and forceless inversions. Last time I rode this was 5 years ago, and I'd forgotten just how insane it is.  Cool first drop.  The airtime is incredible, and your behind is off the seat for most of the ride.  It's amazing how many thrills RMC can pack into a small footprint.   In the front cars, airtimes/ejectors near the end are not fun - too abrupt.   However, middle and back seats were smooth throughout.  I rank this in the lower half of 22 RMCs I've ridden because the layout/ejectors can feel redundant by the second half.  Still a great ride!

This is King's Dominion's best coaster.  RMC hits another home run.  The only other RMC hybrids I've been on are Steel Vengeance and Wildcat's Revenge.  Twisted Timbers is right up there with those.  The start of the ride is fantastic.  It starts with a very unique dive and drop which provide such an amazing sensation.  The next 3 hills provide sustained ejector air time.  Twisted Timbers might just have the best 4 starting elements of any coaster I've ridden.  Then the craziness continues.  You get a series of even more varied air time hills, including one banked to the left and one banked to the right.  There's also an amazing turnaround curve where you are momentarily tilted outward.  You also get a zero G stall and a zero G roll thrown in after that first inversion.  It was just such a good ride and will definitely be in my top 10.
This and Steel Vengeance are the Peak of RMC
Immaculate ride. First drop is disgusting and the whole ride is so smooth. I also love the theming

There are a lot of phrases you can use to describe Twisted Timbers. It's a jack of all trades. Pantherian is its evil twin. It's a bass-boosted Kentucky Derby winner. Its an existential breakdown that you want to do again. These are all accurate ways to illustrate the sheer willpower of this demented ride. I didn't think the drop was anything special, but that isn't even going to make a dent in my rating, because the rest of the ride is just that good. After the drop, this unexpected bunny hop hits you right in the stomach and gives you a good airtime moment. Then you go into a turn that is overbanked and awesome. Then you go into one of the best sequences of pure ejector bliss that you can find in the country. Three back to back to back head rush camel humps (funny, didn't know a camel could have three humps) that try to fling you into another continent. Once you think that's all you can handle, you would lose Who Wants To Be A Millionaire. You get chucked into quick side-to-side movement, fascinating inversions, and of course, the real star of the show, RMC's claim to fame, that sweet sweet airtime, the type that isn't overwhelming but it's still some of the best you'll find anywhere. But, with all of these good things, there is one not-so-great part of the ride. Those who have tall legs, BEWARE. The restraint has uncomfortable shin guards that people with long legs will not like. But at the end of the day, it's a top-tier coaster that is in my own humble opinion the best in the park.

The first half is amazing, filled with airtime, inversions, and speed. However, the second half kinda just spams the “small ejector hill” button too much. Still enjoyable and a massive improvement over hurler but sometimes a bit painful.
Amazing ride, wait times are usually short but can be long bc of the metal detectors. I am blessed to have this at my home park of KD

To borrow a quote from IGN "8/10 too much ejector airtime". Imagine if an entire roller coaster was basically just the last six hill from ArieForce One. A bit of an exaggeration, but man I do not see the appeal of getting blasted into your restraints all the time. That having been said, I do still like the ride overall. The barrel roll drop and first turn are a ton of fun, and the other two inversions are a great time as well. I just kinda wish the layout wasn't obsessed with trying to throw me out of the train.
Great ride but it kind of hurt my thighs
Extremely fun, but too intense to re-ride. Would probably be one of the best coasters in the world if it had better restraints.
Awesome coaster, great airtime, great drop, and good theming, it is my favorite poster in Virginia and my third favorite RMC
The ride is fun and has a great layout
Air time is amazing!! Best ride at kings dominion
Very fun airtime machine which is my favorite type of ride.

Just a great time. The first drop really caught me by surprise and the 3 camelbacks are elite. I'm just not huge on the lateral moments, in the front they're ok but in the back they're just a bit much for me. Still an incredible ride though.
to me this is the real best stand up coaster at sea world.
RIDE THIS AT NIGHT
Great coaster, first half is filled with floater and is so relaxing, but the second half isn’t that good and kind of brings mako down for me. Still really good.
Mako is a high tier hyper with tons of floater. It’s butter smooth and easily one of the most re-rideable coasters I’ve ever done.

Mako is a great coaster. The first half is great. The drop and 5 second airtime hill carry this ride. The the turns in the last half were wild too. After a few rides tho its gets less intense. Overall great ride.

The perfect hyper coaster. Also my most ridden coaster. First drop in the back is INCREDIBLE, lasts forever, never touch the seat, and you get pulled over pretty early. Great airtime, great ending, nothing bad (except for the trim break after the turnaround if it's turned on).

Amazing floater, especially on the five-second hill with. Alongside some of the best floater anywhere, Mako has a killer first drop, an amazing night ride, and a good soundtrack. I might be blinded by nostalgia (given this is my first hypercoaster), but this is still the best conventional hyper (yes, even over diamondback), and there’s nothing to complain about.
Just pure fun from the speed to the airtime to the drops and the banking! It feels like quite a long ride duration when you're on it as well.
Very fun, but scary at first.
The perfect b and m because of its location. I just have been on some others that are more intense like nitro

This was my first time going on a B&M hypercoaster that people didn't hate on. I Really loved the whippy transitions that it did, plus really powerful airtimes. The only complaint I have is the scenery, because the coaster just had flat land around it, but still, not to bad.
Very fun just wish it was more intense
really good floater however the second half could be better
Amazing airtime but a bit repetitive, and in the same style steel dragon is higher and more intense

absolutely fantastic, this ride should be the benchmark for all hypers out there. the fact that its over the water and the layout wraps around the entire edge of the park is so great bro, i love this ride sm
Airtime, airtime, airtime, airtime, and more airtime. Mako is so peak. I love this ride.

Mako is one of the best B&M Hypers ever made. You only have a lap bar without the seatbelt which is honestly awesome. This ride has a good queue and great ops, which makes this thing a capacity eater. The highlights are the first drop and 5 second airtime hill which both are absurd airtime moments, but all the other hills also provide also good floater. Only one hill on this entire ride has trims which is awesome. The second half is slightly underwhelming as you pretty much creep through it. However it doesn't take away from the amazing first half and crazy airtime this ride has.

It was such a vibe riding this at night. I remember flying over the hills faster than other hypers and getting stronger airtime. I didn't feel drained after which I like. It was just a blast, world class ride.

Mako is one of the best B&M Hypers out there, the floater airtime is amazing no matter what seat your in and the first drop is crazy if you sit in the back row. I visited in a quiet time and was able to stay on and ride Mako like 20 times and every time it was amazing. This coaster is very re-rideable and never disappoints. The highlights of the ride for me is the first drop and the multiple airtime hills  providing solid floater in the front and back rows, the 2nd half of the ride after the mid-course brakes is also pretty good as it has multiple low to the ground turns above the water and a bunny hill that doesn't really give you airtime. Other than that bunny hill at the end this ride is amazing and i'm looking forward to riding again.

Mako was my 200th coaster, and what a fantastic ride! It's an airtime machine with an amazing first drop. Yeah, the mid-course brakes suck. Yeah, the second half isn't nearly as good. But who cares? The main part of the ride is so sublime that any little criticisms I might have don't matter at all to me.
Fantastic ride. Best in the park.
Such a fun and graceful giant. Couldn't ask for anymore improvements.

I had nothing bad to say about this ride! The fact that this beauty has a max wait time of 30mins during our visit was UNBELIEVABLE! And I know there are other rides like Kraken with a bunch of inversions that might draw in more enthusiasts, but this ride just goes to show, "One man's trash is another man's treasure". Absolutely amazing! Also, I love the beautiful theming on the entrance. B&M outdid themselves with this one! My favorite part is the first drop. The fact that it's over the water gives for beautiful views and even better illusions. The first drop was built in such a way that you wouldn't realize there was more track until the drop was over. Also, the airtime is insane!! I've ridden it 5 times. It never gets boring.

Smoothest + most comfortable coaster I've been on. Back row is best for airtime intensity. Front row is best for sense of speed and airtime duration. Main con is the airtime hills past the first one don't really get shaped towards the coaster's decreased speed, so they give less airtime with each one. Second airtime hill felt like it would have hit a lot harder if trim breaks weren't placed right before its crest. Everything from the first drop to the trim breaks is 5/5 though.

A titan of a coaster. The sense of speed on this ride is unmatched by any other non-launch coaster I have been on so far. It is much more intense than the bigger B&Ms thanks to the variety in elements and forces. The first drop is terrifying, the following camelback and diveloop are filled with lots of airtime. The rest of the ride has small, close to the ground elements, despite the ride still having tons of momentum. Fast dives, helices, and ejector hills. Great capacity and a smooth ride. Only the lack of outside theming stops this coaster from being a true masterpiece.

To me, Hyperion is the best hyper coaster I've done (As of December 2025) as it feels much more catered to my favourite things about rollercoasters than Zadra was.

This ride is relentless in the back, providing both fantastic airtime and intensity, as well as a standout moment in the dive loop. The whip on that element is nuts in latter rows and outer seats. When I rode this in 2022 I didn't think the outer seat vibrations detracted from the experience, but I'll have to see when I return in 2026!

This ride is the number one at Energylandia, and my personal number one out of the 100 or so rollercoasters I have done. Its speed throughout the layout is unmatched and it has no dead spots in its layout whatsoever. The station theming is still great, despite the lockers being a minor nuisance but I am fine with it. I went for four days and while the first two days were busy, on the third I saw it went to zero minutes and I ran. Front row is incredible on this ride and for everyone saying Zadra is better, it is faster, taller and longer and it feels like it on all three aspects. The vibrations can get a bit annoying but it does not hinder the experience. Completely underrated and is now my most ridden coaster outside the UK.

Fantastic hyper coaster. The first sequence of elements is world class: very steep and powerful first drop, sustained ejector filled camelback, fantastic dive loop with crazy laterals and good airtime, with intense valleys in between. The next section start strong with a really good stengel dive that provides a great combination of sideways airtime and laterals but than the speed hill and giant camelback just didn't do anything. Same goes for the overbank that was kinda forceless but atleast it kept the speed pretty well. The finale is really strong thankfully. It starts with a strong speed hill, another stengel dive and some very fun and forceful twist and turns. The last camelback is pure ejector and the jump into the brakes provides another strong dose of airtime. Only cons of this coaster is the terrible rattle it has in the last few rows, especially if you sit in the outer seats. This rattle seems to be worse in one the trains. The queue line design is atrocious.

Hyperion surprised me - I honestly assumed that Zadra would be my favourite but this mega gave me something to think about. 

Back gives you an insane whip over the hills and the element of surprise - however the front gives you some bonkers ejectors. The first drop is incredible, and the ejection out of the initial camelback is insane. Feels ridiculously fast (because it is). Pure magic.

Not a single rattle in my experience, though the operators do have a tendency to pin you a bit.

Rode it twice on separate trains this week and experienced no discomfort or rattle -- just a pure airtime machine with incredible pacing and forces. Highly recommend back left outside seat for ejector airtime on the first drop and camel back, plus incredible whip on the dive loop.

Don't let anyone tell you otherwise, this machine is a beast. The first 3 elements alone justify it as one of the best clearly, especially that amazing snappy dive loop!
There is nonetheless a little rattle when at the back of the train and on the side. I also got a bit disappointed by the middle section of the coaster that doesn't really keep up with the remarkable start and amazing end of it (though it is important to mention I rode it on an empty snowy day so it might have impacted my experience. This is subject to change in the future).
Best hypercoaster I've ridden!

This beast feels like a giga but somehow isn't. The first drop is absolute insanity, it just feels like you're diving forever. The following cammelback has you hugging the restraint the whole time while it delivers some of the best sustained ejector ever. Then the coaster whips you through a dive loop at a stupid speed. I could describe this ride forever as I have rode it an insane amount of times. This coaster is super addicting and one of the most re-rideable coaster on this planet. Everything about this ride is perfect and I beg Intamin to build more hyper/giga coasters like this one because this is a MASTERPIECE !!!

First drop is amazing but after that in my opinion coaster feels kinda repetitive, location in other hand is GREAT because after you enter the park you say "something small for warm-up" then you turn right and go to the Hyperion
I really had fun riding Hyperion and it's a great coaster, but the second part of this ride is a bit too little extreme and just kinda dissapointing.
I didn’t enjoy it as much as some people do but still loved it!
Perfect ride and I’m disgusted to see hyperia is above it

Amazing hyper coaster. That first drop feels to last forever then it goes straight into that first airtime hill which gives so much ejector the dive loop is super whippy especially on the outside left seat. Then the little bunny hop gives ejector and the camelback gives floater. After that the low to the ground elements are super fast and whippy. 
Despite being such a good ride the theming is absolutely atrocious and the queue line might be worse. Apart from that absolute beauty of a ride.
motherfucker ripped my face's face off <3

Hyperion is an excellent coaster and number 2 to Zadra. The first drop delivers amazing airtime in the front and the ride is really snappy in the back (especially through the dive loop). It's well themed too. The final airtime hill is really strong as well. The layout close to the ground has some dead spots but nothing major.

Hyperion is one of the best hypercoasters. The ride begins with the massive drop into the tunnel, one of the scariest drops itw. Then it goes into a tunnel and proceeds to go up a camelback, that section is soo INTENSE, that i always greyed out. It absolutely flies over that camelback and u get mental ejector airtime. Then u enter the diveloop, an inversion on such a tall coaster. This element has so much whip(everywhere on the train) and it features some incredible headchoppers on the descend. Now it whips u to the left, where u stay sideways, which is cool. The next two elements were a bit dissapointing, i mean the small hill and the big floater hill, sounds great, but the big hill delieveres NO airtime, its too drawn out and the restrains kill it. Then it proceeds to go into an overbank, where u get nice hangtime. Then it goes into a very good ejector pop and into a wave turn, which is very agressive(u get whipped to the side like crazy and there is also an unexpected headchopper), now u just have some twist and turns before u go into the last airtime hill, which is really special, for me the 2nd best element on the ride, very good sustained ejector. The layout is very intense and agressive, so the restraints are very tight on ur body , which kinda ruins the ride a bit. I tought the rattle was not that bad and overall its a very good ride
This was insane, the sense of speed is unmatched. And the airtime was great!

Holy airtime. This ride is an absolute airtime machine, with a multitude of outrageous ejector moments. I only rode it once, but I rode it in the best seat possible (back left inside) and it was somehow even more intense than Zadra. The ride isn’t super smooth, but—at least on the inside seat—it didn’t bother me that much (although I did lean forward most of the ride so it didn’t rattle my skull out). The station is also really cool, but, like most of the park’s rides, it is a realllllly long walk to the station. Overall, this is neck-and-neck with Zadra for the best ride in the park for me.

The first three elements are world class - the enormous first drop into the tunnel is mental, the camelback offers excellent airtime and the dive loop is also great fun. HOWEVER, after this section, the ride kind of falls flat: there is plenty of speed, but the coaster seems not to know what to do with it. There are some hills offering little to no airtime (the little speed bump does literally nothing, it is way too drawn out) and the twister section meanders around aimlessly losing momentum very quickly. The finale ist fine, but nothing more than a gimmick. 
The outer seats are indeed quite rattly, on the inner seats, the ride is a little rough, but nothing too bad - so try to sit on the latter if you are sensitive to roughness.
One major downside is the ridiculously long queue which seems more like a parking garage with very little theming and some light effects, especially on empty days with multiple rides this long way can get quite annoying. 
To sum things up, this coaster is not bad per se, but it does not live up to its expectation by its reputation and appearance - at Energylandia, I prefer Zadra, Abyssus, Formula and even Mayan to Hyperion.
The drop was mental and so was the ejector hill but in my opinion it’s very overrated
First drop is incredible, dive loop is amazing and back row whips through the ending so well. Absolutely incredible ride

Hyperion is tall and intense but there is a bad rattle in the wing seats. The two hills after the dive loop are dull. Having to put all of your stuff in lockers at the start of the queue was very annoying. Best part is the first drop.
Very good ride great ejector on the first drop and the first airtime hill
Lots of fun and the rattle isn't very noticeable. Very forceful and long layout.
Overall, it's a nice ride, but I still prefer the Energylandia formula.
full 3 seconds of blacking out baybeeeeeeee

Fantastic view in the 1st row during the drop, feels like you're gonna dive into the lake.
For the size ride is quite intense - expect greyouts on hotter days. 
Queue is non existent even in peak summer, you can ride it on repeat. And season pass is like 50eur, definitely worth if you're a local.
amazing coaster but very intense especialy as well as super smooth in the back but rattely in the midddle a nice to ride coaster but after 5 rides i needed a break.
Lech is such an amazing ride the back row drop is mental and the intensity is in like anything I’ve been on maybe I think but the airtimes great
Pound for pound one of the most intense coasters in the world. This Vekoma Bermudian Blitz packs a massive punch into a small space, with a drop that plunges directly into a lake-side tunnel.
Lech Coaster is incredible. It has very strong airtimes, the first drop feels like Kondaa with vests. It's the most intense Vekoma I've ridden. It would be great if it were longer but it's great.

Incredibly underrated, absolutely phenomanal ride. Short queues, good operations, comfortable restraints, the perfect balance of a perfect drop, great inversions, intensity and airtime. I will never forget this ride. also breathtaking views from the top of the lift hill, and great theming. The pacing of this coaster is perfect too, it really packs a punch, you never know where its going next. I don't know if this is my favourite coaster ever, or zadra, both are amazing. Yes, Legendia isnt the best park and its better to go to Energylandia, but its so worth it going for this coaster especially because it's walk on most of the time so you can go multiple times in a row. Absolutely amazing.

I wasn't sure beforehand if I was going to like Lech Coaster as the reviews painted it as extremely heavy on the positive Gs. While it does deliver on that aspect, the ride is also glass-smooth which makes it very re-ridable. I liked both the front and the back but the drop is certainly something you'd like to experience in the rear most of the time. 
Apart from the positive forces - greyouts are pretty much a guarantee - Lech also delivers on the other end of the spectrum. The airtime is surprisingly strong despite the vest restraints. They're not too bad but lap-bar only would have been even better, I think. In any case, I think Lech is the full package. I enjoyed every second of it and found myself entering the queue for "just one more ride" more often than I'd like to admit. Brilliant coaster.

Absolutely Epic Ride! Great theming, great 1st drop, love the barrel roll through the station, unbelievable views and basically no queues. Also Re-rides are allowed. Managed 8 rides on the coaster and 6 in a row. Rode it in the day and dark and its fantastic.

Amazingly intense and fast ride. The drop is fantastic and so whippy. After that you're either glued into your seat or flung into the restraint, pretty much no in between. it doesn't seem to lose any speed. I also appreciate Legendia sending out nearly empty trains and not keeping you waiting.

One of the best Coaster out there,intese ,with a Great layout and some Crazy inversions.
The pace in Unreal and you don't have a single second when the Speed decrease

I didn't expect it to be this good, people say it's almost too intense but it's not, yeah it's very intense and I grayed out but not even a bit of a headache. The layout is fun and the drop is awesome, it's pretty long too. After 10 rides, I must say I left a bit nauseous, but it was worth it

Even though it is a smaller coaster in the grand scheme of things, the power this thing has packed into it is insane. Lech Coaster is easily the most intense Vekoma coaster I have done and it is up there as one of the more intense rides I have done. It has that wonderfully engineered Vekoma element flow but the forces are cranked way up. The positive forces are sustained and strong and the airtime is all ejector airtime. All while being a glass smooth experience in a comfortable train.

This rides setting is great being mostly situated over the central lake of the park. It can be seen from anywhere in the park and it looks very nice. Walking into the ride’s plaza the pathways go right under the ride and there is a good amount of theming here. It is a mostly medieval aesthetic that is unfortunately an unrealized vision. In the queue line there is a pre-show room that appears it has not been used in some time. All of the equipment for it is still there but it is currently just a dark room people walk through. The loading platform is great with surprisingly good airflow and the first roll going directly overhead. 

Across all of my rides I found that the back row was the best row on this coaster for the sole purpose of the first drop. It is an intense first drop delivering powerful airtime while twisting quickly to the right giving a strong whip at the same time. It then slams into high positive forces as it threads a tunnel and goes into an oddly shaped dive loop. The way it is designed is like an inclined dive loop except it fully inverts and at the apex becomes the exit of an overbanked turn, it is bizarre. The results are an element that holds a strong positive force for an extended period of time. In most rides at the exit of the dive loop I was greying out and that greyout lasted until after the next element. That being an whippy s-hill that gives ejector airtime while rapidly rotating to the left. An airtime hill follows giving another powerful pop of airtime and it levels out quickly to enter the roll through the station. The shaping of the roll is extremely smooth and halfway through pitches downward into a drop. The train then soars through a tight over banked turn that leads into a tight banked turn around the front of the station under the transfer track this entire time the ride is pulling good force and it concludes with a sudden pop of ejector airtime in the s-hill. The best part of layout flow then follows with a quick corkscrew that turns directly into a small overbanked turn. The outerbank hill that follows is a bit of a dead spot and the helix afterward is not as intense, however the ride ends with one more pop of ejector airtime in the final hill before turning and climbing into the brakes.

The pacing of this ride is amazing how well it keeps up its intensity while navigating the perfectly designed twists and turns of the track. It does have its short comings with the theme being greatly reduced. While I would love to see the theming be used again, that does not change how I feel about this fantastic coaster.
I never blacked out on a coaster as hard as I did on this one.
x8
It is worth the visit to the Legendia park, this coaster is the best variant, layout and overall impression of Vekoma coasters. The hype is strong and it delivers.

A really fun coaster, super smooth with a great first drop and a fun layout. I did feel that it lost some pace towards the end of the ride. The other negative for me is that this ride is SO much better at the back compared to anywhere else in the train which leads to some inconsistency depending on where you end up sitting.

Most intense coaster i've ever been on. The first drop in the back is crazy, intense ejector airtime mixed with laterals. The valley and the entirety of the sidewinder is a sustained greyout moment. The S-hill and camelback provide two strong ejector moments which are extra powerful if you are coming back from an intense greyout. Corkscrew through the station is very snappy, overbank and the turn after are two other heavy-positives maneuvres. Small camelback has some strong ejector and the second corkscrew is as snappy as the first one. The ending of the layout is a mix of intense turns and sudden change of directions mixed with airtime. As with every new gen Vekoma, it's glass smooth and the trains are super confortable. Too bad it's not lap bar only but at least the vest is not very tight. I'm still deciding if I like better this or Hyperion for the 2nd best coaster in Poland.
Some good airtime and forces on this ride. Only thing stopping this going higher stars for me is the dead spots in certain sections

The first 3/4 of the layout is filled with intense inversions (grayed out a few times) and excellent airtimes.  But the last 1/4 lacks similar fun elements, and the ride basically peters out.  A stronger finish would be nice.  Overall, though, it's a smooth and intense ride.  It's a great coaster for this small family park, which is less than an hour's drive from Energylandia.  Glad I made the drive!

If it wasn’t for Zadra, this would be the best coaster in Poland. To be honest, I expected it to be more intense according to the reviews but still it delivered in every aspect. I don’t know why everyone always only talks about the positive G’s when this has the overall package of everything, including great and surprising airtime, inversions and laterals. And the drop in the back row will change your life, my favorite drop so far on any coaster. Plus you can just marathon it when you are at Legendia because it usually has no queue.

A perfect ride. Every hill delivers spectacular airtime (apart from that outerbank, which honestly is a nice break from the action). Every valley delivers bone crushing G's, that drop is one of the best I've ever done. Every transition feels natural, every inversion purposeful. I just wish it was a little bit less intense so I wouldn't get so dehydrated during the day. Absolutely a 10/10 ride, and worth the visit to Poland for alone.
amazing coaster, def a top 2 in poland (1st zadra then this). this has amazing airtime and i love it so much
great ride but don't be a hater just because you think you look cool
Don't play. You're here the same reason I'm here. Steel Vengeance is the best damn coaster in the world and it's not a question.
perfect. dont come and ride it thinking its gonna be the number 1 coaster in the world and just ride it for what it is

Here's the deal. This thing is like EVERYone's favorite/top coaster. It's hyped to death. So you have to ask yourself, is there a reason for that? I visited CP for the first time with the goal of making Steel Vegeance the 100th coaster I've ridden this year so far. My very first ride was in the back row at night. And let me just say this. This is IT. You have arrived. This is an RMC masterpiece. It's long, it's fast, it keeps you guessing, and it constantly tries to yeet you out of your seat. Half this thing is inside its own structure. Because of that (especially at night), you have no clue what's coming next. Oh, a barrel roll? Great, I'll just lean into it. SNAP. We're going the other direction. It's full of little tricks like that. I was really worried about this being overhyped for me. I am quite happy to say that the worry was unfounded.
10/10 coaster, no notes. I went in with very high expectations and they were somehow exceeded. Just thinking about that one back row ride I got makes me happy.
I mean its steel vengence lol, anyone calling this overrated is just trying to be different, best coaster in the world.

Steel Vengeance is the best coaster in the world… don’t say Iron Gwazi is better. Everyone hypes it up as the best ride ever and I got off so mad and disappointed. I got on Steel Vengeance with high expectations and it went over my expectations. That is what I want out of a coaster if it is number 2 on the whole freaking planet

Wow. Just wow. This is THE best rollercoaster in the world, the magnum opus of RMC, this ride has ZERO flaws, from the first drop to the breaks, you are constantly floating while going through the best turns in the world, the amazing pace with nowhere to hang on is an amazing feeling, every element is insane.

I got 7 rides on SteVe, all of them were amazing.  This is a very smooth ride and is also pretty intense. The layout is also full of airtime, the first drop is great, the inversions are good, and much more. This is worth the trip to Cedar Point
This ride is an absolute masterpiece. From the 90-degree drop to the insane airtime, this ride has everything you could ever want. If I could, I would rate this 6 stars.

I usually smile throughout rides on coasters, but there was so much joy I couldn't keep from laughing out loud! I've ridden it about ten times and it is my favorite of the 100+ coasters I've ridden around the world.
