Steel Vengeance is a truly amazing coaster, but it doesn't quite live up to the hype for me.  I love everything about it.  The first drop is amazing, the inversions are great, and there is so much airtime, but in general I tend to like more graceful, sustained airtime instead of the quick ejector pops Steel Vengeance focuses on.  In that way, I actually consider Twisted Timbers to be superior.  As with all RMCs, it is impeccably smooth but the trains are quite uncomfortable for people with legs as long as mine.  It doesn't rise to the point of pain, but it does detract from the experience.  The lift hill is also painfully loud and I must plug my ears in order to avoid getting a headache.

Ride this at least once every time I go! This is a must ride as the airtime is strong and takes your breath away every time. The first time I rode this it drew tears due to the intensity and I also left the platform shaking. Very smooth with powerful first half, specifically the first drop, the top hat, and the overbank. The inversions in the second half are also extremely trippy!

I don't really like the statement "I don't know what to say that hasn't already been said." To me, it feels like a cop-out, a maneuver when one is stuck in a rut and doesn't know how to add to the discourse of an already critically acclaimed thing. My advice is: try and write about it anyways! You won't ever be able to add to a conversation if you don't at least start somewhere. Besides, even if the content is not new, the form can still be strung together in a novel way. Anyways, this is basically a very long way of me saying I'm not sure how to review this behemoth. There have already been people who have gone through this ride element-by-element in a more thorough way than I possibly can with my mere three rides, and I'm not sure if I have any enlightening things to say about this coaster's place in the industry or RMC's history. Except, maybe, that they really opened themselves up to the challenge of making a longer, ambitious coaster, which led to stupendous results. 

But you know what, I'm going to try, at least briefly. You know you're in for a treat when the pre-lift section has airtime. And after that notoriously loud chain lift is a breath-taking first drop that manages to both be long and whippy. The speed hill is a fun pop, but following two hills are some of the greatest elements on any coaster ever. Both give ejector the duration of a B&M Hyper Camelback, and the outward bank of the second threatens to throw you out of your seat at the same time. The Zero-G Roll - Wave Turn - Zero-G Stall turnaround is both photogenic and creative, as it dishes up a variety of sensation in such a short time. The drop off the mid-course is the sort of thing that even looks like it'll give ejector, and from there you are taken into the Kingdom of Wood. The elements after that drop may not be as strong or memorable, but the unique location within the structure of the coaster itself more than makes up for it. That and the breakneck pacing. Finally, the six airtime moments back-to-back is exactly the thunderous finale this beast of a ride needed.

Though Steel Vengeance is a masterpiece, I don't see enough people talk about how annoying its queue is. Originally, I was going to go on a long rant about how the lockers, metal detectors, and inevitable wanding are all frustrating in their own specific ways, but I realized it was too negative for something this good. Regardless, it has made me less enthusiastic to reride it in the past compared to the minimal precautions for something like Magnum, for instance, but I always seemed to find my way on it again simply due to its quality.

I loved Mean Streak, but this became my instant #1 after my first ride.  It's got a fantastic first drop, length of the ride is phenomenal with quite possibly the best pacing I've ever experienced on a coaster.  All of the inversions are great, every element feels intentional and impactful.  There's nothing negative I can say about this one.  It's amazing.

After being wowed by Wildcat and Wicked Cyclone I was excited for holy grail, but was a bit disappointed.  

Arguably, it's more extreme; all the numbers are bigger, but it seems like the speed doesn't allow it to do as much as it could.  No super tight turns or little flings, it just rushes around in a circle two or three times at high speed.  

The trademark RMC ejectors are there still, but almost too sharp, they stop being thrilling and just feel like it's yanking you down, and the inversions feel a bit uninspired

They should have used all the speed it gathers from that first drop do you another circuit around the outside or something first to burn off more speed with larger RMC features, and then used all that empty area in the middle and underneath to have more fun being creative with a bit lower speed

Holy smokes, by far my #1! I don't want to just follow the basic enthusiast opinion, but it's just undeniable how great this ride is. Before coming to Cedar Point, I was worried I might not think this was the best coaster in the park and think it was overrated. My worries were reconciled as soon as we went down that 90-degree drop. H O L Y CRAP! My favorite drop on any coaster that I've done up to this point. The 90-degree drop sensation on a smooth 200-foot hypercoaster is just insane! The first camelback and outer bank are wild. We need more large-scale moments on RMCs like these moments! The outer bank ejects you out of your seat sideways to the left just before you are absolutely yanked back to the right at the bottom of the element. Just insane! The two inversions following in the first half are just great. This stinking stall is wild, and I can't believe no one is talking about it more. It's not the longest stall from a hang time standpoint, but you're literally heading in a downward trajectory. You're gaining speed while in the stall, which is an insane sensation. The second half of the ride is a jumbled mess of goodness, with two of my favorite airtime moments coming right out of the break run. The final bunny hills at the end are fun but not my favorite, and I think they are probably where this ride gets its reputation for being repetitive. The quick ejector pops on RMCs have historically never been my favorite (same case with Twisted Timbers), especially in the front, but they are still a fun time. I kind of just wish the lap bars were a little less painful (wish they could have restraints more like B&M clamshells or Intamin restraints on Velocicoaster), but oh well, that's being picky. This ride is perfect! Ride in the front and back!
Most. Overrated. Coaster. Ever. The length and the excessive airtime paired with the RMC restraints makes the ride incredibly uncomfortable.

Phenomenal ride - undeniably impressive in many ways especially how it covers so much track with no wasted motion. But in turn I always feel the guiding hand of the designer every time I ride Steel Vengeance. If we're splitting hairs debating the best coasters in the world I'd lean more towards the ones that feel like they're getting away with something.

First time I had the chance to go to cedar point and was trying to get through every ride in a single day. Most of the other coasters had a response of “that was fun, onto the next one.” A few made me say “Wow, that was amazing. I’ll definitely do this again later.” Steel vengeance, on the other hand, basically forced me to ride it two more times immediately after to feel all the positions in the train. I’ve never been more certain about placing a coaster at my #1 spot.

What a freaking beast, after having ridden different RMC coasters around the world and you would think it can't get more nuts - yes it can! 

What stands out is the vast amount of unique inversions in different directions and mostly in the massive construction. Combined with the ridicilous amount of bunny hops you will be thrown around like a ragdoll while laughing like a maniac. My nr.1 for sure!
My favorite coaster! This is 100% the best ride at Cedar Point! It just so awesome
I have no words. I waited 60 minutes, and wouldn't have minded waiting triple that for this ride. Total work of art.
Makes the argument that rollercoasters can be works of art.

About as perfect as a coaster can get. Ride operations are always fast (there were dispatching every 45 seconds one time) and its always an amazing ride. Home park so I've ridden it a ton and it never disappoints!
No inversions so unfortunately flying cobras clears

It’s got everything you want in a coaster, except maybe discovering a thousand bucks sitting in the seat when you’re buckling in.  The speed is there, the elements are there and it’s got the layout/duration to match.  Classic.
AlpenFury is the better fury
Fury is a freaking masterpiece. It’s everything you want out of a coaster. My advice is to ride in the front seat.

B&M's magnum opus. It's their best coaster and it's not even close. THIS is the perfect layout for a Giga: excellent first drop, keeps its lightning fast speed, stays low to the ground, forceful turnarounds, and enough airtime to please everyone. With B&M's perfect restraints and glass smooth track and train? C'mon man. Perfect. Sits safely in my top 5 for now.

This ride is the most overrated coaster I’ve done. There’s no hint of ejector on it and the rest of the forces aren’t too strong either. I love the sense of speed but that’s all that I wasn’t disappointed by

HOLY SH*T. Easily my #1 coaster. Just ride it and you'll understand, but you essentially feel like a bullet and are passing through these banked turns at ludicrous speed. Even after that, you're not done and this thing throws some great floater airtime at you. Golden Ticket Award's Best Steel Coaster for 7 years straight now. An experience like no other.

B&M’s best ride ever, Fury delivers nonstop pacing and an unrivaled sense of speed. Save for Steel Vengeance, this is the best coaster I have ever ridden, and there are effectively no cons to Fury. Front row at night is almost the best ride I’ve had on any coaster.

We rode Fury 325 10 times during our December 2025 visit to Carowinds; 2 at the beginning of the day (in the back) and 8 times at the end after the ride suffered a long maintenance delay from the early afternoon to evening. Why? Because it's incredibly re-rideable and if you travel all the way to Charlotte to ride the tallest roller coaster with a chainlift, you ride said tallest roller coaster in the world with a chainlift. The first drop is great of course, but that treble clef turn-around is ASTOUNDING. I read some folks on here calling Fury 325 overrated - and to each their own - but there's something genuinely amazing about this engineering marvel at such an unsuspecting regional park. If Carowinds was my home park, I'd be there weekly to mount this B&M beast. 

Unbeknownst to us, Fury has an incredibly dedicated fanbase of marathon-riders. Several people in the queue with us had tens of thousands of rides alone!
Overrated

Incredible Roller Coaster. Absolutely FLIES through its layout with the comfortable B&M restraints/trains, quick dispatch times, and awesome ops that let us ride twice without getting off at the end of the night. Great Giga coaster. Must ride if at Carowinds.

Fury 325 lives up to all the hype.  It's a masterpiece that definitely competes with the best of them.  It's like taking the best parts of B&M hypercoasters and adding even more awesome elements.  The shining star of this ride is the treble clef and dive into the trench below the park's entrance.  In addition, it's super smooth just like any B&M.  Just ride it.  Easily a top 5 coaster for any enthusiast.
Drop feels like forever, excellent forces, beautiful ride.

So I rode this three times once in the middle once in the back and once in the front I like the front best now this coaster is a beast it was my favorite for a while until I rode wildcats revenge. This coaster is amazing it’s so comfy, has great layout and is so fun the only thing I don’t like about it is its theming I’m scared of bees wasps and hornets lol
Very long and full of a mix of ejector and floater airtime with a short wait.

Truly a legendary ride. Probably my most ridden coaster outside of the Incredible Hulk at Islands of Adventure. This ride just has a presence, being located right at the front entrance of Carowinds. It weaves over and under guests as they walk up, which was just a genius idea. The first drop is incredible. I still remember my first time riding in 2016 when I had experienced nothing like it. It quickly became my #1 and introduced me into the idea of having a favorite coaster. Although the ride is now my #3 (behind Steel Vengeance and Velocicoaster), I still just have an absolute blast every time I ride. The laterals are insane, sense of speed is phenomenal, ride is super smooth, and the layout just works really well. The one caveat I will mention for new riders: don't go in expecting this to ride like a B&M Hyper with non-stop floater airtime or you may end up mildly disappointed. There is airtime on the 3 hills at the end, but the focus of this ride is the first drop, speed, and laterals. Only thing I could nitpick is that the helix isn't super intense and not on par with the rest of the ride. I wish it had been a little bit more tightly profiled, but again, that's nitpicking. Plus, there's a head chopper on the helix! Anyway, I've blabbed too much. Fury 325 is an absolute masterclass!
The best way to describe that first half is like riding a rocket. It's fast and intense, putting the other B&M gigas to shame. The second half lets up but does have three really good airtime hills.
Most overrated over hyped coaster ever. Not even top 10 giga/strata. Wouldn't crack my top 50.

What an incredible ride. The first drop really sets the pace for the ride. This thing keeps up, even coming back to life after the break run with some great airtime moments. And it's smooth as butter throughout. It's absolutely worth going to Carowinds even if you only ride Fury 325.

Fury 325 is incredible! This is the 3rd giga coaster I've experienced, and while I thoroughly enjoyed it, I walked away with the opinion that it was sliiiiiightly overrated. The first half deserves all the praise and more, its genuinely ioncredible, but the second half has two big duds in the tall banked turn and the helix. The airtime hills are extremely strong, but for whatever reason, those two dead spots really kill the pacing.

Not sure it was just the day I went but definitely has a noticeable dead spot. I think it was after hill with the trim break but it really slowed down pace wise for a bit, but picked up for the last hill to give one nice last airtime pop. 
Despite this, it’s still world class. Amazing first drop and speed in the first half, some strong airtime moments, tunnel is fun. I’m rounding up to 10 from a 9.5. Gotta take a half point off for the weird pacing near the end of the ride.
Wow just wow

What an awesome all around experience. Sitting on that lift hill with only a lap bar must be one of the most scary things one can experience on a coaster. A masterpiece from Gerstlauer that i hope they can top some day.

Man this ride is so well themed. Such a fun experience. There is two surprises on this ride I will not spoil, and I highly recommend to not watch POVs of this ride before you get on it. This ride is definitely up there with some of the best rides I have done.
Insane ride, truly the only coaster like this. Does have a slight rattle, but it can be looked past for the insanity and creativity.
Great coaster, with surprises maybee a little rough, but you wont realy notice that. Overall a masterpiece by gerstlauer.
Best soundtrack and Great intensity. Crazy good theming! Love it

Insane ride with insane elements, such as the non-inverting sea serpent roll, the secret heartline roll and the reverse drop on the vertical lift hill. Which has to be one of the most well kept secrets ever. But the ride itself is a masterpiece. The twisted beyond-vertical drop and the low-to-the-ground turns make for a really intense ride experience, and the rattle makes it even more intense. The ride has three main airtime moments, the first drop, the airtime hill in the middle of the ride and the pop-up into the "final breakrun." Not many airtime moments, but you ride Kärnan for the insanity not for airtime. I got three rides in on Kärnan, all in pitch black darkness in row 3, row 4 and row 1.
One of the only coasters I'm a bit scared of everytime before I ride. The last time I rode it sadly had a slight rattle. Still Awesome!
Wow. At first I was scared of riding, but after riding it, I felt so good. The Airtime is AMAZING, The reverse freefall is quite The nice sensation and overall, the best coaster i've ever ridden

this coaster has always been on an higher postion in my wish list and i finally rode it
this coaster has a stunning theme,specially in the queque and in the station.
the coaster also is wonderful to see from the outside and it's very massive.
i took a lot of pictures and the best just became my new screensaver.
what about the ride...what happen in the tower is crazy and unique,but even though i thought to know everything about this ride i was wrong...there are a lot of surprise.
the heart of the ride,that is the "visible" part of the ride is very intense,with a lot of ejector and great force
but i have ti admit,despite i loved this coaster that there are too many rattle,specially on the central part.
i don't hate the rattle,but specially in the exterior seat there were quite a lot of rattle.
this is a very good coaster though,and you have to ride it just only for the "surprise"

One of the things I love the most in coasters are surprises, and this ride, just like Novgorod, is full of surprises! And it was way better than I expected, in the morning the intensity was very high but not uncomfortable, as well as the rattle, that was there but nothing to worry about. I can't say the same about my late afternoon ride, that was way more intense and way more shaky. But for real, I didn't expect to enjoy it this much. Also the drop is absolutely amazing! And I didn't even mention the theming, absolutely world class. This was also a special ride for two reasons: my #200 coaster and my very first ride on which I had an evacuation in my life :O

Perfect immersive experience. That the surprise element in the tower hasn't killed anybody so far is a miracle, it makes your heart stop when you don't know it will happen. First drop and airtime are insane. Rattle is nasty in places, but hey, it's a Gerst.

This rollercoaster is absolutely amazing.

The theming in the queue as well as during the ride is spot on as always at Hansa Park. The entire section in the tower is uniquely awesome and the drop to the outside is very intense and always fun.

There are two very strong ejector airtimes on the ride - I absolutely love those. After the second one the ride sadly loses much of its pace and intensity.

The other real con I have to give to the ride is its capacity. Due to the tower section the ride only manages to dispatch very few trains. Gladly the queue usually takes around 45 minutes so it is bearable to wait.

Overall "Der Schwur des Kärnan" is an excellent coaster with lots of pace and intensity as well as world class theming.
This has all the elements to be world class but the execution as far as the super rough ride and also the elements themselves don’t really provide interesting forces makes it a disappointment.
An unique and absolute masterpiece
this freak is so insanely intense it's unbelievable! PLEASE MORE GERSTLAUER HYPERS PLEASE PLEASE!!!

Probably my favorite theme and overall experience on a coaster. The que experience is super immersive and everything that happens on ride inside the tower is truly unique. The ride is quite well paced and features some good airtime and wild laterals. It is a bit rough at points and the lap bar tends to come down hard despite my best efforts. The ending portion of the layout is pretty useless too. Excellent, but not perfect.
Crazy ride I did find the restraint uncomfortable on my face overall a masterpiece and my favourite ride.

Fantastic coaster! It has probably the best laterals forces i've ever felt. Airtime in great too. Too bad i've never got to experience a back row ride on this, i've had in total 5 rides, 3 in the very front and 2 in the 2nd row. I think the drop in the back row could be legendary.
There is a rattle throughout the coaster, mainly during the lowest sections of the ride, but it didn't cause me discomfort.

Loses half a star for mandated removal of glasses with straps. Has the bones to be an excellent ride, and the surprise in the tower is by far my favourite part of the ride, but it's very obvious why the manufacturer never built something this tall or fast ever again, because it tracks terribly especially in an edge seat - enough for me to refuse an edge seat entirely. The layout has a lot of "waiting for something to happen", and the big element at the start, while an incredible-looking part of the ride, is a pretty major nothing-burger to experience. The low parts and the sense of speed is great and has some solid moments of airtime, and is EXTREMELY intense, but the layout could still do with some improvement.

What an odd ride this is. Such a cool lifthill and drop but damn does it have a bad rattle. I don't mind a Mack rattle but this is really bad. It takes away A lot from the ride experience. The pacing is out of this world wich makes the rattle even worse. The lay-out is great and it does have some good air. I hope the park will improve the capacity cause 1 train every 3 minutes is something you need to fix with a full queue. (Sidenote: it smells like popcorn in the station.)
I bow before this masterpiece.
It was great

Amazing theme and first drop in the back row. Very intense. The turns feel like Furius Baco light not as bouncy as that but not boring and glass smooth either. Awesome lateral snaps through and three really great camelbacks..The double non inverting thing in the beginning after the drop has violent lateral ejector entering it in the front left side. Small dead spot before the final breaks nothing that ruins the ride though

This is a fascinating coaster. The theming for this ride is incredible, on-par with Phantasialand. There are a lot of spoilers that I won't reveal but the coaster itself is intense and unfortunately has a rattle. I would consider it top 5 worthy if it were smoother.

Chaotically fun, Time Traveller dunks you down a 100 foot drop immediately out of the station. Following that, there’s a fury of airtime, snaps, and hangtime-filled inversions. Unlike the competitor for SDC’s first place, Time Traveler doesn’t really have any cons, so that’s nice.
Love the drop right out of the station. Love the zero-g roll. Overall, this is a tamer experience than Ride to Happiness, but still a blast and probably my favorite ride in the park.
this thing is so good that i don't even care about the fact that the launch has barely any kick to it lol

this ride is nothing like i’ve ever experienced, the spinning, lanches, airtime, it’s relentless and calming at the same time, fast but gives awesome hang time, i wish it was a tiny bit longer tho, the second launch feels a little pointless

Mack really hit the bullseye with this one in terms of a fairly high thrill coaster that is also very broadly appealing - it's no surprise Time Traveler is the most popular coaster in the park. I'd give this 4 stars most of the time but if you're fortunate enough to get a back row mostly backwards ride it jumps up a level.
I do not enjoy spinning coasters like this usually and though this is an interesting, large, and unusual example, I still did not enjoy it. I just prefer to look in the direction the track is going.
wish it had more intensity.

Alright. My 3rd fav at SDC and MIGHT make some people mad. Timetraveler. Over all theming is AMAZING and thanks for ac, BUT it was… actually kinda boring and… a bit lame. While sure I’m glad to experience this Mack extreme spinner… it was a HUGE let down. So overall a 7 out of 10
Soooooo much fun!
Most intense drop on any coaster in the back

4 stars only because I'm not a fan of rides that go backwards.  An amazing ride that isn't too intense, but offers a good theme, a layout that is both thrilling and has catch your breath moments, and is small enough to not be intimidating.
An overall great ride, but I was expecting something a tad more intense. Has some great inversions though.

I don't think I've been on anything more re-rideable, and that just goes to show the power of those spinning trains. There's a few elements that stand out, but not all of them hit on the same ride which leads me to keep chasing the best spin possible. Awesome ops, awesome restraints, clocks were vastly overhyped for how simple they are, row 3 is the best.

This ride... is amazing. I genuinely love this so much. My all-time favorite coaster. Better then Outlaw's run, lightning rod, and everything else ive ridden. The spinning is so fun, taking you sideways down the first drop before going around airtime and inversions while not being able to see anything. The ride makes you delightfully dizzy and really does feel like you traveled through time at the ending. Great theming too

This is the greatest spinning coaster in America as of 2026. Spinning through inversions is an experience no other coaster in this country can replicate. The first drop is amazing, and the rest of the layout would already be a strong looper even before you factor in the spinning. I wish it spun a little faster but that certainly wasn’t a significant detractor from an amazing coaster
It could do more on the launches…. But it’s a great ride!

You can never have a normal ride on this because you might go on the drop forwards, backwards, or laterally. Which for every other element has that same aspect. So, the only slight con I could think of is the intensity of the launches. Which isn't surprising because it's mack rides... (edit THE best ride at sdc)
My favorite coaster literally went in not expecting much and the first drop was crazy airtime. I think it was too short tho

This ride has a crazy first drop must ride in the back for wild ejector, great variety of inversions launches are weak but not a major part of the ride for me spinning is fun and didnt make me sick a few pops of airtime top 5 coaster ive been on

Great coaster, but I was a little disappointed. Slowing down for the launch and then the launch not being very intense was a big downside. Very good first drop and inversions. Didn’t spin as much as I expected it to.

It’s really smooth and a ride that always puts a smile on my face. The layout is fun and the spinning aspect is really interesting. Also the theming is amazing. Best coaster in Missouri and that I have ridden at the time of the review.

Overall fantastic ride with so many fantastic, memorable parts and great inversions. My number one before that was Steel Vengeance but this topped it. The only bad things about it is that it often only has one train going, so the lines barely move and the launches are pretty forceless.

Not as good as ride to happiness but we need more of these.

It's biggest issue is that ride to happiness exists.

It needs to be free spinning and more punch in the launch would help.

this was one of the most Revolutionary coasters to open in north America being the first spinning coaster to go upside down in the U.S. and there is a lot of great things to say about this starting with the insane drop out of the station it is so steep and the best part is you don't know what angle you're gonna go down that drop it absolutely destroys the start of Helix at Liseberg while Time Traveler came out in the era where Mack still made weak launches the spinning and energetic first half before the main launch really make you forget that it has a Mack rides launch the inversions have so much hangtime while it's definitely a Family Thrill Coaster compared to Ride To Happiness but call me crazy but something like RTH probably wouldn't be legal in the U.S. we'll have to see what people think of this ride after F&F:HD opens

Apparently I rate Kondaa a bit higher than other people, above Untamed, BGCE, Velocicoaster, etc. I realize the ride has some moments that don't hit as much like the non-inverting cobra roll (henceforth: NICR) and the wave turn, but even those are plenty fun with floater to constrast with the ejector, and don't come anywhere close to counting as dead spots for me. what really gets me on kondaa is the sustained ejector in the first three elements, getting that much ejector sustained is amazing!! and that first drop in particular is absolutely out of this world in the back right. the ending of the ride contrasts the sustained ejector with shorter bursts that all hit and are very very fun! i just think this ride is absolutely fantastic, and well worth the praise

I had the pleasure of riding Kondaa 15 times on my visit to Walibi Belgium. It's an incredible ride that is just so fun from start to finish. It has a great first drop with a twist. Amazing ejector airtime. Some really interesting elements, like the non-inverting cobra roll. Plus, there is the entire entry area and station theming, which is all top-notch. I enjoyed this much more than other Intamins I rode on my trip, like Taron or Hyperion. The re-rideability of Kondaa is what sold it for me. I found the ride to be fantastic in the back row and equally (or maybe even a touch more) amazing in the front row. Different elements shine in both rows. Usually, it's an easy call of whether front or back is better, but Kondaa really surprises you in both.

A really fun airtime machine that maintains its speed throughout.  It's super smooth and very re-rideable.  The layout has such a nice flow to it.  The first airtime hill is great, and the bunny hills at the end deliver one of my favorite finales.  Some people say the non-inverting cobra roll is too tame, but for me it had good intensity.

Kondaa has everything. The surrounding area and entrance/station building look gorgeous and in-theme. The views of the coaster from there are perfect. The drop and first hill are what you want out of a tall coaster like this, before the ride surprises you with the terrifying outside-banked turn on the second hill. The gigantic cobra roll element feels unique, and the second half of the ride is even more forceful than the first.

Kondaa is another masterpiece by Intamin. The first drop is just nice, nothing special considering the height of onily 50 meters. But what follows is where this coaster really shines. It's a relentless sequence of elements including lots of ejector airtime moments that is just a lot of fun. During the whole ride it feels like Kondaa is constantly trying to throw you off. Of course the last row is the preferred seating area,  but  to my surprise also the middle seats deliver a lot of fun and are also recommended. Great ride!

Kondaa is an amazing coaster which is just perfect. The seats are very comfortable with very good restrains. The first drop amazing and is my favourite drop on a coaster because it is not only very steep but also twists to the side. Because of this you have amazing airtime in the back row. The hill afterwards is also perfect and gives amazing airtime, just like the outerbank. The non inverting cobra roll also has great airtime moments. The rest of the layout has so many ejector airtime moments which are all amazing.
Absolutely fantastic coaster, probably the most individual airtime moments on a coaster I’ve ridden and each one is powerful and memorable

Was expecting a pretty solid coaster but this one really took me by suprise! A cracking first drop (especially on the back), some great airtime, surprising positive forces, and good presentation. It really has a presence in the area!

Update 2026: Just rode this in the middle of a heatwave where it kept going down for over-speeding and jesus christ it's insane

This thing is awesome, Especially in the back. That first drop is crazy you can't describe it. It's out of control. It has a little rattle in the non inverting cobra roll but it's not overwhelming. Without a doubt a crazy rollercoaster.

A superb world class rollercoaster that took me by surprise. Insane first drop, crazy ejector airtime throughout and a strong overall layout. I couldn’t get enough of this thing. However,  From riding this in mostly either the back or front row, I notice that the first drop is obviously significantly better on the back, yet the non-inverting cobra roll, which some complain about, is better on the front, as it’s prominently more forceful and notably less rattly than the latter rows. As a worlds first element it’s interesting though, and certainly forceful going into the initial incline on the front. However, other than the incredible large outerbank hill after the initial camelback, I loved the final stretch of this ride, a variety of fun twisty airtime elements that leads into these absolutely insane final bunny hills, with the final one in particular being off-axis, an incredible way to finish the ride, and probably my favourite ending to a rollercoaster. 

I would argue overall it’s a breathtaking front row experience, as the airtime is still insane, and the sense of speed is superb. However, later in the day, this thing was flying on the back row, extremely intense ejector airtime. 

Easily a new top 5 coaster of mine, and I was lucky to get around 10 rides shared between the back and front row on this attraction. Despite some occasional reliability issues.

The more I ride it the more it grows on me. When I first rode it I thought it was good but I wasn't blown away, but I've been twice since and its gotten so much better. The cobra roll, wave turn and trick track double down are kind of forceless but every other element has strong ejector, the first 3 elements being the clear highlight of the ride in my opinion. It just packs in so many elements and is paced so well. Also visually it is beautiful.
Good airtime but some elements are weak and no inversion
This coaster is insane, such an amazing ride. It goes so fast and a great layout with amazing airtime. Really an standout coaster
It's not near the tallest coasters i've ridden, but everything just felt amazing. One of the best i have ever ridden.

While certainly the most intense ride of the park, only using one train does make the wait quite long. The first drop is very steep and left me only being supported by the thigh cushion, but the rest of the layout was really fun to fly through.

No Cons for me, the better and newer version of Expedition Geforce, with the most intense First drop I have ever experienced on a coaster(EG’s drop is softer, but longer).
Best coaster in Walibi Belgium and the second best in the entire Belgium.

You need to ride it!

Awesome, nearly flawless. Delivers on basicly every aspect, has such a unique layout with extreme forces. The ejector airtime and whip on the first drop is so far one of my favorite elements on any coaster. The only con for me is that there was only 1 train operating with a decently long queue but that is understandable. 9.5/10

kondaa is one of the best coasters in the world............. in the back when riding in the front it jut leaves a bit blank and room for more you know??? the duration isnt bad its just that the airtime is not everywhere straight up ejector but i do realy love this ride with all my heart and its easily number 2 in the benelux
Best ride in the world! Goes hard through the whole layout

This ride is excellent, i rate it higher them most people, and its for a good reason. The first drop is amazing and i dont think this coaster has any dead spots. It is an airtime machine the whole way through.
it really does feel like riding a big dragon snake guy c:
Just a very good, fun coaster with a load of airtime. Not quite up there with the absolute best, but doesn’t stop it being thoroughly enjoyable
loved it defenetly rate this above al the other rides in walibi it was verry calm that day i just had a walk on it was realy calm that day
Very nice ride, but gets very boring after riding it a few times. I wish the layout was a bit less boring
For me Kondaa is an epic coaster, filled with speed, airtime, ejector... The frist drop from the back is just insane.
This is the best rollycoasty in the world. My opinion is correct.

Flying coasters are polarising, but as a big fan of Tatsu I was very much looking forward to FD.  This is a far superior coaster.  The first I-don’t-know-what-it-is element is bonkers and the more conventional pretzel loop, whilst not as big as Tatsu’s, is every bit as intense.  The second half of the ride has an excellent helix, a couple of strong heartline rolls and even a bit of airtime.  Anyone who is sceptical of flying coasters needs to take a trip to USJ and be converted.

Although Flying Aces isn’t the advertised standout roller-coaster at Ferrari World, I would say that it easily is the best roller coaster at the park, from both its theming and overall ride experience. The queue is by far the best queue in the park, especially compared to the other roller coasters; it’s not just a series of switchbacks among basic Ferrari theming, it’s an elaborately themed walkthrough of different WWI inspired props and set pieces. Although the main layout itself has basically no theming — as is the case with the other outdoor roller coasters at the park — I really appreciated how immersive and complementary this queue was before you even stepped onto the ride. The ride itself was seriously fantastic, and I’m surprised this ride isn’t talked about more. The layout is packed with plenty of strong airtime moments, often combined with crazy laterals and directional changes, emphasised in elements such as the non-inverting loop. The coaster also has a surprise inversion at the end of the layout which offers some decent hang time, as the coaster loses a lot of its speed towards the end of the course. The main drawbacks of Flying Aces for me are its capacity and reliability. I’ve visited Ferrari World twice: on my first visit in 2022, the ride wasn’t open for the entire day; for my second visit in 2023, the ride was only open in the morning and then closed for the remainder of the day due to ‘technical issues’. Additionally, I believe this coaster only runs one train, and during my visit, dispatches took a long time. While this wasn’t a big issue on my visit as the park was not that busy, I imagine on busier days or days where the ride is actually open all day, it could lead to massive queues. However, looking past these drawbacks, this coaster easily ranks among my best coasters I’ve experienced and is my personal standout at Ferrari World.

My first RMC was a great one, as this is one of the best coasters in the world. Maybe not up there with Toutatis or even Taron for that matter, but it's still incredible. The following speed hill isn't anything special but is still a nice floater airtime moment. The double inversion is awesome. It's more of a floaty element. The next two airtime moments (a normal and an outer banked airtime hill) are sustained ejector airtime moments. The zero-G roll is snappy but nothing special. Black Mamba's roll is more intense. The wave turn is really snappy and the next run of airtime hills offers pops of ejector airtime and the  heartline roll has some great hangtime. The other inversion throws you out of your seat as well. The trains are rather comfortable but the seatbelt can get in the way of the lap bar. Just put it a bit higher up than your lap like the lower section of a car seatbelt and it will not bother you one bit. You can't lower your lap bar yourself, as a staff member will lower it for you. This feels like an unnecessary policy that slows dispatches down, which wasn't helped by the one train operations. Ironically the park's best coasters (Untamed and Goliath) only ran one train, yet the line moved faster than it did with two trains in Japan, so make of that what you will. It also was shut for most of the day, just like Goliath. Both broken down early in the day, and while Untamed reopened around 2PM, Goliath never reopened during the day. What perplexes me is that they ran 2 trains on the torture machine known as Condor, but not on Untamed, which had a 30min queue, while Condor's train often had empty seats.

The best coaster at Walibi Holland and a fantastic creation by RMC. Untamed is a powerhouse of a ride that uses airtime hills to create a relentless ride experience. Every aspect of this ride is meant to be wild, ranging from the ride itself to the “theming.”Appropriately this ride is in the Wilderness section of the park, which is defined by dense foliage throughout the area. While typically I find areas of overgrowth in parks to not look great, it does admittedly work for this coaster.

I would not call this coaster themed, rather stylized with what can only be described as random things. It is unusual but it works surprisingly well and fits perfectly within Walibi Holland. The queue is cool with multiple callbacks to Robin Hood. In the middle there is a section of the former ride intact with an original coaster car positioned on it, which is great to see the park preserve that much of the former coaster to show to guests. Deeper in the queue there are a ton of wooden track pieces from the old ride sticking out of the ground. There are a bunch of “LOVE” signs scattered throughout that I can’t tell what the goal of those are, but what kinda makes it work is how overgrown the queue is. Every theming element looks like nature is trying to reclaim it and it does sell the theme of the ride much better.

In the station the trains look great and it is dispatches with an accompanying drum sequence that perfectly sets the scene for the ride that is to follow. Out of the station the outerbank creates a fun lateral hangtime and goes right into the lift. The drop is a standard RMC drop that gives a good moment of ejector airtime and the speed bump gives another light pop. What follows is an awesome outward banked turn that has an inverting roll going into and out of it. It was not as intense as I had expected, but it was a perfectly held zero-g moment that grew to be one of my favorite parts of the ride. A powerful step up flows into a banked turn to the left and goes into back to back ejector airtime hills, the second being off axis. The turnaround is not as intense as the previous elements, but the flow into the roll and gracefully into the outward bank is satisfying. Going the other way it is full of airtime pops that give strong pops of ejector every time. The “stall” is one of the weaker elements unfortunately, but it at least gives a fun wiggle through the course. A turn leads to the finale with a twisted hill into the structure that feels like it gets stronger as it continues and another quick hill into the roll. This roll is very odd for a RMC, leaning less into flow and more into hangtime as it is angled upward and the train loses some speed. Then it is just one more pop of airtime and then a glide into the brakes.

What Untamed provides is the quintessential RMC experience. It goes all in on providing a wild ride experience with a ton of airtime and dynamic maneuvers while also having its own flair. However there was not a single bad experience I had with this ride and it alone is worth visiting Walibi Holland for.

My favorite roller coaster as of the time of this review. The ride makes a grand first impression when you walk up to it with the entry plaza and the massive sign. The station's theming is impressive and some of the best in the park, and it also plays a cool soundtrack when you dispatch. The ride operators often leave multiple inches of room between your legs and the lap bar (don't worry it's completely safe) and it allows for incredible airtime and hangtime. The turn out of the station is very weird and wacky. It pushes you out of your seat in a way I have never felt before, especially on a prelift section. The drop may be one of the weaker ones on an RMC, but it's still incredible. The speed hill can give a quick pop of floater, and then comes my favorite element on any roller coaster. The double inverting 270 degree stall. This element is genius in every way possible. The inversion going into it gives you some hangtime before you stall out. And this stall out to the side is bent inwards, so the hangtime from the first inversion continues and seamlessly transitions into another type of hangtime, but to the side instead of upside down. And this is all while you have the wooden structure enveloping you on all sides. Then the roll coming out of it feels like a barrel roll downdrop, and continues the hangtime you got in the first half of this element. Just a perfect moment. Then you hit a double up which is probably the weakest part of the ride, but it still delivers two strong pops of airtime and some unexpected laterals. The camelback afterwards delivers violent airtime that is sustained for longer than it feels like it should be considering its power. This is followed by a similar element, but banked to the left on the apex. It's a bizarre feeling to be getting airtime this strong while on your side, but RMC absolutely nailed this element. It's my second favorite part of the ride behind that first inversion. Then comes the turnaround that runs right next to the entry plaza. The entry is a step-up under flip, which gives some nice hangtime, similar to RMC's zero-g rolls. The exit is another outer bank, but instead of delivering sustained ejector it gives sustained floater. After that, you are treated to what seems like an endless barrage of small bunny hops that all send you to the moon. The ride caps off with a perfect low to the ground barrel roll. It feels like you're going to hit the ground with your hand, and the element itself is super drawn out and delivers the strongest hangtime on the ride. It's an amazing way to end an amazing coaster. This ride is really just incredible and it's the best roller coaster I've gotten to experience in my life

The views of Helsinki are awesome and the way the layout interacts with the surrounding rides and terrain are the cherry on the top. Easily top 10 coaster worthy.

What a fantastic coaster, my #1 in Europe beating the Ride to Happiness. It's pacing is perfect, the setting is amazing and because Linnanmäki is open until 22:00 you can get many rides. Operations however can be improved drastically, trains stack basically every time because people keep loose items in their pockets.
The ride was awesome! At the first element ”zero g winder” I knew that this is going to be my favourite ride ever! The ride was so smooth and intense! This ride definitely deserves its spot at top 10

After my first morning ride, I was like - it is so fast! And in the evening on a hot day it was blowing me away all the time! Launches are fantastic, layout is very creative, packed with airtime, positive Gs, hangtime. Taiga is another masterpiece from Intaming. But do not ask me if it is better than Taron. One bad thing that I can say about Taiga is that the first launch aims towards sun setting side and the sun in Finland is very sharp and very slow fading and I was blinded on every evening ride.
The best terrain coaster I've ever done and the best intamin Multi launch coaster. Taiga is an amazingly paced thrill ride wich leaves you breathlkess when you hit the breaks.

Perfection. Not a single inch of track wasted. From start to finish, this is just an insane, insane ride! There's no moment to catch your breath. It is so much faster than the POV makes it out to be. Taiga has it all: great launches, airtime, hangtime, speed, pacing, theming, positives, whip, you name it. This is Intamin's magnum opus right here.

Taiga is an excellent ride with a beautifully designed layout that delivers a wide variety of forces. 

The experience changes a lot depending on where you sit. My first time was in the back row and it felt incredibly intense, with strong positive Gs throughout. 
On my re-ride in the second row, it was a completely different thrill, with less intensity but spectacular moments of floater airtime all over the place. 

What makes Taiga special, in my opinion, is that it manages to be thrilling without ever feeling scary, making it enjoyable for almost anyone. Add to that the breathtaking views and the butter-smooth ride, and it’s truly something remarkable.
It’s big blue and beautiful
Absolute cinema🙌 In all seriousness this is one of the best rollercoasters I've ever ridden
Best coaster in europe I have rode it 26 times this summer My 4th best coaster in the world Behind falcons flight velocicoaster and steel vengeance
The best roller coaster I've ridden so far. Lunches are kidna strong and fast, the inversion at the end is unexpected. Coaster itself is long which is a big plus.

We got a morning lap on back row and it was gooood but not great. First half a bit soft. I heard it warms up in the afternoon. Unfortunately it held a 40 min queue all day so we only did one second lap. Front row at 2040. I heard the back row is best but the first launch blinded by the setting sun, and feeling the flow of each element in the front row row felt like flying. Second launch and top hat excellent. Plenty of ejector airtimes. Absolutely storming. On a par with Velocicoaster, that run. 

Would love to return and lap more times. Really epic. In hindsight I wish I’d paid for some single shot queue jump laps (€11 per time). But only in the afternoon!
Really fun coaster with a really intense and fast paced layout. Really compareable to velocicoaster
10/10 ride, L O V E it!
Definitely the best rollercoaster in Finland.
Absolutely amazing. That's all I can say.

An absolute masterpiece. The zero g winder, stall and final barrel roll all give awesome whip and hangtime, but the layout also has moments with strong positives and amazing ejector. The whole layout also uses the terrain and nearby rides very well to it's advantage.
Perfect
Very good ride
Easily the best coaster in Finland. It has a rattle, but because of the awesome restraints it didn’t take away from the ride experience. On my 2025 and 2026 visits it broke down multiple times.
it was amazing i love this ride so much but after riding it 5 times in a row i stil think toutatis is bether

It's sooo good I'm just waiting to go to it again last year went with my brother.I also went with my class to linnanmaki but I was disabled and they don't let you go to the ride but with my brother I wasn't disabled sorry for my bad english it's my second language

I'm not a fan of hangtime, so the first inversion doesn't do anything for me. From there on the things improve. The first half is still warming up but after the second launch, things get wild. There are some great moments. My favorite part is the sudden drop after the zig zag. The best coaster in Finland.
Extremely good and intense! Perfect launch coaster. God I love the inversions on this thing. The airtime moments hit hard, and the whip, and the turns are so powerful

My new #1, displacing SteVe.   The train whips through the layout, and every seat delivers an outstanding coaster experience.  Great first drop, snappy airtimes and transitions, crazy inversions, and all with butter smoothness.  When I rode the first train of the day, I was a little disappointed.  But man, just an hour later after it warmed up, I was blown away.  By early afternoon on a hot day, this thing was hauling.  LOVE Zadra!  I couldn't get enough of it.
I did this in August 2024 and it was amazing. Definitely my number one. The pacing, the elements , the airtime, it's a perfect ride

Zadra is simply spectacular. It's a great ride in every row but the first drop is best to be experienced in the back. You'll leave your seat for what feels like an eternity before the insanity kicks in. Zadra just hauls through the layout without catching its breath even for a moment. Every element hits while also being smooth as butter. The airtimes are strong, the inversions fun and the signature stall simply outstanding. You'll pass it with so much speed that you'll truly feel weightless, and if you decide to look down at the ground, time seems to stop for a few seconds. There's not a single thing I disliked about Zadra and I could have ridden it all day long without ever getting sick of it. The ibox trains are not the most comfortable, to be honest, but I didn't mind too much. Long story short: This coaster alone is worth the trip to Poland.
Best ride ever did on my life. coming again in June 2025 just for Zadra
Definitely the best roller coaster in Energylandia but sadly have long queues (especially for the firs row) also the location kinda suck because entrance is not that obvious
What a coaster! One of the best!
Absolute masterpiece. My favorite coaster by far, the 0G stall was proablly the best part, but the drops and inversions did not disappoint either.

Zadra is a great coaster in the morning and an absolutely incredible one in the afternoon once it has warmed up. The pacing is relentless, and it has some truly stellar elements and moments throughout. Is Steel Vengeance, Iron Gwazi, or ArieForce One better? Yes. No. Maybe? These are all world-class roller coasters by RMC, and each one caters to a slightly different taste, but all of them could easily be your #1. The only downside to Zadra is that QUEUE. My god, why is it so wide and so long??? I felt lost before I ever got to the station, and on a busy day, it's chaos. BUT I will happily deal with that if it means I get to ride this truly fantastic roller coaster.

This is my number 1 so good, whippy and best pacing on a coaster I get why it's so good. The whole thing there's so much airtime. However my only con is that the restraints are so bulky and it kind of hurts whenever there's bursts of ejector, nonetheless still one of the best in the world and my number 1

It was my first RMC, and I'm definitely hungry for more!

Energylandia is my home park, and I've ridden Zadra around 20 times at this point, in different weather conditions and at various times of the day.

This ride is all about phenomenal pacing, power, and, depending on when you ride it, airtime.

In the mornings or on colder days, Zadra runs much slower, and the airtime moments are very gentle and floaty. The inversions feel much more graceful than snappy. However, when it warms up later in the day and the weather is sunny and warm, it absolutely tears through the layout like a beast, and the airtime is incredible. On the first drop, you get launched right out of your seat!

You also get some beautiful views of the Polish countryside and nearby lakes. The zero-G stall is epic! I love how quickly and snappily the train rotates going into and out of the element. The airtime hill is great as well, although it's not quite as powerful as Hyperion's camelback.

The biggest drawback of this ride is the queue line straight from hell. It is extremely long, which makes reriding Zadra a nightmare.

To sum it up, riding Zadra is a religious experience for me. 10/10, would recommend!
One of the best in Europe and one of the best in the World. That pacing and concistent forces are unmatched.
Absolutely incredible, my number one!!!
Been on this 6 times over 2 days; still not had my fill. 🤩

Stunning ride to look at. Extreme pace. Awesome elements, including the very photgenic first drop and large upside-down stall. Some of the drops diving into the support structure are terrifying. The second part of the ride has even stronger G-forces. All in all a world-class ride. Only a few downsides keep it from a perfect score: The theming is scarce, up to the point of the entrance being difficult to find. The dives into supports remove the sense of the extreme speeds, especially on the huge first drop. And finally, the ride reaches the downward-inclined brake run so fast that it leaves you wanting more.
ZAMN ZADDY!

Best coaster ive riden. Went to energylandia as the first theme park outside of Denmark and it was CRAZY. Nothing ive riden even comes close zadra and even tho i had heard mixed reviews about this ride it was still crazy, the first drop is wild and the stall is way taller then you think when on it and it has some crazy ejectors the only thing bad about it is the lapbars. it was my first RMC and its a hyper.

This is my first RMC, was meant to follow Steal Vengeance from last summer but that didn't happen. I'm not sure what any other RMC might do to beat this for it's first drop, incredible inverted stall and magnificent pacing and intenstity all the way to the break hill. Maybe the multiple airtimes of SV might sway when I get to ride that but the grandeur of the set pieces here are breathtaking. There is no let up whatsoever, from one element to the next, and the one tiny bit of discomfort is from some pulsing up the lift hill! Otherwise a sumblimely smooth and thrilling creation. I visited in April, went straight to the ride at 10am and had five rides within an hour with the re-ride gate open, so can't speak to queues anywhere in the park at this period. Just hope for good weather!

Masterpiece. Zadra is worth that tag. It is not just a powerful hyper coaster with great drop. It's something more. The airtimes are well distributed. Elements appear out of nowhere. The zero-g stall is like a deliberate, intentional, triumphant flex, to the park and to the world. Everything feels thought out, like you are being played with by some master-mind. Well, I guess Alan Schilke is that master-mind.
Great ride no cons expect that I was on a empty day and I had to walk in the empty queue and it took me 5 minutes. Yeah.. that’s all
Perfection. Crazy pacing and every element hits. My #1 coaster

The first drop is a real heart-stopper and the pacing throughout the whole ride is relentless. Despite its extreme layout, it's unbelievably smooth, making every inversion and airtime moment feel effortless. And you get absolutely zero nausea! Simply the best roller coaster I've ever ridden

My #1. It's the smoothest thrill coaster I've ever rode, it has my single favorite element of any coaster (the zero-g stall, this one does feel like you're neither touching the lap bar nor the seat for multiple seconds), it has a good amount of the type of airtime I love (sustained flojector), and the first drop is absolutely amazing. It's only downside compared to some other world class coasters is that it's not quite as action packed as e.g. Voltron, it doesn't have as many elements and there's a tiny amount of downtime between some of the elements. It's biggest downside is the physically stupidly long queue, even if it's a walk-on each re-ride still takes 10+ minutes of fast walking.

Best coaster i have ever been on. So good and thrilling, perfect drop, so much airtime and that one inversion that leaves you hanging out of your seat for 3 seconds is the best element on a roller coaster i've ever seen. It also looks beautiful with amazing theming. RMC did so so good with this one. A great night ride, and it was the perfect end to my 2025 roller coaster season.
Love it so much. Smooth from beginning till the end. I get alot motion sickness in most rollercoasters, but this ride was just pure fun and not a moment i felt sick (during or afterwards)

This coaster is an absolute masterpiece, definitely the 2nd best RMC behind Iron Gwazi. The amount of ejector you get on every single hill is absurd. It doesn't let up until the very end and feels like it never ends. And that drop- holy shit. It feels like being launched to saturn and back in the back row. Unbelievable ride that's worth the whole trip to Japan

A little bit disapointing. Zadra is much better. The pace is not the best, the inversions arent intense and it has dead spots. It is still an elite rollercoaster, much not the best in Japan, you cant compete with the beast Eejanaika.
You should come to Japan to ride this and the Eejanaika.

my first RMC and it did not disappoint. only con is that it's so far from home!

First ever RMC coaster, and I was blown away at how good this coaster. The pacing, the speed, the inversions.
My one complaint was the trains. Quite tight fit.
Definitely the best rollercoaster in japan

The last end of this roller coaster is exceptional. The pull is too great to accelerate and then move to the first drop! The American sitting in front of me also looked very happy. It's a vehicle that all mankind should ride.

Hakugei is my first RMC coaster and what a ride its got so much airtime dare i say a bit too much airtime becuase the lap bar hurts your shins on each airtime moment but its worth it the first drop is insane try to go for the back row because the first drop in the back is insane but overall this coaster is world class 10/10.

素晴らしいローラーコースターです。

Maybe it's kind of overrated, as the inversions are literally weak...

Best coaster in Japan, no doubt about it. The only dead spots are those weird left turns.

This didn't feel like a Top 10 coaster to me.  Maybe this gets higher ratings because it's the only RMC many of its riders have experienced?  Hakugei ranks in the middle of the 23 RMCs I've ridden. 
My favorites (Zadra, SteVe, Gwazi, AF1) leave me gobsmacked, but Hakugei left me wanting more intensity.  I kept thinking, "Come on.  Go faster!"  It has a grand and sweeping layout, and as a result the airtimes and inversions don't have any real "pop" to them.   Overall, it's smooth and fun, but it's not what I'd call thrilling.  Still, it's a good coaster that is worth the trip to NSL.
I love this rollercoaster, the inversions are awesome. There's like one section of the ride I remember which felt pretty rough and it's a little slow but other than that, lots of hang time.

I've never been so disappointed by a coaster. I really want to believe that the cold weather was neutering the ride. The drop is fantastic in the back, and the first 15 seconds or so are good, but I wouldn't consider it elite. Then, starting from the low-to-the-ground turn about halfway through, the coaster (for me) consistently fizzled out and dropped dead. Ran with zero power for the remainder of the layout, mild floater and sadness. Bummer!
Great ride! Great pacing, great setting next to the water. Fantastic air time. 45 min line on day 1. 20 min line in day 2.

The elements are all massive, which is both a good and bad thing. They feel grand and last a long time, but lack any whip or intensity because of it. The first few elements are spectacular, but it then has quite a few duds as the ride progresses, especially the inversions which all lack bite.

The drop and airtime simply makes it one of the best coasters I’ve ever ridden. It looks visually appealing, right next to the sea, you can get a view of it before you look down on the 80 degree drop. Amazing. Pure fun. Must do.

Hakugei's 1st 2 3rds of the track length is some of the best experience you can have on a Rollercoaster. It has a minor dead stop on the return trip back to the station where it slows the train down a bit. Otherwise it's an excellent ride!
Having more launches than words in the coaster's name is particularly impressive with this one
The world’s best family coaster. No doubt about it.

To start off, this ride is not intense. It's more of a fun ride than a wild one. I really enjoy how they decided to keep it screen-free, unlike most of the other Harry Potter rides. The motorcycle and sidecar train is quite unique as well. It lasts a long time, but doesn't overstay its welcome. I think the final launch is a bit underutilized based on the speed it gives, the ride could be a bit longer there. The wait times are also somewhat abysmal, but that is to be expected on a ride like this. Some additional queue theming in the cavelike section could be nice. Otherwise, a simply enjoyable experience.
Best themed coaster I’ve been on. Highly recommend the bike.

Update: the line is so much more tolerable than before with more people in express lane than regular que

The other day I say the wait was 30 minutes on a Monday without rain

Amazing layout, great launches, incredible theming; just so much fun.  Yet another Florida family coaster that puts everything else out there to shame.  This is blast to ride and even the queue is loaded with easter eggs to keep any HP fan entertained for the hours they may need to wait.
Bike go vroom. Cool theming.
great boosts, theming, layout and more, more and more

I know why it’s not as intense as I want it to be but I still love it.
This is one of the best coasters I've ever been on. I did go border line insane though from the caves.
Long line always

lovely ride. in between the madness that is velocicoaster and the kiddie coasters. hagrid’s is immersive, fast, and an allrounder. the bike seat is better than the cart so make sure to get it. lacking ever so slightly in intensity. the cart vehicle only seats 14 at a time which means the queue regularly hits two to three hours but the removal of universal express helped substantially. a 3 minute 25 second coaster is basically unheard of nowadays and is very welcome and it never feels like you’re on too long. i love that no screens were used.

Let’s get the only con I have out of the way, wait time is almost always an hour, not because they don't have good operations, but because LITERALLY everyone wants to ride it. Anyways... MASTERPIECE, what can I say, this ride is life changing, pure fun, all the "no inversions" "it's not intense" ride junkies can shut their mouths because you will not get on a better ride. No ride has this level of theming and pure fun, every time you think the coaster could not get better it does, somehow there's another launch or a vertical spike or a backwards moment or a surprise drop track, this ride does everything beautifully, a magical story and animatronics, one of the best themed queues in the world, and super unique coaster cars.
