I LOVE all the launches on this ride. It is so much fun and although it is not intense, it was way more fun then I was expecting. Queue is way too long for me to re-ride this unfortunately.
The queue is HORRENDOUSLY LONG!!!! 🫩
Comfy intamin ride, big potterhead so I loved it, great elements, great theming, well done intamin

Even though it's framed as a family-friendly ride, the option to go on the motorbike seat elevates this to a whole new level. It feels way faster and more immersive sitting in such a loose-feeling restraint, with the launches, air time hills, backwards section and drop track elements making the coaster feel packed with so many different thrills.

A near perfect rollercoaster let down by the insane wait times (2 hours for us) exaggerated by the fact our small kids who couldn’t ride had to queue with us to get to the parent swap handover room. We felt like we were being super unfair to the kids for our excitement to ride this coaster. Sorry kids, but it was worth it! 
One of the most fun rollercoasters of all time, even though it’s not hugely intense. It’s just so interesting, next level theming, amazing layout, surprises at every turn, multiple launches, comfortable ride. It has everything. Lodged itself firmly in m memory bank!

It has great theming and the launches felt amazing, especially the final one. It does break down often and wait times are very long, but it’s awesome when it breaks down when you’re on it, it happened to me and we got to reride it.
Best themed coaster. Love it every time. The launches, the theming, the carts. Really long ride aswell.
Very fun and bubbly ride. Drop track surprised me first time. I liked the motorbike better than the sidecar.
That drop track still manages to scare me- got front row and the spike is good I maybe want a bit more in the backwards section but it’s still 5*
As someone who is currently scared of bigger coasters, this is the perfect amount of intensity for me! One of Universal's greatest.
Masterpiece theming, but I had to wait 2.5 hours to get on.
The trim kills the drop but other than that and the pointless wall stall, it is absolutely incredible!!

Toutatis is a world class roller coaster. The launches are amazing and the pace is flawless. I absolutely love the theming and the ride is a great combination of intense elements, airtime and lots of fun. 10/10 experience!

This is a home park coaster for me, and despite many, MANY rides over the last nearly three years, I never get bored of it. The launches are punchy, almost every hill has great ejector, the heartline roll is really snappy and the stalls both have great hangtime. Toutatis is also consistently smooth and well operated, with at least two trains during the low season, and all three in the summer and during Halloween.

This is Intamin's best work.  Great launches, fun hangtimes, all kinds of airtime, smoothness, intensity, unique laterals, cool inversions.  I just love this coaster.  It definitely lives up to the hype.  It's a pure adrenaline rush from start to finish.  Toutatis makes its sister Pantheon feel like a kiddie coaster in contrast.   Intamin knocked it out of the park with this one.

Unfortunately Toutatis just didn't do it for me. Now, there's a number of reasons I think that is. The layout has some great moments, but too much of it was average at best. The stall didn't feel like it did a whole lot, the section after the first launch sort of meanders a bit, but the key part that really was underwhelming was the top hat. Talk about a dead spot when you're crawling over the top thanks to the huge trim brake. One of the biggest killjoys I've experienced. However I think the main reason I wasn't a big fan is actually the trains. Other Intamin coasters (and other rides that are similarly aggressive) have seats that are raised up so your feet aren't touching the floor. Toutatis sits you very low down, and combined with my tall frame means it was just a bit unnatural with the restraints. Which made the very aggressive pops of ejector a bit uncomfortable. Don't get me wrong, it's still a great ride, excellent in fact. But it's no patch on the likes of Taiga and Helix. Perhaps as much a case of overhyped as anything else.
10/10, nothing to add. Had 7 rides in one day, every single ride was better than the one before!
This ride was just amazing! The ejector airtime on the back row was so much fun.

FREAKING AMAZING!!!!!! All elements are incredible apart from the forceless wall stall, that does nothing... And the stupid trims. They ruin the drop. Launch is incredible, and the huge airtime hill is so fun, very pacy. There is a slight rattle in one of the trains, but it doesn't effect the ride.

An awesome 2023 rollercoaster. Every element is forceful, no matter how big or small. The triple launch has you flying out of your seat, into your seat, and free falling, one after another. Parc Asterix's theming style also makes this coaster shine even more.
It was super cool! The launch is very good, it had amazing moments of airtime, the theming was also amazing. Though the trim at the top hat kills it and I also didn't like the restrains
Nice triple-launch
So good it compares with steel vengeance, it might not be long but it has really good elements!

I was expecting good with this coaster, but not this level of airtimes which were insane. The triple launch section is amazing with the spike on the last row where you completely fly. The sensations are crazy. Everything else is great on this coaster, so nice.

This is my personal number 1 and in my opinion the best coaster in Europe. This ride is just airtime airtime and I love. Toutatis has a nice pace and a wonderful swing launch. The stall gives some great hangtime and the barrel Roll is really fun. I am looking forward to getting back on this. Must do in Europe.

Very good coaster, potentially better than RTH. It is disappointing that there is a few dead spots such as the trimmed top hat and outer banked hills at the start of the ride, but the wave turn provides a good moment of weightlessness to catch your breath- although the transition out of it could be snappier. This ride is awesome,  one of the most intense I have ridden and definitely showcases the masterpiece of the blitz model. The highlight is the triple launch and abundant moments of airtime.
Slow pacing on the top hat, but the best coaster in entire France. A must-ride!

First tip: go on row 10. From the first mini drop, you get pulled which gives you more airtime, then you hit the first launch, after a stall with amazing hangtime, you go across more airtime pops, then into the swing launch. The airtime is simply magnificent. All launches are punchy, and if you’re in row 10 the spike gives you so much weightlessness. The trims on the top hat kills the ride a bit, but the two turns leading into the Zero-G stall is intense, the stall itself offering much hangtime, and finally, another airtime hill, giving ejector airtime for like the 194749104th time. Then, you go through a wave turn stall that doesn’t do much, then into a crazy intense turn and a heartline roll. I haven’t ridden Velocicoaster so I can’t compare the rolls, but for me the roll on Toutatis offers lots of whip. Two more airtime moments then into the brakes. Truly a masterpiece! Intamin smashed it again!

The best coaster in France. I was really looking forward to this ride, and wow, it completely exceeded my expectations. From the moment you leave the station, the coaster doesn’t stop until you’re back again. The view from the back row during the backward launch is absolutely insane. The only downside I’d say is the trim on the top hat. Other than that, the coaster is simply fantastic.
At least one time in your life you should do this, especially if you live near france. The airtimes on this one are absolutely crazy, they are so great and fun tho it's scary.

I really liked Toutatis - theming and location are great. Format and layout are really solid. But, intensity was one notch down from what I was hoping for - a 7.5 out of 10. A little more speed and height and it would be a top 10 for me. Instead - really good, but not great - and it could've been.
It’s great and I really wanted to keep it as my favorite coaster but the rattle (non-existent in 2024) cost it the first place.
“wowza”
Amazing ride with many ejector airtimes, fun theming, great for back row! maybe 1 more inversion could've been added

The beginning is a nice warm-up, the launch-section with the spike is the absolute highlight of the ride, but afterwards there are multiple elements that are completely pointless (top hat and zero-g stall). Overall it has a lot of airtime with good theming and launches. It's not as super smooth as Kondaa or Taron, it has a small rattle that becomes annoying if you're there on an empty day and marathon it, ride it dozens of times.

Amazing ride, amazing pacing, straight into the action right from the start with the first launch , this first roll where you feel like you’re going to fall out of your seat, the zero g roll , the great turns too, and also this turn that goes right into an inversion is magical, smooth ride. The launch feels amazing, especially when you’re on the back and fly up that 51m arrow, the tophat is a bit disappointing but the rest of the ride is great, when you get off you just wish it was longer
steel vengeance still better🤣🤣

Wow! With Iron Gwazi ranked at #2 in the world... I had very high expectations. After my first ride, let me tell you, it exceeded them. What a trip. As soon as I got I off, I thought, "what in the world just happened to me??"

This ride is relentless. The pacing is amazing. The transitions are amazing (and surprising). Airtime in the back row on the first drop is stellar. I LOVE that downhill barrel roll that I just learned they call "The Death Roll." What a wild element. I rode this in the back row, front row, and a few spots throughout. Every spot is a great time. Back is definitely going to be more intense and give you more airtime, but the front row, especially on a night ride, is so much fun. On that note, riding at night is a completely different animal. Highly recommended.

I'll be coming back for more Iron Gwazi!

I’ll post a real review probably bc this is a masterpiece but I’m actually shocked that some guy rode this with COVID and then rated it poorly.  I mean the jokes write themselves (no taste!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!)
I got off this absolutely lost for words. The first drop is unreal and every single element hits so hard. It is fairly short but only because you are going at such a high speed.

While Iron Gwazi is no doubt a good ride, it is greatly overhyped.  Unfortunately, Iron Gwazi does not live up to expectations, while a very fun ride, it simply is not elite.  Compared to other rmc hybrids, this layout seems to have larger drawn out spaces in between elements as opposed to rides like Twisted Timbers and Steel Vengeance where each element immediately flies into the next with very limited space in between.  The highlight of the ride is easily the first drop, being the one thing Gwazi has over Vengeance.  It personally shocks me how so many consider this the best RMC when it personally is my least favorite out of the five I've been on.  I know its a hot take but Gwazi truly didn't impress me, and I rode it over four times across multiple visits, both of which had great weather.  A lot of people compare this ride to Steel Vengeance, which to me is a great shock as I don't even see these two coasters on the same level.  If you believe Gwazi is better that's great!  We all have our own opinions, but this is one I personally just don't get it at all.  Rmc hit an incredibly high note with Steel Vengeance, due to so many comparing Gwazi to Vengeance my standards and expectations were set far beyond what they should've been.  Part of me wonders if less people would prefer Gwazi over Vengeance if Gwazi opened first, as to me, this is nothing but a ride carried by hype.

This ride is tied with steel vengeance for my rankings at number one. It is a perfect ride except that it is half as long as Steve. If it had been made at the same time as Steve it would be worse, but it benefited from all the elements of the 2018 and 2019 RMCs (Hakugei, Zadra, Untamed, Twisted timbers) and it is also in Florida which is way hotter so that is an unfair advantage too. It is more intense than Steve Which I love, but its half as long. I rode Gwazi at its absolute best time of year, july 29, and got a night ride. same for Steve. Steve is better at the start of the day, but I am basing it off of the night rides when they have fully warmed up. Gwazi was super rerideable for me and is nowhere near so intense its uncomfortable to marathon like some woodies like the legend for instance. Snooty coaster enthusiasts dunk on Steve for no reason, but objectively Gwazi and Steve are the best RMCs and which you like more is preference, but don't go saying that some like Steve more because its more intense because my 50 year old mom marathoned Gwazi and we got like 8 rides in the last 2 hrs. of park operations (she likes Steve more than Gwazi because its longer, and Gwazi is not too intense for her.) This is tied for my favorite coaster though and I absolutely adore it, but people who don't have Steve, Gwazi or maybe eejanaika or like the ride to happiness are just kidding themselves and are objectively wrong. Gwazi and Steve are evenly matched but get way overly nitpicked by anyone who wants to disagree with the popular opinion. These are the best two RMCs, plus incredible night ride (also how in the absolute heck can it get such good airtime on an overbanked turn???? Best overbank ever!!!!!)
I wish I could rate Iron Gwazi 6 stars. Period. Cheer up to Allan Schilke.

Iron Gwazi is fantastic. Amazing first drop, the inversions are crazy, and the death roll is one of my favorite elements ever! However, similar to Steel Vengeance, the ride experience is severely damaged by those RMC trains. Why, oh, WHY do they have to be SO PAINFUL? But this ride wasn't nearly as aggressive on my entire body as Steve, so it was way easier to handle than Steel Vengeance, just causing a mild discomfort at certain times. Also, the operations SUCK. Genuinely horrible and I was only able to get 2 rides because of this.
Still a world class coaster but disbatches were awful and very short. Still awesome though

This ride did not live up to the hype for me. While it is most likely because I only got 2 morning rides with covid on it, I still am gonna hate on it.  Most of the elements were complete duds, with little to no force, and there were even a couple of rough patches that hurt my head. The elements that disappointed me the most were the death roll and the wave turn. Starting with the former, the death roll is the most nothing burger inversion I have experienced. While it looks sort of cool with the world spinning around, there was zero force to be felt. No airtime, no laterals, no positives, no hangtime, nothing. It was too fast to give any hangtime, and too slow for laterals and/or whip. Now for the wave turn. I usually love wave turns on rides, especially RMCs. So, you could have imagined how excited I was to ride Iron Gwazi when I saw it had a wave turn. Little did I know that this would be the weakest wave turn I have experienced by far. It feels like you are lying in bed with a fan blowing in your face. The world is on its side, and you have wind in your face, as well as the zero force that you would feel when lying in bed. I could go on and on about Iron Gwazi, but I will stop here. I am reriding it later this month, hopefully not in the morning and hopefully not with covid, so hopefully I will enjoy Iron Gwazi more than my first experience on it.
There was a dude who had ridden this at least 2k times. I need his mindset and his thighs for how much ejector this has. Perfect

Until riding this, wildcats revenge at Hersheypark was my favorite coaster. This was very similar just bigger, better, faster, more… front, back, middle… just outstanding! My new number 1! Well Iron Gwazi. Where do I even start? Whilst I will say right off the bat that Steel Vengeance is still my top RMC and with that number one coaster, Iron Gwazi is certainly the most intense and punchy RMC out there. The ride absolutely hammers you with a great mix of positive G Forces and also stunning airtime in its layout. The drop is sensational, the outerbank is airtime heaven,the death roll is hands down my favourite inversion on a coaster, the wave turn is a wonderful element, the stall is taken wonderfully and the latter airtime hills all deliver the goods. Now people like to compare this to Zadra and I personally have to say thats an easy win for Iron Gwazi. Is the drop on Zadra better? No. Are the inversions on Zadra better than Iron Gwazi's? No. Is the wave turn better? No. Is the airtime better? No. Is it more intense? No. So I really think its a no contest and taken into account Zadra is also an epic coaster, that should tell you exactly how good Iron Gwazi is. One negative though has to be the operations. 3-5 minute dispatches is just not good. It was very common to see the previously dispatched train parked up in the break run before the loading train even had its lap bars put down. Hopefully that improves. That however is the only negative for an otherwise perfect coaster!!

Nice one. Very very very good. Better than steel vengeance imo which might make some people crashout on me. The layout felt more exciting and the inversions whipped more. The airtime moments were also more powerful than the ones on steel vengeance. 10/10 insane.

Genuine contender for best coaster in the world. Insane airtime, fantastic hangtime, great launches, artistic layout, no dead space. Checks virtually every box you could want. The queue theming is dry, but the coaster itself? Virtually perfect.

This ride is actually so underrated for no reason. Sure the theming could be a bit better but it really doesn’t take away from the ride itself at all. And the ride is absolutely incredible. Seriously, this is one of the greatest layouts on any roller coaster for the fact that literally every single element hits on this thing. On most coasters, there’s at least one element that doesn’t hit as hard as the rest, but on this, that doesn’t exist. Even before the swing launch, you have world-class hangtime and two very weird hills that give off-axis floater. Then the swing launch which cranks things up to 200. The backwards speed hill is seriously one of the craziest moments of airtime ever, and that spike is incredible. Then, the rest of the ride is just a mix of incredible airtime and an incredible inversion with lots of speed. Absolutely incredible ride and it should be praised more.
Didn’t know what to expect when I first rode this and I was throughly impressed. I don’t care about theming, this ride delivers!

Toutatis shows how this layout should be done with great intensity throughout.

Very interesting coaster that's kind of hard to pin down and masters in awkward airtime. Having been on Toutatis comparing the two feels unavoidable here - Pantheon's top hat without the trim is noticeably better and I don't think the huge gap in theming is what ultimately separates the two. Toutatis is more immediately engaging out of the station whereas Pantheon's zero-g winder doesn't do a ton other than shift my seating position. Where the gap widens is after the top hat - the outward banked hill on Pantheon feels oversized whereas Toutatis' banked hill is profiled more tightly and gets to follow a super strong ejector hill that Pantheon doesn't have. Toutatis also has stronger turns that have some whip that Pantheon can't really match - the latter still has awesome elements for sure but not as satisfying of a layout overall. I don't think dressing up Pantheon with a bunch of theming would suddenly make this one of the best coasters in the world but it might ease concerns about private equity driving creative decisions.

While many people have been calling this masterpiece overrated in recent times, I’d say it’s the most complete ride I've ever been on. The theming is insane from the moment you enter the queue until the very end, and the ride itself is close to perfect. The first half gets a lot of hate, but it genuinely surprised me with several moments—especially the dive loop in the front row, which almost nobody talks about. The way you get violently thrown entering that element is incredible. The second launch and the top hat are as great as everyone says, and the following elements continue to deliver. Then the ending hits like nothing else out there. The Mosasaurus Roll already has a legendary reputation, but the twisty afterward and the entry into the brake run coming immediately after the roll are insanely agressive and seriously underrated. I don’t think those moments are talked about nearly enough. The famous highlights like the launches, the top hat, the stall, and the Mosasaurus Roll all delivered exactly as expected. But it was these less-discussed moments that surprised me the most. They’re what truly set this ride apart, making it easily my number one, and I don’t see it being beaten anytime soon.

The paddock section is so fun with a fantastic one-two punch after the first launch with hangtime on the first element and surprising airtime on the dive loop after it. Even the moments between the dive loop and second launch are fantastic with great headchoppers, theming interaction (especially at night) and a punchy airtime hill. Then that second half... fantastic pacing and sense of speed. And the operations on this with 5 (6??) trains with sub-60 second dispatches. Is there a better all around coaster on the planet? I can't imagine so.

This is Universal Orlando’s airtime machine, no questions asked. The first half is full of multiple wonderful sustained ejector moments that provide the best, most, and strongest air at the resort. Almost at 250 coasters now, with most of Europe’s and the U.S. West Coast’s biggest rides under my belt—but I’ve never experienced something this intense in my life! I’d need something like Eejanaika or Intimidator 305 for a fair comparison, but this thing? It’s not even close to X2—it’s absurdly intense!
So first conclusion: this is not for everyone.

Now that you’ve been warned, let’s get into the details!

The first launch is nice and punchy, done in two phases. I’m not the biggest fan of the two-step system, but it’s followed by a solid first brain-melter of a G+ moment. Then we hit the top hat with a very strong and sustained ejector, and as we drop down again—disaster strikes!

This is the moment everyone talks about: “Why the trims?” you might ask.
Well, without them, you’re just dead. No joke.
Even as a seasoned rider, hitting that valley at night folded me in half against the lap bar with those insane forces. That’s never happened to me before!

Okay, we’re past the most “sensitive” moment. Now we’re back in the air, still catching airtime, especially on the first hill, leading into a turnaround—not super noteworthy, but solid.

Then it’s ejector after ejector, before that gorgeous 180° in front of the entrance, which looks great and leads into one last (slightly weaker) airtime moment before hitting the second launch.

From here, the layout shifts focus—less on airtime, more on whip and dueling elements.
We enter the Celestial Spin, which is visually striking for the dueling effect, though less intense in terms of raw sensation than, say, a Death Roll or Maus au Saurus Roll.

Then comes a massive overbanked turn—not much to report there, except that even up that high you’re still getting solid G-forces. Then comes the EGF turn, which is just incredible, possibly my favorite element of the whole ride!

After that, your skull gets crushed in a long helix that climbs slightly toward the end (or the start, depending on the side), kind of a mini I305 warning shot—though to be fair, probably not quite as intense as I305, lol.

Then one last airtime moment, not quite as crazy as the first half’s, and finally a last pop of airtime as you hit the brakes.

So… what do I think?

It’s absolutely excellent: incredibly intense, tons of ejectors, a wide variety of elements, a great length—but yeah… probably too intense for a lot of people.
The ejectors don’t go into leg-ripping -2G territory, but the positive Gs are extremely pronounced and relentless throughout!

Watch out for some minor rattle on the green side, but nothing major.

Conclusion:
A world-class coaster, not to be missed. If you can handle the intensity—go ride it NOW!

I slightly prefer green over yellow, but this side is still great in other ways. For starters, the yellow side had a shorter queue when I rode. Also, the part where the ride does an inversion over the other track (the inversion on this side faces down) is a lot more relaxed than on the other side, offering a little bit of easy on the body thrill whilst still maintaining its world renowned intensity. More onto the ride itself, there were some really fun overbanked turns and it also had stunning views of the Isle of Berk next door. I'm going to keep in line with the fact that there's a flux capacitor on the back of the trains and say with utmost confidence that we hit 88 miles per hour and saw some serious crap.
I prefer velocicoaster, but this packs a punch

Personally i think the yellow is superior to green as it is more comfortable in my experience. doesn’t quite live up to the insanity that is velocicoaster just a few miles away but i truly wasn’t expecting epic universe to have a coaster of this degree so it is very welcome. two incredible launches up to 112km/h with a very cool racing element to it, you are neck and neck the entire time with the green side. although the launches are quite rattly and since it is so new and everybody wants to try it, it goes down quite a lot, leading to longer queue times after. in my experience the queues are anywhere from walk on to around half an hour.

While green is better, yellows airtime is noticeably stronger and you feel so weightless going through the hills in the first half, after the second launch you definitely feel some of the momentum loss when compared to the other side but without the comparison it’s still so much fun and an elite coaster in its own right

Stardust Racers is more than just a roller coaster--it's an experience sent from heaven. I rode the yellow side in the front row at night with onboard audio, and that was one of the single best roller coaster rides of my life. The airtime is both powerful and comfortable, the trains are beautiful, the launches are intense, the theming and vibes are truly celestial, and the soundtrack perfectly ties it all together. Every time I think about Stardust Racers I can't help but smile. While the green side has more sustained airtime moments, I prefer the sharper, more abrupt airtime moments on the yellow side.
Griddle123 has ridden this ride
I LOVE IT, SUPER FUN! I wish I could ride green side tho :( 10/10
BANGER! One of the best coasters ever. Really high re rideabillity. The ride is so awesome. Fast, dueling, airtime, two launches. It is insane. Really amazing
Sat in eighth row Celestial spin was good but really ricketty

From the moment it was announced, this was the coaster on the top of my bucket list, I knew it would be my #1 whenever i got the chance to ride it because it hits ALL the marks for me, and now that i got the chance to ride it, i confirmed my theory and it's not even close. this ride has absurd ejector, strong whip, and doing all that while spinning is completely insane!! highlights include: the jojo roll, the entry and exit into the top hat, the airtime hill on the second launch, the entry into the double-inverting dive loop, and the double up at the end, but even the less powerful moments are absurdly fun due to the spinning. this ride is everything i could've asked for on a ride, it more than lives up to its name!
This rollercoaster is designed by God.

I would give this ride 6 stars if I could. This ride is absolutely insane. My current number 1 coaster in the world. The experience begins as you enter the queueline, which has some very cool steampunk theming, like fans, schematics and there is a huge fireplace thing that is super cool. Then you come into the outdoor section of the queueline, which has some nice plants and a water wheel thing. There is plenty to look at in this part of the queue, though you will most likely not be there long. You then ascend some stairs into another, smaller steampunk section of the queue, this time indoors. There are some more schematics and a big boiler thing, which I think is very cool. You then ascend some stairs and lo and behold, the station is right there. 
In the station things can get quite stupid. If you are at the front of the queue just before being let into the rows, PLEASE do not allow anyone to push past. This will give everyone else the green light to push past and queue up outside the row they are waiting for which already has 2 train loads worth of people in it. Very messy and uncivilised. When you reach that section of the queue, if you are at the front, hold it with and iron fist.
The station itself is very cool. There is a hologram thing surrounded by cogs that says stuff like, "Live today, love tomorow, unite forever." The trains are beautifully designed, with each individual car looking like a cog or some piece of a clock or something. The restraints are you typical, comfy Mack restrains. Then you get sent out the station into the first inversion, a Jojo roll. You get some INSANE hangtime on that inversion in the front two cars, and you get whipped through it much quicker. Then you come to a stop at the launch.You may still be spinning a bit from the Jojo roll, so you might take the launch backwards, sideways or whatever way the car is facing. Suddenly you launch, and halfway through, you begin spinning like crazy. You go up the top hat, with entering the base being super intense, and at the apex getting some WONDERFUL airtime. You then meander through the top, though this is not boring or bad at all. In fact, at dusk you can get some insane views with the setting sun. The drop off the top hat is great, and you get launched into the banana roll. This is pretty crazy and gives some great hangtime. I find it quite intense. You might take it backwards or sideways as well.
Coming off the Jojo roll you get flung into the vertical loop, which gives oodles of hangtime and some crazy G force. You get whipped into the next inversion, a zero G roll I think, which is full of airtime and hangtime. I definitely recommend putting your hands up for this bit. Next there is an S hill I think, which gives decent airtime, and then you hit the second launch. The second launch gets you spinning even more, which is greatly needed for the next element. However in the middle of the launch there is a hill which gives insane ejector airtime because you traverse it with such speed. Then you get thrown into the craziest part of the ride. The flying snake dive (I think). You get thrown up into the air. You spin around so much in this part, which just makes it crazier. You sort of do a roll thing that transitions into a dive loop. That is kind of what the flying snake dive is. You get wonderful hangtime, and there is just a sense of extreme craziness here. By far the best element of the ride.
You then come off the flying snake dive into an S hill I think, or it might just be an overbank. It is hard to tell when you are on ride. You do get plenty of G force here though, it is very intense.
Then you come into a VIOLENT double up, each hill giving aggressive pops of ejector airtime. Then it is over. You come into the brake run and come back into the station. What a ride. The theming, inversions, airtime, intensity, hangtime... everything comes together to make an insane experience. Next I have to mention the onboard audio. The soundtrack was specifically designed by Tomorrowland to fit the ride, so that the music increases in tempo as the ride intensifies. It does a great job of that, and the ride would definitely not be as good without it. It syncs very well with all the different elements and just adds an extra layer of goodness to the experience. Next, the area is very cool and aesthetically pleasing, with lots of cool stuff. I will place some guidelines for riding below. You do not have to follow these, it in my opinion make the ride way better:
If you can, ride near the end of the day when it has warmed up.
Put your hands up for the Jojo roll, entering the top hat, exiting the top hat, apex of banana roll, vertical loop, the whole of the zero G roll, the S hill, all of the second launch, flying snake dive and last two airtime hills. This will give you better airtime and hangtime.
Ride it over and over again, because with this ride you get a new experience every time. Your last ride my be way better than your next, maybe because more spinning, maybe because you took an element sideways or backwards instead of forwards, whatever it is. You have to try it a lot to get the ultimate ride.
Ride at dusk to get some insane views.
I prefer the front car because it gives more hangtime, but the back car is way more intense. I guess it is just preference, but these are undeniably the best cars to ride in.
Do not ride it repeatedly. When you get off it can be very tempting to hop in line for another go, but usually 2 or 3 rides at a time is enough before you should take a break and try some of the other rides at the park, like Heidi the ride or Dino Splash. There are some hidden gems elsewhere in the park. 
In case of bad weather the ride may not operate and may not be running its best, so check the weather forecast and plan accordingly.
The End! Thanks for reading! :D

It is almost a perfect coaster, crazy reride ability, not that many people so you can keep going forever, sometimes you don't even have to get out of the seat to go again, the music on ride is also a great addition. First car is the best overall experience, 2-3 are definitely worse, number 4 is good for the whip when the train is going downhill.

I think that rth has everything I've ever loved: being different, with a different theme (I'm also a fan of edm!) and a soundtrack that gives me chills everytime, also the atmosphere in the station and in the Tomorrowland area. It's just magic. One of the things I love the most is that, unlike most of the coasters, it doesn't have that "intimidating" mood, it doesn't try to scare you...it only gives you magical vibes. It's difficult to put it into words...I feel like I'm in heaven. It's always a mix of laughing and crying of joy on the brake run. I've never, and I say never, been so emotional and happy in my life. Its name is perfect, it's so different but I fell in love with it since the first time.
This ride is all I would ever dreamed. The intensity is great but not too much, just how I like it. The spinning too, not too much but definitely enough to give you new experiences and unpredictability. The inversions, for me, are magic. the first one is the best hangtime I've ever experienced. the banana roll and the loop, while not forceful (if not for the positive Gs in the valleys), give amazing hangtime especially in the back row, giving you the time to spin and giving a sensational out-of-control and freedom feeling. The 0g roll and the dive loop feel like a front/backflip if taken sideways and give you pure upside-down ejector airtime in the front row. 
The airtime moments are so unique and different from each other...the one entering the top hat is the strongest ever tried, the one exiting in the back (better if backwards) is the best ever tried, the one during the second launch is the most underrated moment of the ride, the hill after the dive loop feels so out-of-control, and the last bunny hills are one of the most fun elements ever.
Also the launches are masterpieces, with the first one being punchy and amplified by the spinning, and the second one being enhanced with the airtime.
I love how the music is perfectly syncronized with the layout, and I absolutely adore how the ride intensifies while going on, giving you the most floaty-gentle elements in the first half and the most forceful in the second half. The escalation of intensity is something I absolutely adore on coasters in general.
I can understand why someone could not like it, for example who likes pure airtime or pure speed over anything else, or who privileges extreme intensity or crushing G-forces. But if someone asked me to imagine the how would the perfect coaster look like for me, I bet I couldn't have imagined anything this good. I just cannot wait for my next visit and the only thought of it...makes me so emotional.
This coaster is a out of control ejector filled masterpiece

WOW if you live in the UK you gotta go super easy to get from via calais, better than falcons flight that spinning sensation is just so amazing, although its so intense may be over intense for some people but otherwise a masterclass mack needs to make a giga spinning coaster that would be INSANE!

I rode RTH barely a week after riding Voltron at Europapark. Having read all the reviews, and RTH being in the world's top 10 (well, for now), I expected something out of this world, but to be fair, while it was indeed super fun to ride with many ejectors, an incredible theming and some intense moments, I definitely didn't feel gobsmacked the way I did with Voltron. Perhaps because on my first ride, I was sitting backwards and didn't have much luck with the spinning, I actually felt a little disappointed when I realized my expectations had probably been too high. However, I rode it 5 other times throughout the day in different seats/directions and got to like it more and more. I'd definitely advise the fourth train, facing frontwards for the best experience, and do put up your hands to enjoy the airtime even more ! The coaster put us up and down so many times I didn't even know where I was anymore, you easily lose track of where top is and where bottom is. The layout is quite fun, much attention was paid to the theming too, and the trains are so comfortable! I didn't experience any rattle. RTH is not my favourite coaster but definitely still worth a visit to Plopsaland, it IS a very unique and technical beast Mack Rides brought to that park.

Most has been said already, so I'll just confirm that this is a very good coaster, probably one of the best ones in the world. As a Belgian, I missed out on this ride up until now. Just before moving overseas, I counted myself lucky to score a few rides on Kondaa. There's pro's and cons to both rides. Some people will like Kondaa better for the first drop and the pacing, others will prefer Ride To Happiness because of its uniqueness. Truth is, it's pretty ridiculous we have these two coasters in the tiny country Belgium actually is. The only coaster I personally can compare RTH somewhat to, is X2. They both are masterpieces, and RTH is for sure way smoother. Go ride this thing and just enjoy the fact it's located in a family theme park. You can reride this absolute gem of a coaster at least ten times on any given day without the need for a fast pass. And we all know how rare that actually is these days.
Just AMAZING!🤩

What a coaster...this was on the top of my bucket list for a very long time end it was abolutely worth the wait.
everything is perfect,powerful launches,great inversions and a very complete layout..maybe a bit too short.
the top hat in back is surely one of the best element i have ever experienced and the same for the flying snake dive and the two final hills.
and as a edm fan and tomorrowland lover the theming and the music give something even more special to this ride.
No other coaster makes you HAPPIER
Best ride I've ridden
Best coaster on earth. You never know what happened.

Ride to Happiness is a masterpiece. 
The ejectors on back car exiting the top hat are some of the strongest I've ever experienced. 
The theming is immersive and the trains consist of the usual comfortable Mack Rides seats and lap bars. 
The pacing is relentless.
There are minor vibrations in the middle two cars but nothing serious.
It's almost too intense but it's a must-ride attraction.

The roller coaster that... gets very slightly marginally worse the more you ride it. Your first ten laps are by far the best you'll ever have, as the entire time you'll be having the ride of your life. Laps 11-25 you start to realise that certain elements are better when they're taken facing a specific direction, and then laps 25+ you're almost a little disappointed when you go through a part of the ride not facing the direction that you wanted. The randomness is by far the best part of the ride until you've ridden it 30-odd times, then you start to realise that if you had a button to make the ride exactly the same every single time, would you press it? Sometimes I just want the guarantee of that backwards drop in the back row or to front-flip through the double roll, y'know?

The Ride to Happiness remains one of the very best amusement machines ever built. That layout with the spinning trains is just mental, you get forces and airtime that you simply cannot get on any other ride. Some of the best elements ever put on a coaster are on this ride, notably the zero g roll and the ridiculous double-inverting dive loop, and then it finishes with 2 of the strongest ejector hills I've ever experienced. Not to mention the gorgeous aesthetic of the ride, the station, the area as a whole and the immaculate trains. It's super comfortable as well, in my opinion Mack do the best trains in the business and these are no exception, the auto-lowering lap bars always sit in the right spot for me to get the airtime. The one area it gets let down by is the rattle, which is very inconsistent, sometimes it's fine but occasionally I have a ride that's a lot worse, combined with how intense it is it really knocks me for six. It does concern me how it will ride in 5 years from now. Whilst that means it isn't as rerideable as it once was, the bottom line remains that RtH is an incredible ride, truly elite, and still firmly sat in my top 5

One of the best roller coaster I've ever been on. It is amazing. First of all, the theme, and especially the music, are fantastic. The layout itself is also great. You have the pre-launch inversion first, the inversion with the best hangtime in the world in my opinion. The launch is fun too. After that come some great moments. Then comes the second launch, this one is much better than the first one because it has airtime. Then comes one of my favourite inversions on a rollercoaster. This one is very special because at that moment you don't know where you are. After that, there are some great airtime moments.

I love everything about this ride. The theming is great, the queues are usually pretty manageable, and the ride itself is unique, intense and unforgettable.

If you haven’t been, go!

Where do I even begin… RTH is an absolute beast of a roller coaster. I’ve never experienced such an intense ride before. After the first insane hangtime, I genuinely thought I was going to pass out or at least grey out, but luckily I made it through!

I’m personally more of a fan of crazy drops, and spinning coasters aren’t really my favorite, which is why I didn’t give it a full 5 stars. That said, if you’re looking for an extreme coaster that truly pushes your limits, this is the one for you!
OH MY GOD, BEST COASTER IN EUROPE
Simply an amazing ride! The best coaster in Belgium, and one of the best worldwide.

This ride is incomprehensibly good. I can't even put into words how insane some of the elements are and i'd have a hard time picking out the highlights of the ride as it's all so good. The double inverting dive loop is my favorite inversion ever, the 2nd launch is my favorite launch ever, and the tophat has my favorite drop ever. I can't believe this thing exists and i can't wait to ride it again.

This is one of the BEST coasters ever created. The layout is amazing. The spinning isn’t “too much” to make you sick…. I love the jojo roll, and I love that every single ride is different. 10/10. Wish more parks had these.

This thing is genuinely unbelievable. I live pretty close to this park so when this was announced I was hyped as I’d have a big RMC near me. While I was a little skeptical about how it’d run, I got on this thing, and over  25 rides later, this thing is absolutely perfect and one of RMC’s best. The only moment where you can breathe is the space between the underflip and the camelback. But once you hit the camelback, this thing doesn’t let up and literally tries to kill you with each element. Some of the most aggressive elements ever constructed are on this ride, with elements like that camelback, the double down (combining INSANE laterals with ejector), the super snappy downwards roll, the incredibly aggressive pops at the end, those insane wave turns, and of course, the stall, which is one of my favorite inversions ever. RMC and Hershey hit it out of the park with this thing, finally having a ride that most can agree is the best in the park.
This ride is absolute awesomeness, The ride is amazing, butter smooth and has very high capacity. The ops could do a better job though at loading.
This is the 2nd best ride at Hershey Park right behind Skyrush.
This was my first RMC and the reason I now understand the phrase “standing ejector”. I almost shit my pants. My goodness.

This is at my home park, but there's no bias needed to rave about a ride like this. It's probably the best or one of the best layouts on not just an RMC, but on a roller coaster period. It throws everything at you in a very smooth, flawless, seamless sequence packed with so many extremely surprising elements which leaves you guessing what's coming next. Ridiculously powerful ejector airtime, aggressive lateral jolts, a beautiful collection of inversions sporting whip, snap, and hangtime, all with violent pacing throughout the entire course and solid ride length over glossy track to top it all off. When we hit those last two hills on my first ever ride, I actually couldn't even believe that the ride was this unthinkably powerful. Some of the most extreme forces on any roller coaster ever, and it's absolutely perfect.

This is my favorite roller coaster by far it’s twice as good as furry 325 at least it’s butter smooth, has a great layout and has great restraints. The elements flow like water in a stream. I expected this to be great but I was wrong it was so good that I cant use words to describe it. I love it it doesn’t matter where you sit it’s always amazing it’s the best coaster I’ve ever ridden so RMC if you are reading this keep on doing what you do best hybrid coasters.

This was genuinely a dream come true for me. Since I became a coaster enthusiast I wanted one day for Wildcat to get RMCd. This is my home park they had such a good opportunity for an RMC and they took it. I had literal dreams of this being a reality and every time as the train dispatched in the dream I would wake up. This dream happened more and more leading up to its opening. And I can truly say it’s everything I dreamed of. This is genuinely as of writing this the best paced coaster I have been on. Each element just adds onto each other and the ride feels like it just keeps gaining speed. Theres plenty of airtime and different forms of it as well. Not to mention the inversions are all extremely well done. There is not a single moment to breath on this coaster and thats how I like it. This coaster is better then anything I could have imagined.

Fantastic ride that's just below the Tier 1 RMCs for me. Obviously the pacing of this thing is unreal and the elements on their own are nearly all very good (the underflip is a miss). I don't really feel a cohesive thesis behind sequencing of said elements that gives Wildcat's Revenge as strong an identity as this company's best creations.
amazing one of the best rides ever the harness / lap bar confused me but awsome ride
My first RMC IBox coaster. This ride really just throws you around like a ragdoll it's nuts. How is this real lol

This is by far my most ridden RMC hybrid coaster and it's easily the best one below 200ft. Some of the strongest airtime I have experienced on a coaster, whippy inversions, and unsuspected positives. Incredible ride.

I keep hearing "this RMC is a mini Steel Vengeance" about all the middle-tier RMC's but Twisted Timbers didn't do what this does. All 4 inversions are reminiscent of SteVe's and I felt that same power on all the airtime hills. I want rerides.

Another top tier RMC. I have it as my favourite over Hakugei, SteVe, Twisted Colossus, Twisted Timbers and Iron Gwazi. Why? This ride has the power but not the painful bunny hops of SteVe & Twisted Timbers. Prefer the layout to Gwazi too. The margins are very fine. Only downer are the slow operations at Hershey - though the clientele trying to carry stuff on ride rather than locking it up for free are part of cause of that.

My first RMC was definitely a great one. Wildcats Revenge has an amazing layout and perfect pacing. It starts with a great pre-lift, followed by the loudest lift ever constructed. This is followed by a spectacular ride packing in some amazing airtime moments, my favorites being the beginning camelback, the wave turns with insane sideways airtime, and the crazy double down with insane laterals. I am usually not a lateral fan, but the way wildcats revenge adds it to the layout is world class. The elements keep you guessing and the sequencing is world class. I am not the biggest fan of most of the inversions, the step-up under flip does not do much for me and the zero g rolls are just fine. The zero g stall is amazing and one of my favorite moments of the ride though. Wildcats Revenge is silky smooth and has the best pacing of any coaster I have ever been on. It always feels like your in an element with no breathing room in between. The last hills are crazy, especially since I still had a lot of room for airtime. The brake run set up and the last two hills, are very painful though, you get slammed into the side of the train. The lap bar also can leave my thighs bruised at the end. Other than a few cons, Wildcats Revenge is almost perfect, with an unmatched flow of elements, pacing, and relentless ejector airtime. Not to mention, it it wicked intense with crazy positive g's and whip. Overall, Wildcat's Revenge was the perfect coaster to introduce me to RMC, and it will always be one of my favorite coasters.
Rerode it and it was amazing!

Restraints are slightly more comfortable than steel vengeance and it doesn’t have all the annoying bunny hills that tear up your thighs. If it was longer and taller this would give SV a run for its money.
The first couple times I rode it would be 5 stars but the last time I rode on every airtime hill hurt my thighs

My first "hybrid"... Now it's my favorite type of coaster. 

Love the flow and relentless energy of this ride. Favorite part was how long you were inverted during one of the barrell rolls... Was not expecting something like that!

You have to empty your pockets, remove hats, and take off your glasses (unless you have a strap) and store them in lockers before boarding. Having also been on Iron Gwazi recently, HersheyPark elevates the guest experience here in a few ways:

1. The lockers are at the end of the queue, rather than the beginning.

2. The lockers are FREE. 

3. There's a practical reason for the lockers rather than using cubbies in the station, like every other coaster at HP... Unboarding happens in a different part of the station than boarding (speeding up the line).

One of the benefits I experienced from having the locker "choke point" before you line up in the station: the line for the front does not have the opportunity to get as long.  Most rows had a 1-2 ride wait, while the front was only 4 rides.

MASTERPIECE! This is (as of July 30th) my #1 coaster, the pacing is unbeatable, it delivers so much ride in such a short amount of time, the ejector moments are insane, the first drop is soo good. The twisted double down is my single favorite element on any coaster, the ejector pop then, while still in the air, you get whipped sideways almost painfully in to the side of the car, then before you hit the bottom of your seat, you get ejected again! I don't know why people hate on the end of it, with the snappy zero g roll and powerful airtime hills, every part of this ride hits. Even the small 140ft drop is one of the best in the park. This ride is insane, the pacing is world class! MASTERPIECE!

I love, love, love Wildcat's Revenge!! My personal #1 coaster. The first drop is fantastic, the ejector airtime is great, the pacing is phenomenal, the underflip is amazing, and the whole layout is a masterpiece of thrill and intensity. It tries to kill you, but it never feels uncomfortable. RMC cooked with this one!

This was the first RMC I rode at currently sits at my #3 overall.  I was blown away by this ride and ended up going on it 4 times in a single day.  By converting Wildcat to Wildcat's Revenge, Hersheypark turned a terrible ride into an absolute masterpiece.  There are so many things to love about this ride.  The pacing and variety of elements are amazing.  It's a super aggressive, yet very smooth ride.  I also appreciate the updated lap bars with the nice big handles to hold onto.  This is easily Hersheypark's best ride.  While it still falls just a tad short of Steel Vengeance, it's still an incredible ride considering it's only about 1/2 as long as SteVe.

Nothing tops these RMCs, man.  They turned chicken shit into chicken salad.  Packs an amazing punch in a small package.  One of the few rides at Hershey Park that isn't a capacity disaster.  If you don't like this ride, we can never be friends.
This ride is perfect and is so smooth and still has so much intensity

Most balanced and best coaster at the park. It's got airtime, inversions, an amazing first drop, hangtime, and no dead space. I think the restraints are a little uncomfortable, but it doesn't stop this from being 5 stars.
oh wow

Constantly hyped as the BEST WOODEN COASTER EVER... and maybe it IS???? Certainly the best I have ridden so far. The first drop is amazing. And this has some of the strongest ejector airtime of any coaster I've ridden. In the back, it's powerful! Like your torso is about to rip off your hips, powerful. The layout is fantastic. The big airtime hills mixed with sudden and repeating direction changes and other surprises. Just an excellent experience overall. THAT SAID... man! Some parts were quite jarring and painful for me. Really rattled my head, neck, and back around. Enough that I needed some breaks. I could not marathon this thing. Remarkable coaster regardless.

My girlfriend is terrified of scary rides and anything she could get motion sick on or make her feel nauseous; so no inversions or generalized insanity. This was our first ride at SFGA and what an absolute madhouse of Gs and all types of force. I had a stomach after from the bar punching me in the stomach so hard during the ride, but my GF was fine.

Wow... El Toro, is a rough but awesome roller coaster. I came off this ride knowing it's my new number one coaster. This ride can be described with one word and the word is........ AIRTIME, and that's what I love about THE BULL so in my opinion it is the BEST coaster in the park.
Oh heck yeah! Pfabulous!

The "Bull" still delivers some of the most violent ejector airtime on the planet. The first two camelbacks and the "Rolling Thunder hill" are legendary for trying to launch you into the atmosphere. While it has developed some noticeable roughness and "potholes" in the turnaround, it remains a bucket-list wooden coaster for the sheer intensity of its drops

So many insane airtime moments throughout the entire ride. The ejector airtime over each hill feels like it is going to rip you in half depending on how fast the ride is running. The Rolling Thunder Hill is one of the standout moments of the ride; the negative G-forces are so insanely strong. Genuinely one of the best airtime moments I have ever experienced on a coaster.

I just recently returned to SFGAdv since Kingda Ka first opened and FINALLY got a chance to ride El Toro.  I had really been wanting to ride this to be able to compare to Skyrush and Steel Vengeance.  El Toro is every bit as good as it's hyped up to be.  The first drop is amazing.  The first half of the ride is loaded with strong ejector air time.  The last half is very forceful with its tight turns.  I would say the air time on El Toro is comparable to air time on Steel Vengeance.  It's both forceful and sustained.  I do think Skyrush has the overall strongest airtime with its low hills taken at high speeds.  Still, El Toro is truly a masterpiece.  It did have a little bit of roughness, but is still smoother than most wooden coasters I've been on.  I recommend getting a ride on this when it is warmed up.  My first ride was immediately after the ride opened.  The second ride was right before the park closed and it was a much faster and more intense ride.  The difference was significant.

Rode it in the fall and was told repeatedly by others that this thing absolutely COOKS in the summer months.  Thinking this could be a five-star under the right circumstances.  Nasty first drop, serious ejector time.  Will need more rides to accurately judge.  Not to be confused with Tor Johnson of MST3K fame.
Woah.

My rating is mostly because of the fact that I was completely stapled into my seat during my first and to this date, ONLY ride on this coaster. It was digging into my stomach the entire time and made the experience very uncomfortable. My stomach hurt for the rest of the day after that. The layout was good, but I would've enjoyed it more if I wasn't so uncomfortable.
A ride with great airtime and amazing restraints very intense but is very rattly. Just RMC it!!

What is by far the single greatest wooden roller coaster I have ever experienced in my entire life ever (Never ridden the Voyage btw), El Toro is a masterclass of mechanical engineering, and another fine work of 2000’s Intamin where they built these amazing, ultra intense machines. For as much praise as this coaster gets, it took a bit for it to click for me. Allow me to tell you the story of me and El Toro.
Before going to SFGAdv, one of the rides that I kept hearing about here besides Kingda Ka (R.I.P. 😭) was El Toro. I saw an immense amount of praise towards this coaster, and by watching videos it looked absolutely effing amazing. The way it tore through its hills looked unbelievable. I couldn’t wait to ride this coaster. Unfortunately, this was around 2022, when El Toro came off of two accidents, one in 2021 where the train derailed, and another in 2022 where it developed a nasty pothole that injured its riders. For a short period of time, I legitimately thought that this was the end of El Toro, and that it would be closed forever and I would never be able to ride it. Luckily, unlike what Cedar Point did with Top Thrill Dragster after its accident (R.I.P. my buddy 😭) Six Flags pursues through the hardships and fixed most of the problems with El Toro to keep it still running for a couple more years to come, at least until the men in suits at Cedar Flags decide to destroy another one of my favorite rides, and I would finally get to ride it on my trip to Six Flags Great Adventure in July 2023.
Now I was worried whether or not El Toro would actually be open for me along with Kingda Ka. Both rides were freakin’ open, and I had the chance to ride both. El Toro was the last coaster I rode the first day, and while I may gush over this coaster, that wasn’t how I felt at first. I sat in the middle of the train, and rode it, and at first I was a little disappointed. I still really liked it, but thought it didn’t quite hit that sweet spot for me. The first drop was great, the hills were great, and contrary to my initial concerns, that first ride was extremely smooth. But I felt like it was missing something to keep it from being extraordinary, and I vastly preferred Ka. However, we went again the next day, and since I got three more rides on Ka that day, we also got two more rides on El Toro, and both times I rode it that day really made it shine for me, and made it truly prove itself as one of the greatest rides I have ever ridden in my entire life. Like I said, the first drop is great. But man, that first drop is far more than great. Easily the single most powerful and stomach lifting first drop I’ve ever experienced on a rollercoaster ever, and it’s tied with Fury as my favorite coaster drop. The airtime you get on the two camelbacks and the rolling Thunder hill is absolutely incredible, and very powerful in the best way possible. While I didn’t list it as one of my pros, another major thing this ride has going for it is that it is INTENSE. Like, easily one of the most intense coasters I’ve ever been on in my life. It’s not quite on the same level as the Intamin Stratas or I305, but it’s definitely in my top 10, about equal to Maverick, and even more intense than any of the hybrid coasters that I’ve ridden, even including SteVe and Iron Gwazi. I mean, the G’s you get at the bottom of the hills are insane, I was genuinely being pushed forward because of how freaking intense it was, let alone all of this on a wooden coaster, it makes even more amazing. Not to mention just how freaking fast you tear through the wooden track on this ride! Holy crap is it aggressive in the best way possible, just like a bucking bull: Now while I didn’t list say my first ride the day before was smooth, I felt that these last two rides on it I took were a bit rougher, and I noticed some bumpiness. It’s weird, because the hills and stuff were butter smooth, but it was the twisty sections where I noticed the track grew a bit bumpy and beat me up a little. It was still perfectly tolerable, and in no way detracted from the awesomeness on this experience, but it is a shame that it has fallen into this state, especially since I heard it was completely glass smooth when it first opened back in 2006.
Regardless of some minor flaws, El Toro was still an absolute rush, and is easily one of the greatest rides I have ever ridden, and I forever thank God and my Dad for blessing me with the ability to go to this park to ride it and Kingda Ka. I still slightly preferred Ka, but that’s nothing against El Toro, it was more-so that I have a bit of a bias towards Ka, as I was able to relieve the childhood memories and joy from riding Top Thrill Dragster before it shut down. Unfortunately, as of August 16, 2026, I will never ride El Toro ever again, primarily because I will never ever visit that hellhole of a park ever again after what they did to Kingda Ka and my memories of Dragster 😭. I guess now this and Jersey Devil are really the only things this park now has going for it. While I will most likely never be able to ride this coaster ever again, I will never forget the amazing memories I spent riding it in the first place. It was an absolute rush unlike anything else I had ever ridden, and is still the most amazing wooden coaster so have ever seen in my entire life. It’s a massive shame the Intamin Prefab is extinct, as I genuinely believe there is a market still for it, and that the possibilities for this type of ride could make for some of the greatest rides ever in the modern industry. I guess like the hydraulic launch coasters, it just wasn’t meant to be, and unfortunately they’re on borrowed time. Thankfully, unlike Dragster and Kingda Ka, you can still ride this coaster and appreciate the amazing engineering that went behind making such a monstrous machine of mechanical engineering. While I may never ride it ever again, I will forever cherish the memories I had riding it while there, and I forever thank God for granting me the chance to ride it, and forever thank my Dad for bringing me there to fulfill that dream. As much as I hate to admit it, I fear this coaster may be on borrowed time. Once the merger happened, I knew Cedar Fair would sink their slimey little claws into Six Flags, and destroy Kingda Ka out of pure hatred and cowardice all because they think Top Thrill Dragster was the Satan of coasters 😔. I also feared that they would murder El Toro, and while it still exists even after some recent accidents, I am genuinely scared that it may be on borrowed time, and I dread the day this coaster will eventually meet its demise. I pray to God that doesn’t happen anytime soon, and that many enthusiasts still get the chance to experience this amazing ride. Until then, I will always cherish my three rides on this coaster, and I can confidently and proudly say that I tamed El Toro ❤️.

An absolute beast of a coaster. Extremely intense, with insane airtime and positive Gs. The launch doesn't have a massive initial kick, but it feels endless and build up a lot of speed. The pull up into the top hat is probably the worst part of the ride. It jackhammers about as much as Anubis the Ride's pull up. The top hat has some of the strongest sustained negative Gs that I've ever felt. The zero-G roll feels like Blue Fire's roll on steroids. It's extremely snappy and has a great pop of airtime. The immelmann has great positive G forces at its start and incredible airtime at its peak. The hill that follows has a great pop of ejector, and the cobra roll and vertical loop have insane positive G forces, to the point where you feel your feet tingling from all the blood being accumulated in your feet. The final airtime hills are just as insane as the rest of the layout. They're extremely abrupt and intense. Overall, Beyond the Cloud is one of the most intense coasters that I've ever ridden, second only to Eejanaika. It's short, yes, but it has an amazing layout that has zero dead spots, a layout that flows from element to element so quickly that it's hard to even know what's happening anymore. My only "gripes" with this coaster are its rattle which absolutely CAN give you a headache, and its very slow, single train operations. Despite these small flaws, this is without a doubt my second favorite coaster. Absolute Mackprodukt.

Beyond the Cloud completely lived up to the hype for me. The launch felt ridiculously powerful, especially because it throws you straight into the huge top hat almost immediately. The speed over the top combined with the view made it feel way more intense than I expected. The ride’s pacing was nonstop too — there was basically no dead moment once the launch started. The zero-g roll felt smooth, the immelmann gave insane hangtime, and the cobra roll threading through the vertical loop looked absolutely crazy from both on and off the ride. The lap bars also made the airtime stronger than I thought it would be.
During my visit specifically, I got really lucky because the ride was hauling after it warmed up later in the day. My night ride ended up being the best ride of the day since the lights around the park made the launch feel even faster. The operators were also dispatching trains super quickly for most of the afternoon, which kept the line moving better than expected.
There were still a few annoying things during my visit though. The ride went down for technical issues for around 15 minutes while I was already in line, and after it reopened the queue suddenly got way more crowded. I also noticed a slight rattle near the pull into the top hat on one of my rides that gave me a bit of a headache afterward, although it wasn’t terrible. The speakers in the queue area also kept cutting in and out during the day.
Universal pros: incredible launch, elite pacing, strong hangtime, smooth lap-bar restraints, unique intertwined inversions, and an overall world-class layout. The coaster also looks amazing visually, especially the massive top hat.
Universal cons: occasional roughness in high-force sections, long wait times, and some elements — especially the cobra roll and vertical loop — are less intense than they look from off-ride.
Overall, Beyond the Cloud is easily one of the best launched coasters I’ve ever ridden, and it’s the kind of ride that immediately makes you want another lap as soon as you hit the brakes.

The ride ends with a 90° right turn into the brake run.                                                                        I was blown away by Superman. Although SeaWorld Abu Dhabi is not known for its ride collection, it is the home to one of the best multi-launch coasters in the world. Manta may be a ride simple in name and presentation, but it is a ride with an incredibly diverse layout that truly anyone can enjoy. It is not too intense, it is e lengthy experience and it was an incredible flow.

The entrance for Manta is tucked downstairs in the park and it is a small, but well-detailed queue. The day of my visit, Manta was a walk on all day and I was able to get many laps on the ride quickly across all the train. The loading procedure for this ride is interesting in a neutral sense. Groups would be grouped into the station but stand on a dot about 10-12 feet away from the actual chute for the row. We were only allowed to approach the chute once guests had exited the ride and procedurally the crew was methodical and consistent. While it did not matter due to the low demand for the attraction on the day I had visited, I can see how it could be a cause for operational concern on a busy day. Once the train is clear, the ride starts with a turn into the first launch alongside a tank with mantas swimming around. I particularly liked this tank as it is the same tank in the plaza for the ride’s entrance, allowing riders to see through to guests on the other side.

Launch one has a good kick to it, getting to speed quickly and into the first element. It is rather tame in the front, but in the back the drop off gives a nice moment of ejector airtime. The airtime hill and wave turn following give strong pops of ejector airtime as well across the train, but was noticeably stronger in the front row. It then flows into a quick s-bend and then the train gracefully glides through the corkscrew. There is a little bit of lateral force through the rotation and it is great how it wraps around rockwork. The rest of the first segment is a step down in intensity, focusing on rapid s-bends that still provide a fun side to side motion.

Launch two is the tamest of the launches, just being a boost to get over the hill following it. The airtime hill is very dependent on where riders sit. The front row gets a strong moment of airtime at the crest and the back row follows going over the hill. However, the middle rows do not get much airtime with a decent float at best. The following sequence is great with a snappy S-Hill into a cutback that gives a good amount of hangtime prior to diving into a low heartline roll. The roll is really good with a great roll rate that has a moment of laterals similar to the roll on VelociCoaster, but it does not quite reach that level of intensity. The twisted double down into launch three is milder, giving a sense of weightlessness but nothing I’d consider to be airtime.

Launch three has a good punch to it and the element after it is fantastic in the front. The twisted crest gives a strong pop of ejector airtime and laterals that really throws riders around. In other rows the element is not as strong, but nevertheless it marks the start of one of the best paced segments on any roller coaster. The Zero-G Stall is quick and has a whip in the entry and exit that creates a wonderful wiggle effect going through it, similar to how VelociCoasters feels but about a second shorter. It then charges through the overbank and twists into a barrage of small hills and tight banked turns that give a succession of small pops of airtime into positive forces while navigating around some scenery. It ends the ride in a satisfying sequence of being tossed around in a wild yet controlled manner. It is far from the most intense roller coaster in the world, let alone on Yas Island, but it is easily the most fun I have had on a coaster across the Yas Island Resort.

The perfect wooden coaster!
