Absolutely fucking incredible. The best wooden coaster ever constructed. Perfect terrain usage by the Gravity Group allowing for one of the longest ride durations out there ALSO paired with completely relentless pacing. This ride is so long that it is exhausting to marathon, as you are constantly being thrown around by the aggressive airtime and laterals while simultaneously being battered by the wooden track. Diving into the layout, Voyage is truly a 3-in-1 experience, beginning with a large first drop for a wooden coaster and multiple large B&M hyper-esque hills that provide great sustained floater airtime. The following section has been dubbed the "spaghetti bowl", which stays low to ground with quick pops of airtime and great laterals. Until this point, the train has been traveling up a hill while managing to keep its momentum. Downright masterful. The final section is the return run, where the train begins flying back down the hillside following the midcourse. I don't even mind the midcourse on this ride since the train gains its speed back so fast. Insane engineering. At this point you truly begin wondering if this ride will ever end. As the train makes its way towards the final brake run, the interactions with the station and thanksgiving area of the park are incredible, as the train flies all around the station area. As for how Voyage runs, the staff at Holiday World maintains the ride spectacularly. The ride consistently has the PERFECT amount of wooden coaster bite, contributing to a texture that adds an additional layer of aggression. With regards to the setting, the location is simply immaculate, as the layout is so secluded out in the woods. This allows for what is probably the most religious coaster experience on Earth, a night ride on the Voyage. I myself am yet to experience a night ride on this beast (not a beast reference), but from what I hear it is absolutely pitch black throughout the ride. Being tossed around on a woodie in the dark is just other worldly. Attending the premier coaster enthusiasts' event, HoliWood Nights, allows you to experience TRIMLESS night rides on Voyage, which are just absolutely demented, as the ride highballs it through the final third of the ride. All in all, this is a perfect ride and the epitome of what a wooden roller coaster should be. My #1 for a reason.
This ride is a work of art! No wasted track, everything has a purpose!
Best coaster in the world

What can I say that hasn't already been said?
Voyage is incredible, the combination of length, variety of forces, and location out in the woods makes it one of a kind and one of the best coasters ever built.
Strong airtimes, especially during the first half. Second half has less intense airtimes, but a ton of high speed banking. A masterpiece
This coaster is absolutely incredible. Riding it 5 times in one day has solidified it as my favorite wooden roller coaster.

Never was able to get a trimless ride at HWN but even a trimmed ride on this kicks butt, it regains its pace so fast after the midcourse and somehow feels more intense than the first half. My only minor complaints are that it is slightly rough especially in the back row and the first couple drops are only moderate floater airtime but those are very minor gripes compared to the greatness that is this ride.

This ride grew on my a lot. I rode it in the front and then back mostly keeping my hands up, but it was actually a bit too aggressive and kinda hurt how it yanks you around. But I rode it for the third time in the front row while it was lightly raining, and I actually held in for most of the ride, and that ride was incredible. Voyage is basically perfect for what it is trying to do: a long, aggressive, airtime-filled layout through the woods. Hopefully I can ride it trimless some day, but it goes hard even with the trims.

Over a mile of pure insanity. Makes incredible use of the terrain to keep so much of its speed, its still flying even as you approach the breaks. Great floater airtime on the camelbacks going out, and then insane ejector the rest of the way, especially in the triple down and the masterpiece of a finale coming back to the station.
When trimless Voyage at night walks in

It’s the Voyage, it’s fast, long, airtime-packed, long, buried in the woods, long, pretty rough, did I mention that it’s long? The PTC trains aren’t great to begin with, but the natural roughness honestly grows on me each time I ride this lengthy beast. If you do want a smoother ride, train A, at least for now, is far smoother. Despite the few flaws, the Voyage is still one of the longest, and the single best wooden coaster around.

The Voyage is a monstrously large woodie. The first drop and airtime hill are incredibly smooth; Gravity Group & Holiday World have done an excellent job with the constant retracking. It goes on and on feeling like it will never come to an end. The best part was the aggressive triple down in the second half underground. Some parts had a nasty vibration including the bottom of the triple down and a couple of overbanked turns. It would be a top 5 coaster for me if those transitions were smoother.

World-class airtime and laterals delivered with a purpose. Flawlessly executes maneuvers a pre-RMC wooden coaster has no business doing. My only nitpick is that it's kind of thematically redundant with the rest of the Thanksgiving area given how much there is to work with for the holiday as a whole, but that's not really the coaster's fault.
Literally just a combination of the beast and el toro
SAVE ARIE AT ALL COSTS!!!
Loved ArieForce. My #2 overall. Sucked riding in the back when a guy with a pocket full of quarters rode and I got pelted with quarters the whole time. Not the rides fault. 10/10
yeehaw

Edit: it is such a shame that fun spot is closing and there is a real chance that this ride gets torn down 😭😭😭. I’m praying for it to get relocated to a different park because this ride deserves to be saved!!! I’m hoping Carowinds buys it. Arie force one will be severely missed. So long.                    

We drove 2 hours out of our way to ride this coaster and my god was it worth it. Great drop, the raven truss dive gave an awesome floater sensation in the back row, the stall lasts foooreever and the hills after that are so strong that my thighs hurt. The “arcade” roll was amazing and gave lots of whip and the second roll was almost as good. Many people complain about the end, but in my opinion it’s awesome, yes it hurts but in such a good way. Back to back to back to back insane ejector hills all the way into the strong breaks. It’s so worth the trip, 12/10. Better than steel vengeance.

I have never experienced a ride that has made me laugh so much. It’s the equivalent, for a grown man, of being a baby thrown in the air by your dad.
The park itself is dire. But Arie Force One was a walk-on and I got to ride it repeatedly in different seats.

MUST SAVE ArieForce One:

ArieForce One is a roller coaster that simply should not exist. It's a true unicorn. A world-class, headline-grabbing, top-rated mad masterpiece of engineering and fright plopped into the painfully underwhelming Fun Spot America Atlanta. How? Why? What was the actual plan here? Was it that adding a world class RMC build would boost attendance enough to build up the rest of the park? Because the park (not horribly small in terms of acres - it's probably large enough to support a lot of growth) has very few rides and those that exist are of the county fair variety and are set so far apart that huge sections of the park feel abandoned. But above all this towers ArieForce. Again. Why?

It really is like finding a four-star restaurant in the middle of a food court. But it is found and appreciated. So much so that a 1600-mile trip (pilgrimage maybe?) made some sort of deluded sense. Worth it?  Well, the first hill is absolutely awe-inspiring. As the train climbs higher and higher, you get a moment to appreciate just how absurdly large this coaster is compared to its surroundings. Then the drop arrives, and from that point the only thoughts I had were of survival. Any calm reflection or idle wondering immediately gives way to the purest of adrenaline hits. From that point forward, ArieForce One barely seems interested in anything other roller coaster have done. It attacks the layout with a relentless energy as if it's trying to shake the rider off it's back.

Aside from the hills and the pace, what makes the ride especially memorable are its freakish inversions. They're a fascinating mix of thrilling and unpleasantly disorienting. They're not always graceful, but they're certainly unforgettable, and they give the coaster a personality unlike anything else I've ridden.

In fact, ArieForce One honestly feels like the execs at RMC just handed the project to some talented but obnoxiously overconfident junior designer and said, "Fine, let's see all those great ideas you keep talking about." It's as if, tired of hearing complains that nobody would listen to their revolutionary concept, they just let them loose on a random park in not-doing-so-well Fayetteville, Georgia. The result is this gloriously over-the-top coaster packed with elements that really feel just a little too wild, just a little too ambitious. And that's... okay. As I rode this on Independence Day with my family, I was proud that something as unique as ArieForce exists and that we could experience it on the 250th Anniversary of America. It is daring and flawed and unique as heck and all the more wonderful because of it.

Perhaps the highest compliment I can give ArieForce One is that it is one of the only truly frightening roller coasters I've ridden. Not because it feels unsafe (although it does), but because it constantly pushes beyond what you expect a coaster to do with only lower restrains. No over the shoulder and so even as an experienced/old enthusiast, there were moments when I genuinely wasn't sure it was actually safe to ride. That's incredibly rare. 

It's also impossible to talk about ArieForce One without feeling sad. Fun Spot America Atlanta is scheduled to close for good this summer. It was stunningly obvious that the park had a destination coaster but was in need of almost everything else. But you never want to see a park close. I am certain that Fun Spot Atlanta was the first park (or favorite park) of many people. The magic of amusement parks is that they don't have to be great parks to be great to people. Some of my best park memories were of the now gone Conneaut Lake Park. Small, only one marquee ride - the venerable Blue Streak - but a thousand years ago it was one of the keystones of my summer. For many of us, our local parks are not the biggest, flashiest, or most polished destinations, but they nevertheless give us something extraordinary. 

And speaking of the park, a real shout out and thanks to the crew at Fun Spot. Everyone we encountered was pleasant on the bewilderingly (to a northerner, anyway) hot and humid day at a park that was about to close for good. And that isn't a small thing. 

But back to coasters. Is A-F-1 the most audacious roller coasters in America? Possibly. But does ArieForce One stand out as proof that amazing experiences can emerge from the most unexpected places. Absolutely... Just... Absolutely.

The juxtaposition of this coaster with the rest of the park is WILD. Walking around the nearly empty park with small flat rides everywhere, and then seeing this $12M steel monstrosity is something else. The coaster is absolutely fantastic. The stall, the big outward banked turn, and the double-up into the arcade roll are the standout moments for me. Another standout moment is when you're enjoying yourself and ArieForce One punches you in the stomach... aka, the brake run. As a tall guy, the quad down also got to be pretty uncomfortable after 10+ rides, but it is a great finale. Doesn't top Gwazi for me, but it's an amazing ride.

Is it a bird? Is it a plane? No, it's ArieForce One, swooping down from the cosmos and delivering a ride experience worth every single penny of park admission, and it's an honest shame that such a fantastic ride has to close. Every element hits you with as much force as a bullet train at max velocity. The airtime absolutely delivers and is hands down some of the best in the world. I don't know what Mr. Arie was thinking when he decided to erect a world-class Rocky Mountain Construction beast in a park where the next best ride was a Hi-Miler that was arguably one of the rattliest experiences ever, but I digress. Somehow, despite this ride being the one good reason to visit the park, me and my family made it all the way down from northwestern Pennsylvania to Fayetteville, Georgia to pay our respects. I rode four times, once in the back, once in the middle, and twice in the front. I went in the middle for my first time, and this was not the best way to ride, even though it was still extraordin-ARIE. I can't decide whether the front or the back is better, because they both were incredible. The back gave the best airtime and the front felt faster. Don't get me wrong, though, both are great. They also crammed some surprisingly decent theming in there. The ride experience and layout were top-tier and amazing. From the start, you're greeted with some small hills. These hills aren't too strong, unless you ride in the back, but they do offer some airtime. You then go up the chainlift and if you turn your head around, you get a stunning view of the park, or lack thereof. Once you get to the top, you are confronted with an intense 146-foot straight-down drop. This drop offers some nice floater airtime on the way down. You are then pitted face-to-face against the terrifying Raven Truss Dive, an inversion consisting of a small outer-bank turn, a dizzying flip upside down, and then a half loop inside of a big white truss, giving an insane rip-your-pants head-chopper effect. The ride then tries to kill you with an endless zero-g stall (the longest in the world, as a matter of fact) and a diabolical outer-banked airtime hill that both gives some of the best airtime in the world and washes any doubts you had about the ride down your neighbor's cistern. The ride then throws a double-up airtime hill (ejectors galore), a head-slicing Arcade Roll (an unprecedented roll that goes right over the arcade. Who knew?), a 'fakey' airtime hill (a sort of outerbank with some excellent negatives), a forceful turn, and then a similar roll right above the grass. These inversions are unique and creative, and are by far the best  of all time, bar none. After these mind-numbing elements, you rush into the famous quad down, negative g-force aplenty. These four hills give you ejectors so undeniably groovy that you slam into the lap bar at full force, and it hurts so bad but the airtime is so good that it hardly matters. I got unfixable bruises from this element and I do not regret it one bit. After that, you go up a larger hill that also offers some revolution-ARIE airtime. The emergency brakes are pulled and you slow down to a halt. I had the pleasure of meeting the YouTubers behind Coaster Spectrum after I got off, and they were super friendly and they genuinely seemed like they were nice people. I had fun lapping this without too much of a wait, even though it was the Fourth of July and it was blazing hot. I can see why the park is closing, but even so it's always sad to see any park get the axe. I had a fantastic day at Fun Spot, with ArieForce, Hurricane, and the two go-kart tracks I went on, Victory Lap and Road Runner (unfortunately Samson was closed) being the highlights of the day, even though ArieForce was the best. It's not every day that I give a coaster the 'Masterpiece' tag, but this one absolutely deserves it. Hopefully this coaster finds a new home in a different park, where it can see new and old riders soar again on this top-tier attraction. So respect, salute, and goodbye to the best coaster I'll never ride again. There has never been, there is not, and there will never be a coaster quite like ArieForce One. Edit: It happened. Fun Spot Atlanta is now closed for good. ArieForce One is now standing unused in basically a parking lot in Fayetteville. Let's hope that this intense combination of great elements finds a new home in another park someday. I've seen a video that said that the CEO of Enchanted Parks was seen inspecting the ride, so my hopes are high that Michigan's Adventure or Worlds of Fun buy the ride, and this insane creation can ride again.

Uh oh.  Fun Spot Atlanta just announced that it's closing in August 2026. (This place is basically a county fair, and I never understood why an elite coaster was built here.)  I hope another park adopts this awesome RMC.  I live in Missouri, so I'd love to see it land in STL or KC.  Both parks could use a signature ride like AF1.  Anyway, it's a phenomenal coaster with relentless insanity.  There are so many great moments, but that arcade barrel roll is incredible and is my #1 favorite inversion.  FYI - The ride ops won't staple you unless you request it.  I stapled myself once, and the airtimes were unpleasant.  However, with a slightly loose seat belt and the lap bar an inch or two above the thighs, the airtimes/ejectors are phenomenal.  I thought the ending quad-down was going to be "too much of a good thing," but I was wrong.  I love that finale, especially in the back!   Also, front seat after dark is amazing.  I may have to make a special trip to Atlanta to experience AF1 again in case it doesn't get relocated.

Made the last day, last-minute trip for my son, who's been kicking himself ever since he skipped out on Kingda Ka. Loved the inversion just after the initial drop and the fact I could ride hands up for the entirety without second guessing myself. So smooth. 

I mentioned to my son after braking that I forgot to take motion sickness pills before riding and we both said in unison, "Who cares!", then high fived. Hoping for this comes back sooner than later.

Incredible coaster and probably my favorite RMC for however long it lasts. That amazing outward banked hill into the double-up into the arcade roll is up there with the best sequences ever designed on a roller coaster. Airtime on the dive loop is much better in the front while everything else is slightly stronger towards the back. Got nothing but zen rides on Arie for three hours on a 2026 summer day - probably a telling sign that this park was on its last legs. Praying Arie finds a home somewhere - it would be almost unprecedented for something this good that's still squarely in its prime not to survive.
Highly recommend riding in a downpour, hilarious experience getting thrown every which way while getting waterboarded. 11/10
This ride is perfect
I got bruises on my thighs from riding this 10 times :)

Flew all the way from Boston to ride this before it closed. Absolute masterpiece. Good airtime going into raven truss dive. Awesome zero g stall. The 3-element combo of the outer bank to the double up to the arcade roll is insanity. And the quad down at the end is brutal.
Perfect RMC. The Quad Down didn’t bother me. Got 13 rides.

Welp, that's another one in the books. It's a shame that this has to go, but you have to admire Arie for trying. I mean, the man spent tens of millions and burnt a 35 year old park into the ground to get his name on a coaster, and he somehow made it worth it. Three years of Fun Spot Atlanta being on a map is worth thirty where Dixieland sat around getting older thanks to this ride. The best parking lot coaster that we're ever gonna see.

If there ever was a perfect coaster, it would be this one. Arie truly pushes the boundaries of the intensity limit while providing a ride as smooth as silk. There isn’t a moment of dead time on the entire thing - every second is elite. Purposeful and methodical in its pacing and layout. So much variation between how each element feels. I am beyond lucky, grateful, and sad that I got to ride this marvel of engineering only a few weeks before it’s gone forever. I’ll be chasing the feeling that this coaster gave me for the rest of my life. Rest in peace.

i have no clue how this thing is legal. one of the most psychotic roller coasters i've ever been on in my life. everything this ride does, from its airtime to its inversions, is seemingly done in the most bonkers way possible. its also just insane to me that this incredible coaster is at this dinky FEC that also happens to be my home park LMAO

This ride is almost perfect. It’s got airtime, hangtime, the arcade roll, and that ending is very similar to the ending on Magnum only more painful. Please let this masterpiece be relocated and not scrapped.
The embodiment of a perfect ride. Great pacing and every element hits. Ejector is some of the strongest on any RMC. Outerbanked hill is insane lateral airtime into a seat slam.

How the heck did Fun Spot of all chains get this top tier RMC? It’s super well paced, super whippy, and super fun. The only possible con is that those last few bunnyhops make your legs feel broken, but it was the best coaster in Georgia until the park shut its gates yesterday. I don’t have as many rides as some others do, but I’d say 23 total is enough to have a solid opinion and to miss this ride already.
I love every part of this ride. The raven truss dive took me by surprise, and the zero-G stall was absolutely fantastic. The airtime on this coaster is relentless, and it's easily my number one.

One of the most insane coasters I have ever ridden and I don't think very much will ever top it. I expected a very Wildcat's Revenge like experience and it over delivered in the best way possible. The drop is great and is somehow overshadowed by other parts of the ride. The raven truss dive is snappy especially in the back row when you get pulled down through the element. The sped hill provided an amazing pop of RMC ejector and the stall felt like nothing else I had ever experienced on an RMC. It felt more drawn out than something like Wildcat's Revenge but still provide some nice snaps entering and exiting the stall and the hangtime while you are up there is so good as a you feel like you're hanging forever. 

After the stall is what I say is the second half of the ride and the better half if you ask me! The outer bank turn is extremely strong and sustained with an amazing mix of ejector and laterals all at the same time. Like the outer bank, the double up is also very sustained, particularly when you drop down into the arcade roll. Speaking of the arcade roll, WOW! It met my expectations with how fast you take that element and the insane whip you get as you take on the roll! Then you come to the turn in before the barrel role and it is absolutely the most intense moment on any RMC G-force wise. It is so freakishly insane I can't put into words! From here you proceed to snap through the barrel role just like the arcade roll and enter what is one of the great sequences of airtime hills on any coaster besides maybe Steel Vengeance in some circumstances. The five airtime hills are crazy, insane, and any other word to describe how wild this sequence is! The ejector on these hills is unlike anything on any other coaster anywhere and the strength of the airtime is amazing and perfect! Then to top off the amazing ride experience, you get one last ejector pop before SLAMMING into the break run. 

This is by far one of the greatest coasters ever built with how strong each element is and the pacing is some of the best as well! Overall, I don't think many other coasters will top ArieForce One and I hope one day we see this ride end up at another park for the world to experience!

After the Lech Coaster, which was a little bit too agressive for my tastes, Vekoma fully delivers with this coaster. The front gives you a milder ride with floating airtime while the back delivers some good ejector airtime. Great first drop, wonderful hangtime in the following inversion. Some snatchy twists and turns, an inversion through the station and fun, fun, fun. Your daddy will also like this.

probably the smoothest coaster i have ridden, 
very good layout and inversions,specially the one into the station overall a perfect ride.
in my opinion with the lap bar instead the vest restrains this would be even better

It's smooth, it's fun, is not too intense and it's pretty long. Super approved! One thing that I'm sorry for are the restraints, I truly believed that with lap bars this coaster could have been so much better
It was amazing
I my top ten . CRAZY!!!! If you haven't rode it. YOU SHOULD!!!!

What an amazing ride, the pacing is incredible, not a dull moment from start to end. It's smooth, intense, fun and filled with air at almost every element. Worth the trip to Northern Denmark by itself.
This is a smooth ride with wonderful moderate forces.
why the firebird green

A masterpiece by Vekoma and Farup. A well designed layout that flows very well and is filled with airtime. Love the inversions. The first one has nice hang time and a twisty pullout. The second inversion is stupid fast and the third is a fun station fly-by. The trains are super comfy, yes the vests take away some of the airtime but it doesn't really bother me to much. The ride has a nice length and a very high re-ride ability (had 17 rides in and still wanted more!). A class standout coaster for this amazing park! Best coaster in Denmark no question.
Literally a perfect ride, and a perfect blend between a looping coaster and an airtime-focused coaster

Fønix is a good coaster for this park i grow up 30 minutes away from Fårup i i loved this from when i first rode it. I have not been to any park outside of Denmark yet but i still think Fønix will be one of my top coasters

This is such a fun coaster. It's glass smooth with a great layout. The barrel roll through the station was a highlight. The staff even sprayed the train and guests with water as you rode the ride! Definitely worth riding.

What a wonderful ride: glossy smooth, fun inversions, great pacing and bucketloads of airtime! Additionally the corkscrew through the station is a cool gimmick (better cover your ears when waiting in the station, it can be VERY loud!), the trains are very comfortable and the optical presentation of this massive coaster is also fantastic: the wooded area looks great and the color scheme is just beautiful. What is not to love about Fønix?

At last, I got my first ride on a Vekoma MK1101. A moment I've been eagerly waiting for. Luckily, Fønix did not disappoint. 
The drop is amazing, the stall-loop delivers some hangtime and even the tophat-like element afterwards delivers airtime. One of the standout elements is the rapid heartline roll afterwards which is easily the best one I have done so far as it repeatedly left me dizzy. The remaining layout is mostly made up by floajector and ejector airtime hills, I'd wish for a little bit more variety here. Being a Vekoma nex-gen looper, Fønix of course features a station-fly-through element, a great heartline-roll/corkscrew.
Without a doubt, Fønix is the best roller coaster in Denmark and I can't wait to experience more Vekoma next-gens.
Oh and not to forget: Fønix is laughably smooth.

Smooth aa butter, airtime, hangtime, compact layout with no dead spots, the roll through the station... only thing that would make this better is lapbars instead of the annoying harness. Amazing ride, 100% my thing.

Up front its near perfect, all airtime hilld slap, the first 2 inversions are great, and alot of airtime moments. Both ejector and floater. Only forceless element is the roll through the station, but that has headchoppers

However up back its ALOT less intense. The first airtime hill doesn't hit like at all, and the second and third inversions do absolutly nothing force wise

I went to this park with mixed expectations for this coaster but actually, this thing is much better than expected. Allthough I have to mention I haven't got the chance to ride Lech Coaster yet, this thing is really well balanced. Most prominent is the airtime which you'll get throughout the whole lay-out. I also love the three inversions and where they're located. It is a pity that Vekoma still uses vest restraints on most of their thrill coasters, but they didn't bother me that much. Also, with two train operations and stacking right before the station (not the final brakerun) capacity isn't an issue, either. It's not the most extreme coaster out there, but one everyone can enjoy multiple times and I think it's the perfect addition for Fårup Sommerland and the best rollercoaster in Denmark for sure.

Fønix is just a masterpiece, its so smooth so much airtime. 3 incredible inversions. its got straight, twisted and outerbanked airtime. its not too intense but thats what i like. so incredibly reridable. and i dont think the trains are too bad either. the plaza is also beutiful. and it fits so well in fårups line-up. for me its a easy 9/10 if the airtime would be a bit stronger, more intense and more theming it would easily be my number 1
Not as intense as Lech, but very re-rideble. I loved this coaster, for me a masterpiece bye Vekoma.

Incredible airtimes in the front and back. I have to admit that the front row was more fun imo, but the drop was way more violent in the back. I understand why some people might think that it’s not intense enough, but I think it’s perfect and it actually has some forceful moments. The immelmann stall inversion after the drop was stunning and the other inversions had some very good hangtime too. The pace was amazing and the train runs very smooth and fast later in the day through its layout. Absolute perfection on that scale

This ride delivers ejector airtime at the whole time. When there is no airtime, you will experience awesome inversions. The corkscrew through the station, a Immelmann as a 0g-Stall and a highspeed heartline roll. All 3 are very well placed. What should be said, that only 3 of 13 airtime moments are classic straight bunnyhills. All other are waveturns, off-axis or twisted hills. So the ride has a great variarty.
Holy cow, that's a ride. 100% adrenaline, but butter smooth.

Fonix is an amazing ride that delivers in almost every way. It’s got a great first drop, lots of airtime moments, some fantastic inversions, and overall a great layout. However, I do have two small gripes about Fonix. First off, it focuses much more on airtime, and it hardly has any intense moments during the entire ride. Second, even though it’s the tallest in Denmark, a lot of the ride’s elements take place low to the ground with small pops of airtime that don’t really provide the punch I look for. But I can look past those two things and come to the realization that Fonix is an outstanding ride and one of the best in Denmark.

Oh Boy, Where should I start with this ride. Fønix is an absolutely fantastic ride experience starting with a great drop and delivering all the way through, as it should be. Once again Benjamin Bloemendaal shows how he is a true expert at his craft and proves that a fantastic coaster neither has to be tall nor launched. It does leave off where lech coaster started, however, not quite as intense, which I think is a shame. The complete package works really well though and is just incredible fun. A shame it has vests though :(

I came to Denmark for the first time to ride this beast! It was exactly how I was expecting. Very smooth, fun. I loved the stall loop - that was my favourite part. Even with just lap bar without vest it would be even better. But Vekoma did vests looser than on older coaster like Formula on Energylandia, so it was not a big deal. It is not as good as Lech coaster, it misses some intensity, but it is amazing coaster. Also very reridable.

Objectively, a really really good roller coaster, especially on a technological basis. Subjectively, not a big fan. There is not a single outstanding element imo, besides maybe one airtime hill that might be too extreme already and the rattle is unbearable. I did have some rides where I was spared but most of my rides were pretty exhausting to a point where I was physically incapable of continuing to ride any big coaster that day on top of having a headache and feeling dizzy. I will give it the benefit of a doubt for the moment.
Lukas Metzger and Patrick Marx carried

Inner seats? Amazing. Outer seats? Better hold on. Got a few more rides on this now, and I can now say I like most of Voltron's layout (but especially the launch, the first half and the beginning of the second half). Its diverse, interesting and has many great elements. But the last few elements right before the ride ends drag down my rating quite a bit. They are too rattly, uncomfortable and forceful, ending in a headache during hot days.

After just one year of operation, this coaster already exhibits excessive rattling, which is quite disappointing. In 2025, we expect a smoother ride, especially from a renowned manufacturer like Mack Rides. While the coaster delivers impressive G-forces, the vibrations significantly detract from the overall experience. This level of roughness is unacceptable and needs to be addressed to meet modern standards of comfort and enjoyment.

Voltron Nevera is an absolute beast of a coaster, yeah it is quite rough in the three times that I've been on it, but nonetheless the theming is world class, it's insanely intense with the best airtime and hangtime I've experienced, except for the roughness it's well over comfortable, the launches are very powerful especially the triple launch, the pacing is incredible (keeps going without a stop), the music is insane and the storytelling as well. The only thing that I would suggest is onboard audio and make it possible that every train is smooth so that everyone has an insane ride. Masterpiece of a creation

This coaster is a masterpiece in engineering - a showcase of what Mack Rides is capable of. A moving platform in the station, up to 7 trains on the track at the same time, a surprise effect before the launch, lots of different ride elements. There is also very good theming in the queue line and the station. The downside for me: Way too much ejector, the ride reels off the various ride figures far too quickly one after the other. It is a "Jack of all trades" - but "Master of none". E.g. there is a vertical launch - but the one on Wicked is much better. There is a zero stall, but it is short. There is a shuttle launch section, but it is no comparison to Toutatis. There are dives and tight turns near to the ground, but there are other coaster which do this much better. And so on.

I rode it about 10 times over 2 days, and the experience was incredibly hit or miss. With some trains, the ride can be immensely rattly and uncomfortable, but on a good train the ride is pure joy. The hangtime is unlike any other I’ve tried, the launches are snappy, and the seats (when in a good train) are some of the best. A minor negative is that the ride feels a bit long, and the pacing falls off toward the final third.
Really fun coaster, just not tippy top tier for me. Also a very noticeable rattle

Overhyped and underwhelming..
As a season pass holder we couldn't wait for Voltron. The fear of the Mack rattle was always there while construction. But it is worse then expected. The middleseats are bearable and pretty ok. On the wing you get off the ride like you have been in a ring fight. 
It is not that the two other big dippers are anyway better. But they are way shorter and not as intense.

It's not a bad coaster by any means, i will give it another chance in three weeks. Just not what you expect from a coaster opening in 2024.
Right now my top coaster in the park is still Wodan.
3 stars in an outside seat, 5 in an inside seat.

As already said in other reviews, the theming is fantastic, the dispatch is surprisingly very efficient, and the profusion of details all along the queue line makes you forget that you have to wait for at least 40 minutes, you hardly ever stop walking for more than 30 seconds in the line.
And you don't see time passing by.
It's very immersive and well done, the animatronic is absolutely stunning, and the show with the electricity that occurs every 15/20 minutes is pure genius.

I was looking forward to riding this wonder, and came back to Europa park especially for Voltron, 2 months after my first visit.
I had high expectations, and they were fulfilled, except for a few details, not a big deal anyway.
I was tense and excited, and didn't expect such an energetic and relentless ride! 
I hyped myself by watching the official teasing videos and the ones published by YouTubers.
The vertical launch is out of this world, so unique, and the layout is punchy all the way.
The only moment you can breathe is on the turntable (crazy element!), hearing this magnificent soundtrack for a short while.

The layout is nothing like I have ever experienced before, it features airtime, hang time, laterals, and absolutely mad G's inside the helix. 

Rode it 6 times, and we got the non-rattly and the rattly trains. 
Some really have an uncomfortable rattle.
I hope that this will be fixed by the park, as i read that they are doing some experiments on the trains.
And it does make a difference, particularly on the outer seats, which are a bit more challenging than the ones in the middle. Not for the faint at heart, it's a bit uncomfortable! But packs a lot of intensity!

In a nutshell, it's a wonderful ride, my #4, I highly recommend to ride it if you fancy intensity, and really well themed attractions. One of the most beautifully themed I've seen.
A must ride for any enthusiast, anyway! 
I must say that I have a plus for Toutatis, which is punchy, intense, but smooth when it's been heated all day long, on back and front seats.
I never felt any discomfort riding it, it's so reridable (4 times in a row yesterday, and 3 more during the day) and it remains my #1 for the moment, after a good 80 rides on it or so.
Just behind Toutatis, I rank ride to happiness and Eejanaika, Voltron, Taron and F.L.Y.

Although I love Voltron, here are the cons : 
Didn't get the teasing tremors before the launch, as seen on some videos, and I was a bit disappointed about that, but it's not a big deal, maybe the park decided to inhibit this system due to technical issues, I don't know. 
Just after Eejanaika, Voltron is the most intense rollercoaster I've ever ridden.
It doesn't prevent the ride from being one of the best machines in Europe right now.
Loved it and would reride it for sure.
Its flaws are minor.
The lightning effect before the launch is fabulous! 
I recommend to go and experience Voltron by yourselves!

I enjoyed Voltron, but only if I tightly grabbed the restraint.  If I relaxed or put my hands up, the lap bar punished my thighs on the airtimes and inversions.  It doesn't help that ride ops staple you.  Also, the layout felt kind of choppy, like they wanted to cram lots of crazy elements into a compact space but didn't think about how those elements would flow together.   Overall, it's a unique ride with great hangtimes, launches and pace.  I just wish I didn't have to ride it so defensively.  As for the oft-mentioned rattle, my 5 rides in various seats were smooth.

This is easily the best coaster at Europa Park. It's awesome, something new and especially the first half of the ride feels very well composed. I love the non-stop intensity, the ejector airtimes and the variety of maneuvers. 

The inner seats deliver a much more enjoyable ride than the outer ones. On the outer seats the train rattles so much it destroys the experience almost completely.

The reliability is awful. The ride broke down several times. It shouldn't happen this often after being one year in operation by its manufacturer.

The theming is excellent and the ride feels very well centered around it.

Overall, this is an excellent rollercoaster that brings variety in terms of elements, has outstanding theming and delivers a very good ride experience (except for rides on the outer seats, they are atrocious).

Absolutely insane coaster. I didn't find it particularly rough but I usually did have a headache for 5-10 minutes after riding it. I don't know what caused it because i've never had it on any other ride. If not for that this would be 5/5.

Inner seats: great ride; many inversions and the turntable is really unique. 
Outer seats: Rattle. Ride is not so enjoyable on the outer seats. It ruins the ride.

The good things: It's intense, it's long, it has a lot of elements. But why does Mack the same design flaw, Gerstlauer does decades since? The combination of 4P-Rows and short trains imply a very discomfortable rattle on the outside seats. Yes, the whip is cool, but not at the costs of Rattle after two years of operation. Silver Star has as well a rattle on outside seats, but this coaster is 23y old. The long trains keep the rattle as well in an acceptable range. The theming is overall great, but the huge waiting hall is ways too loud with all the sound effects. I accept the good concept and the nice whippy Elements, but overall I'm a but disappointed.
Loved the new gimmicks they tried and the duration of it is good,has a good break in the middle but the last part gave me a headache for a few minutes and it had a bit of a rattle

An extremely intense coaster with a great and very long layout and really good theming in the queue/station. It's a masterpiece. But depending on your train/seat it can be too rattly, and either way this is one of the few coasters that I could never marathon re-ride, it's just too intense for that.
DAMMM SO GOOD!

Voltron is really a showpiece of everything Mack can do on a coaster. There's element after element and pretty much all of them offer something to the layout, quite an achievement on a coaster exceeding 4000ft. The launches are all excellent, really snappy, which is a pleasant change up from the usual Mack fare, which are fine but nowhere near as thrilling as Voltrons. The beyond vertical launch is very strange but good fun. All of the inversions are good without being necessarily outstanding, apart from the stall, which offers some extremely memorable hangtime. Every airtime hill is pretty crazy ejector, all of them are awesome but the Wave turn in the second half is by far the best, that really caught me off guard. The layout as a whole is also extremely intense, almost too intense for my preference really, but if you're a fan of intense rides then voltron is going to deliver, the helix at the end is bone crushing. You experience all this in the most comfortable trains in the business, Mack have nailed their lap bars and seats. Unfortunately the ride definitely has a rattle. It isn't too bad on most of the trains but a couple its much more pronounced. I think depending on your tolerance for that, you may be able to look past it entirely. For me, it took away from it just a bit but it didn't stop Voltron from being a truly epic coaster. It's definitely one of the best rides in Europe and whilst it's not a ride I can hammer out laps on because of the intensity, it's certainly a coaster I would travel back to Europa Park for, even without Wodan and the fact that it's the best park going. Top, top coaster

The layout, the area, the launch, the build up in the station. All good things that make this a great ride. The first thing I enjoyed was the area around it. The way this coaster looks is amazing! Then you have the waiting line which has a great theming. The show you have with the spools on the roof cought my be surprise! The ride itself fullfills the hype that build up in de waiting line and the moment before the first lauch straight up. Then you go tru a layout where a lot is happening. The hangtime you have it the stall is the most hangtime I expierenced yet. The secont part has a good build up aswell, with again a strong launch into the tophat. But that is also the part where this coaster gets a bit to intens for my, because the first half has so much element. Which make my enjoy this coaster less then I expected.
Everything about this ride is amazing, apart from the rattle. If you can, sit on the inside seats.
Great coaster but queue lines a bit loud and chaotic. Outer seats can be rougher than inner seats.

I LOVED Voltron. The first time I rode it, it was way too much for me, had to lie down for like half an hour afterwards. But the next day, I made sure to eat and drink enough beforehand, so my second ride was much more enjoyable and I could ride it again soon after. The Layout is so much fun and it's just overall a stunning coaster, just make sure you're in good health before riding! I didn't notice any rattling, but my friend said it had a noticeble one on one train on the wing seat. Tho, as insanely fun as it was, it doesn't top Ride to Happiness for me.

The beyond vertical launch is pretty forceless and does nothing, the hangtime afterwards is great and it feels like you're being pulled down while upside down, the downwards corkscrew afterwards doesn't do much and the bunny hill after gives decent ejector, the 2 immelmans have you out of your seat in a slightly uncomfortable way and it makes it quite repetitive but they are both pretty fun, the stall is crazy, its overhyped due to not lasting as long as hyped up to be (2.2 seconds isn't much) I prefer Hyperia's stall due to it lasting longer and being more focused on floating instead of hanging, the airtime hill that follows is incredible and is the 2nd best moment of airtime on the coaster. The upwards S-curve doesn't really do anything but its fun, the same can be said with the dive loop after. The bump into the turntable can be a little painful. This part of the coaster isn't themed to a high standard as I think it should. The backwards launch is the punchiest launch on the coaster and the spike gives great floater airtime. The launch is semi-powerful and the tophat gives sustained -0.7g which is really nice, The airtime hill afterwards is insane and after riding it over and over it began to make my jaw hurt. The wave turn that follows is a little forceless but it gives some good airtime and on the front right gives great laterals, The double up gives 2 decent pops of airtime and the drop of the mid-course brake run is alright. The corkscrew after is pretty forceless but the turn makes you grey out every single time (I think it hits about 4.5g-5g), the corkscrew after does nothing (as always) and then the airtime hump into the brakes gives a good pop of airtime. Amazing coaster but I don't favour airtime as much as others so it doesn't make my top 1. I prefer Taron due to how I like near misses and great pacing and elements that go well together. The rattle on Voltron is noticeable and can sometimes cause a little bit of pain but its completely tolerable and people are overreacting way too much about it. Comfortable seats and the restraints raise a little so you can get more airtime which I think is great. Needs some more theming in the ride area and it will be top 10 in the world no doubt.
Wtf intamin? This is insane. Ejector every corner, excellent inversions, ultra smooth ride, comfy lapbars… i cant find a single bad thing about this ride. Incredible

BATMAN! This ride is a great experience in every way. For its size, and for a theme park like this, it is simply the perfect thrill ride.

An awesome preshow with multiple decorated scenes prepare you for a gorgeous "Train" station with the Batmobile waiting for you. The standing launch to start off the ride feels snappy and powerful. The small trains fly through the area with lots of interactions with the path. But the highlights are definitely the second launch, the "semi-holding" brake at the top of the tophat, and the very long zero-G section. Finally, the brake run at the end of the ride is bizarre, and especially thrilling on the front row. Even the final scene with the animatronics and lasers is fun as you pull into the station. This ride is fun, gorgeous to look at, and even more relentless than some of its bigger brothers in some aspects. It's the perfect package.

AWARD WINNER: WORST ONBOARD AUDIO. look, i know this is a really stupid thing to get all up in arms over. but one of my biggest pet peeves in coaster design is when there is thematic talking during a coaster section. and you know why that's a problem ?? I CAN'T GOT DAMN HEAR YOU !!!!!! the roaring of the train coupled with the wind and the screaming and shouting makes any voice completely inaudible outside of the intentionally slow sections that would end up being quieter, where talking would make more sense. anywhere else, i want the only audio coming out of those speakers to be a transcendent musical score. this ride overdoes it with the talking during the parts where i am shouting through the glorious insanity of the layout. i just want some loud music

I absolutely, positively LOVE this thing!  Awesome mix of launches, ejectors, hangtimes, inversions, laterals, pacing, airtimes.   It's also as smooth as glass with great restraints.  I was able to get the front seat for 6 of my 9 rides (light crowds).  The hangtime on the top hat is awesome in the front.  It does everything so well.  Two of my rides were in the rain, and the train was flying over the wet track.  GREAT coaster.

An incredible ride from start to finish featuring some of the most intense elements a launch coaster can provide. With the reputation of this model, it was expected to be good but I was surprised by how much power this ride packs. All tied with a nice ribbon that is the presentation and theming of the ride. To avoid spoilers, all I’ll say is the theme is good with one great set piece in the queue, however the it did cause the queue to move at an awkward pace and at times felt the story of the ride felt longer than necessary. The trains are slightly different from other Intamin launch coasters, with the back row of each car being staggered to the sides similar to a B&M Hyper. Additionally, the seats felt slightly wider than other variants and the lap bar was extremely comfortable as usual. With a small train, there is no bad seat but the back row was my preferred row. Each seat has speakers for on-board audio, but it appeared it was not operational in all seats during my visit. Launch one on this provides a powerful kick, an instant boost in speed into two floaty elements that caught be off guard each time. It quickly moves into the less punchy second launch and into one of the most bizarre top hats. It twists rapidly to the right and there is some floater airtime on the ascent, however the drop is very unusual. A set of permanent magnetic brakes are positioned to hold the train slowly over the drop. In the front it was slightly uncomfortable with my body weight resting on the lap bar, but in the back it was comparable to what a B&M Dive Coaster holding brake feels like. One the train releases every row gets a sudden pop of ejector airtime as it drops beyond vertical, which creates a strange mental game. Typically I expect a top hat to be a quick element with an airtime filled drop on the other end. However, the trim causes that drop to be delayed by a few seconds, which is fine but I do prefer top hats that are more immediate such as the ones on Pantheon at Busch Gardens Williamsburg and VelociCoaster at Islands of Adventure. I am glad it exists, but it is just not my thing. What follows though is the first insane element of the ride, an ejector airtime hill. This hill is in contention for the most powerful airtime moment on a steel coaster with how sudden and strong the airtime is. The only thing I can compare it to is El Toro’s (Six Flags Great Adventure) Rolling Thunder hill in the front, but not as powerful. A dive loop with a wave turn like entrance follows which gives a small pop of air before diving an into a step down. The step down is another dose of powerful ejector airtime before twisting into two comparatively tame elements with the S-Hill and Corkscrew, which provides great path interaction. A small wave turn gives a pop of ejector airtime and launch three leads to the most mind bending element of the ride. The turn following launch three creates a strong lateral force for the right side of the train and the ride slowly begins to twist into the most insane stall I have experienced. The way this stall slows the train down and how flat it is creates a sensation that no other stall has replicated. It feels it goes on forever and time slows down, it was incredible. The quick twist right into the brakes was especially whippy on the left side of the train and the brakes being a spike is such a wonderful way to end an insane coaster. A creative layout, good theme and presentation with some of the best hardware in the industry make this ride unforgettable. Yet despite being intense, it was never too much to get right back in line to ride again. While there are a few things that hold it back from being perfect in my book, it is a one of a kind ride that provides an unbelievable experience.
Insane intamin coaster

Super Elite coaster - so many elements are peak. I can't decide what I like best. Never ridden Velocicoaster so if this is it's little brother, it must be amazing. Does have low capacity as it's only drawback.

Absolutely crazy! I had to hold on because I went FLYING out of my seat! I love a coaster that is pure FUN and zero pain! The seats are great. The airtime and hangtime rivals RMCs, but no uncomfortable shinguards. The theming is also great.

This ride is amazing, its extremly smooth, its layout is the most creativ and crazy thing i have ever seen. The artime you get should be illegal, its just an master piece. The night rides on this are incredible do not miss night rides on this its out of controll. The only bad thing is the capacity but on my visit the ops were extremly fast sending a train every 30 seconds its creazy

Having just ridden Toutatis, I want to compare BGCE to that. Firstly, the preshow on BGCE is amazing. Arguably the best queue theming I have seen. I think that Toutatis back row’s launch is quite better than BGCE first launch because of the pull you get from that first pre drop on Toutatis. That said, BGCE’s first launch isn’t bad. After then, both coasters has one airtime moment and a hangtime filled inversion. Then there’s the second launch. BGCE’s launch is better because it isn’t a swing launch but Toutatis has a more airtime filled launch. The trim on BGCE is much more better than Toutatis’s one as well. Then BGCE hits me with probably the single best airtime hill I ever been on, the one before the dive loop. It’s simply nuts. The dive loop on BGCE is quite wacky and I like it. It has elements unique to the ride, unlike Toutatis. There’s a drop down where there’s another pop of ejector, and we hit the third corkscrew which doesn’t do much. The third launch is mid, but the zero-g stall is bliss. Hangtime at its peak. Much better than Toutatis. After that we hit the brakes.

Overall, Toutatis has just more airtime moments for me, but BGCE’s quick pops cannot be underestimated as well. And although Toutatis has good hangtime, BGCE’s quick pops executed the hangtime just perfectly. So, I like BGCE more, one spot above Toutatis for me.
I was a little underwhelmed, but it is still a good ride.

This ride is unbelievably good. Some of the craziest ejectors I’ve ever experienced. Great duration, brilliant elements and a surprisingly punchy launch, the hangtime on that stall and at the top of the top hat are incredible and the ejector on the small airtime hills are super aggressive. Genuinely a near perfect experience. 

The really long pre-show does hinder the re-rideability slightly, and the capacity isn’t amazing. But the actual theming is good enough where the themeing isn’t really required. But not really much to complain about ride experience wise, it’s got literally everything you want. It was also flying on a night ride so I 100% recommend that too.

This is the coaster that made me an enthusiast... and my first ever major coaster, which is insane tbh. I walked in not knowing it was an extreme / thrill, or what that even meant, walked out both shocked and euphoric. It changed my life. Its just a masterpiece, the launch, the theming, the pre show, that absolutely gorgeous first top hat, and the launch to the hat... The ridiculously good zero-G... Idk what to say, its truly intense, perfect layout and pace, and very very smooth. Incredible!!! In Intamin We Trust

As my first roller coaster with an inversión and a launch It made me stop being afraid of riding roller coasters, i rode It 5 times and It was amazing, confortable restraints nice layout and the brakes at the top hat really were frightening 10 out of 10
The ride took forever to ride 3 hours while I had more hopes up for a decent coaster

 Similar feel to Toutatis.

Excellent ride. Kept breaking down with a train stuck on mid launch but back in operation quite quickly.

Almost perfect

This is as good as a modern coaster could be. Really complete ride with no real pacing pulls no meandering like Velocicoaster. This is far better. Amazing top hat and camel and zero g stall. The second corkscrew would be better as a camelback. It has great elements but I almost wish it wasn't so smooth. I'd rather have funny shuffling in between elements to make the filler track less smooth and boring. This is why i prefer older rides

It's incredible what Intamin, Parque Warner and Parque Reunidos have accomplished here. This ride has the complete package. First of all the queue line, there's a section of switchbacks on the backside of the Wayne Manor where you will spend the majority of your wait. You will be divided in group of 40/50 people and sent inside the indoor portion of the queue. From here the actual experience starts. There's a preshow in Bruce Wayne's studio with some cool lighting and effects and then you proceed into the batcave thanks to a secret passage. You go through an abandoned tunnel and you will find yourself into the coaster station themed to a Gotham City Subway Station. Here you'll board the super comfortable train. The design of the front car is fantastic, it looks like the Batmobile with lightning and a lot of cool features, there's on board audio too. After dispatch there's a small show scene with the joker shoting at you with a cannon and the you get launched into the layout. First launch was surprisingly intense, very forceful despite the modest stats. The first inversion has a lot of hangtime which I like. Second launch has a good kick and you blast into the spectacular top hat. This is my favorite top hat, good positive forces going into it and nice ejector cresting it. There's a trim brake at the top that will slow the train to a crawl but it works to the coaster advantage. The drop feels like a dive coaster drop but on steroids, the front will be hanging over the drop and then get a brief moment of ejector while the back doesn't really have the hanging feeling of the front but gets the superior ejector in the drop. There is a fast change of direction at the bottom of the drop and then you get launched into the sky from the powerful ejector hill. Second inversion is really good with a surprising airtime pop at the top, there's a small dip with a sudden ejector pop and a whippy s-hill. Third inversion is a fast corkscrew with some nice lateral and a somewhat pop of airtime in the backrow while your upside down. Before hitting the last launch there's a nice wave turn with some great lateral airtime. Third launch has another good kick and you enter the finale of the ride. Here there's the best inversion on the ride, a super slow zero g stall with an insane amount of hangtime that will transition into airtime in the pullout from the element. You will then enter the weird brake run that has a "surprising" spike element. No force on the spike, it's just there to slow the train before entering the station. There are a Joker and a Batman statues on the brake run and you will return into the station.
Phenomenal coaster and is now in my TOP 3 in Europe.
Excellent, Ride basically the European cousin of Velocicoaster.

When I visited Spain for the first time last year, I first visted PortAventura & Ferrari Land, and then Parque Warner Madrid. This coaster was just simply the perfect launch coaster and currently sits as my number 6 of my favorite coasters ever. This ride has some of the most strong airtime moments I've ever felt on anything, and the theming and preshow were done EXTREMELY well. For me, this is easily the best and my favorite launch coaster I've ever done, and I rode it multiple times which got me many different and incredible experiences. 10/10
Absolutely fantastic, the pacing is amazing and that airtime hill is perfect!
Great Coaster. But unfortunatly it opened at 2 pm for some reason, 2 hours after park opening and on both rides the Onboard audio wasnt working.
I just don't get the hype. It's pathetically short, is way rougher than a coaster this new should be, and with an attempt at theming so lacklustre it makes the car park look like Disney World.

There's a little rattle that gets worse as the day goes on but that didnt take away from the ride experience or stop me from riding this masterpiece as much as I could. Every element absolutely slaps what an incredible coaster with phenomenal forces, love it

probaly the best ride in the UK amazing first drop in the back row and lots of strange ejector moments with the new nylon wheels it runs super fast but theres a VERY noticable rattle on all the even numbered rows but apart from that absoutley world class
Overrated
even after 10 rides on this freak the first drop made me feel like i was about to find out whether i was going to heaven or hell

AWARD WINNER: MOST INCONSISTENT. Hyperia's full of mood swings, feeling on top of the world one minute and wanting off it the next. Some days she wants to give you the ride of your life, other days she wants nothing less to do with you. Whether or not your hour plus of waiting to glide on her wings is worth, is decided seemingly entirely by a coin flip. Will you run through her layout glass smooth enjoying every second, or will a jarring rattle crack your head open like an egg? It's truly a roll of the die in a way that no other roller coaster is. We're talking about a roller coaster here, remember.
Hyperia is the best coaster at Thorpe Park and in the UK. My favourite element has to be the stall. I mean it was absolutely amazing. 10/10.
In another universe this has a theme. Also I'm NEVER calling this Flipzeria
Big One > Hyperia
Rode it twice, first time was good, the second was quicker but had the most insane rattle. Gave me such a bad headache! Kinda disappointed

Hyperia is a really great ride, but it needs more length. Like just one more hill would make the ride feel so much more complete. The valleys were also not as intense as I expected them to be, I expected to gray out at the bottom of the first drop but I only started to gray out a little bit. The hangtime wasn’t as good as I expected but I did get nice floater on the Outerbank. The 2 hills after the trims also hit a lot harder than I expected. Biggest problem is definitely capacity and theming. Like I know it seems weird complaining about this more than Chinese coasters but Thorpe gets a lot more guests so this ride gets very high average wait times. And of course it lacks theming, but the vibe in the station is very nice.Also there’s a bit of a rattle but I didn’t really notice it that much. I think the rattle on this is around the level of beyond the cloud, so it adds some intensity. The lapbars also seem to come down more on this than the other Mack’s with this restraint I have ridden.

EDIT: I refuse to call it Flipzeria, and until the name changes back, I will be moving this down my ranking to my 3rd favorite just because of that sponsor
anyone who disagrees I know where you live
The first drop is the best in the world, the Kraemer roll is insane and the stall seems to last forever the final wave turn and hill are also great

Hyperia has some good elements and the layout itself is decent, but it’s massively overglazed. For all the hype surrounding it, the actual experience feels surprisingly underwhelming. The ride is comically short, and before it really has a chance to build momentum, it’s already over. The first drop is decent, but after that the ride never really reaches the level I expected from all the praise it gets. A lot of the elements honestly feel like they do nothing and don’t leave much of an impact.

What makes it more disappointing is how badly it’s running for such a new coaster. There’s a noticeable rattle throughout the ride that takes away from the experience and stops it from feeling smooth and polished like a brand-new flagship attraction should.

Honestly, it feels like they cared more about breaking records and building the tallest coaster in the UK than actually creating a genuinely great coaster experience. The height is impressive, but once you get past that, the ride itself just doesn’t feel world class at all, which is pretty disappointing considering the expectations.

I’m not saying Hyperia is bad, but people talk about it like it’s one of the greatest coasters ever built, and I honestly just don’t see it. For me, it feels massively overhyped compared to what it actually delivers.

I can't select every item on the list but this packs a punch! Just what the uk needed, this has made thorpe park my favourite theme park, that first drop will leave anybody speechless especially on the back row😂 will be returning in September.

Oh man I was disappointed in this machine. I live in the UK and whenever I passed the site I would pop over to see it being built. I even went to the launch day and had a very early ride but jeez, it was so underwhelming. The 1st drop felt slow and forceless. You basically do a figure of 8 and then the rides over. I've been back a few times just to check if the ride had bedded in and nope... still a coaster which could have been so much better.

Hyperia is still to this day, the most disappointing ride in which i have ever ridden. The layout sucks and is way to short. The elements do not hit at all and it is rougher than any other coaster at Thorpe Park. The area around as well is completely unthemed and overall the entire experience is lacking anything. It is a huge shame as i was looking forward to the UK getting a new rollercoaster. I hope whatever comes next to the UK is far better than this extremely pathetic excuse of a hyper coaster. I have not included Hyperia in my tops due to the fact that i only rank down to around 120, and Hyperia most likely sits around 150. I will say, it does a fantastic job at drawing crowds from the good rides at Thorpe Park

The queue took 2 hours in the unthemed queue with the ride breaking down every few minuets. The ride on it's own is an amazing coaster with a amazing layout, but when comparing it to other rides at the park.. It's just poor.

The airtime for Hyperia is excellent. 
The airtime from the first drop and outer bank turn is insane. 
The stall delivers incredible hang time. 
There are things that could be improved; theming, operations, splashdown trims, queue line cattle pen, and ride length. 
Otherwise, it's a really good and worth riding.

This ride goes HARD. Ridden this 16 times, 3 times at night and this ride always delivers a world class, jaw dropping experience. First drop, outer bank roll and dive loop are insane. It’s shaky a bit, which notches it down to my number 2, but it’s a short and punchy ride.

Hyperia is without question the best rollercoaster at Thorpe park and in the uk. Being someone who’s only ridden ~100ft  and less coasters up to this point this was a massive shock to actually go down the drop. It feels genuinely out of this world to be ejected like that with just a lap bar going straight down, it feels as if you’re going to fall out it’s so good. The valleys shook me around a bit but hey not so bad and definitely doesn’t ruin the ride. The Immelmann is great, strong floater and I always grey out when I get to the top which no other coaster makes me do. The outer bank I felt should’ve done more I was kind of hanging there for a bit. The stall felt the same but was also great nonetheless. It was crazy to have your hands down on the stall and just hang from your waist. Almost at 250 coasters now, with most of Europe’s and the U.S. West Coast’s biggest rides under my belt—but I’ve never experienced something this intense in my life! I’d need something like Eejanaika or Intimidator 305 for a fair comparison, but this thing? It’s not even close to X2—it’s absurdly intense!
So first conclusion: this is not for everyone.

Now that you’ve been warned, let’s get into the details!

The first launch is nice and punchy, done in two phases. I’m not the biggest fan of the two-step system, but it’s followed by a solid first brain-melter of a G+ moment. Then we hit the top hat with a very strong and sustained ejector, and as we drop down again—disaster strikes!

This is the moment everyone talks about: “Why the trims?” you might ask.
Well, without them, you’re just dead. No joke.
Even as a seasoned rider, hitting that valley at night folded me in half against the lap bar with those insane forces. That’s never happened to me before!

Okay, we’re past the most “sensitive” moment. Now we’re back in the air, still catching airtime, especially on the first hill, leading into a turnaround—not super noteworthy, but solid.

Then it’s ejector after ejector, before that gorgeous 180° in front of the entrance, which looks great and leads into one last (slightly weaker) airtime moment before hitting the second launch.

From here, the layout shifts focus—less on airtime, more on whip and dueling elements.
We enter the Celestial Spin, which is visually striking for the dueling effect, though less intense in terms of raw sensation than, say, a Death Roll or Maus au Saurus Roll.

Then comes a massive overbanked turn—not much to report there, except that even up that high you’re still getting solid G-forces. Then comes the EGF turn, which is just incredible, possibly my favorite element of the whole ride!

After that, your skull gets crushed in a long helix that climbs slightly toward the end (or the start, depending on the side), kind of a mini I305 warning shot—though to be fair, probably not quite as intense as I305, lol.

Then one last airtime moment, not quite as crazy as the first half’s, and finally a last pop of airtime as you hit the brakes.

So… what do I think?

It’s absolutely excellent: incredibly intense, tons of ejectors, a wide variety of elements, a great length—but yeah… probably too intense for a lot of people.
The ejectors don’t go into leg-ripping -2G territory, but the positive Gs are extremely pronounced and relentless throughout!

Watch out for some minor rattle on the green side, but nothing major.

Conclusion:
A world-class coaster, not to be missed. If you can handle the intensity—go ride it NOW!

The second half then focuses on racing/dueling with lots of near-miss moments with the other train, the supports, and the track, including an inversion where the trains twist around each other. As usual, the operations at Universal are excellent with stacking only seldom occurring and double-stacking never occurring.  They were also happy to accommodate my requests for the back row.

As of the time of this writing, this just barely makes it into my top 10.  That leads me into the only issue I had with this coaster, rattle.  The rattle seems somewhat train-dependent, but is definitely worse overall on the green side.  It even manages to vibrate rather badly during the strongest airtime moment of the ride, when the green track passes under the yellow track during an airtime hill in the first half.  That is the first time I can remember ever experiencing such a sensation during airtime on a steel coaster.  While it certainly isn't bad enough to ruin the ride, it does push it across the line into headache-causing territory if I were to try to marathon the ride, which is why it isn't any further up in my rankings.  I'm also concerned about the future, because if this thing starts rattling as bad as Copperhead Strike currently does, in combination with the higher intensity, it could easily become headache-inducing in just one ride.  I'm hoping that Universal's maintenance will be good enough to avoid this.

Also, as a side note, I typically collect a T-shirt of a coaster (usually my favorite coaster there) from each park I visit.  However, when I visited Epic Universe in October 2025, I wasn't able to find a T-shirt for this or any other coaster in the park at any of the gift shops I could find.  Considering my political inclinations I never thought I would say this, but Universal, please offer ride T-shirts and take my money!
