Where to even begin with this ride. Falcons Flight is a marvel in theme park design and ride design. An ambitious idea challenging the limits of what a ride can do. Records that have previously stood in place for upwards of 25 years were not just broken, but in every sense shattered. Over 70 feet taller than Kingda Ka, 6 mph faster than Formula Rossa and over 5,000 feet longer than Steel Dragon 2000, all on one ride experience. It is positioned to dominate the park’s skyline and entry experience while also using a natural cliff as a stage for the record breaking moments. 

As expected for the world’s largest roller coaster, its presence is noticeable from miles away with the giant camelback standing above the entire park. Within the park and walking up to it the ride is omnipresent no matter where in the park you are. The camelback dwarfs Colossus and Spitfire, the final overbank dominates Discovery Springs. The entry to the park is woven into layout. Then during quieter hours, the roar of the final launch and ascent up the camelback echos throughout the park. Falcons Flight is the first and last ride every guest will see during their visit.

The entrance to the ride is positioned in the City of Thrills area of the park and the entrance is tucked into the back right corner of the land. This area is themed to the fictional Falcon Industries, a tech company focusing on creating high speed technology for space exploration. Falcons Flight is themed to be a product of the company taking inspiration from the behavior and nature of falcons and based upon the opening ceremony animation, they have developed a mechanical falcon that serves as the train for the ride. The queue does not clearly explain what the ride is, just that the experience is to mimic flying like a falcon. Fitting considering the falcon is the fastest animal in the world and soars to great heights, perfect for the records being broken.

Prior to entering the station, all loose articles must be placed in double sided lockers. Nothing is permitted in pockets, but glasses with a strap were permitted. The ride is also strict for guests with long hair needing to tie it  back and wear a safety hood provided by the attraction to keep hair secured. Metal detectors are in use and the queue moves quickly from this point onward.

Boarding these trains it is immediately noticeable how low the seats are to the floor. It has ample leg room to create what feels a bit like a lounge chair and in order for the lap bars to close properly every rider must put their legs out straight. It is the standard Intamin LSM coaster seats, but the rows are positioned further apart creating ample freedom. The most notable feature is the presence of a windshield at the front of each car. Concerns were initially raised how this would affect the ride experience as even though it eliminated the need for goggles to be worn, it was unusual to see. Ultimately, I did not find the windshield to be a source of concern, especially when seated in the back row of each car. Due to the staggered seating, these seats are more exposed and the wind is much stronger. Which I found across my rides preferring the back row of each car with my favorite seat being the back left. 

The ride begins with a punchy launch into the launch lift. Once it gets going the acceleration  mellows out to a gradual pace that send the train into a twisted drop. In the back rows this drop has a great pop of ejector airtime and the laterals toss riders to the right. It is especially wonderful in the back right and is the strongest moment of airtime on the ride. The following elements are smooth and flow well together with floater airtime over the top of each crest which is best experienced in the front row. My personal favorite element in the first segment is the wave turn diving under the structure for the hill. It is provides a wonderful moment of sustained airtime and it profiled nearly. The hill following is hit or miss depending on row and how full the train is. Some rides I got decent floater airtime, others it was very minimal. Typically the front row was consistent at being good, back rows had variability in the strength of the airtime. A swooping downward S-turn then leads into the hop into launch two.

Launch two does not have much of a kick, but it is mental how much the train accelerates while also climbing the cliff. The sound of the stators transitions from a whine to a roar and as the train reaches top speed it begins to shake from the acceleration. It is nothing uncomfortable, but that shake highlights just how much power is in that launch. It is particularly exhilarating to look around during the launch and see the ground alongside the ride drop away and climb the cliff. No other ride in the world is able to match that sensation and it is hard to wrap your head around just how high the train is. The top of launch two flattens out and gives a pop of floater airtime then curves upward on top of the cliff. At the top the tack banks outward over the cliff face, which depending on when you ride affects how this element is. Since Six Flags Qiddiya operates in the evening hours, there is not much daylight during operation. While it is still thrilling at night, the darkness does not sell how high the track is due to the void. However in daylight, it is incredible. All of the natural landscape that is massive looks small up there and in the back left it is so easy to get a great look down. The rest of the elements at the top are nothing to write home about, however the tone it is about to set is something that can only be described as unnatural.

As the train straightens out and rolls to the edge, a single screech of a falcon is played and then the train hits the trim. At that point, all noise is gone. When I say it is quiet, it is not in the sense that sound is muffled. There is no sound up there. Never have I ridden a coaster that has gotten to that level of silence before and there were plenty of rides with a full train where everyone went from screaming and laughing to nothing. Depending on how full the train is depends on how long the trim holds. Empty trains are up there much longer and full trains go through it a bit quicker. Regardless, the view is breathtaking. The entire park is laid out in front of the train and typical huge rides are tiny due to a mixture of the distance and the height. Those seated in the front are hung over the vertical drop off the cliff for a few seconds and the back gets a pop of ejector airtime once the trims loose their grip. What follows is what I can only describe to be the most intense moment on any coaster in the world.

Launch three is terrifying. Not only is the train entering it at a high speed, but the way it accelerates the train is ridiculous. When the train hits the stators, the ride roars in a way no other ride has ever done. You are pinned to the seat and the train shakes violently as it launches through the valley. It is the most powerful launch I have ever experienced and the only ride that comes even close to it was Kingda Ka’s launch. It is aggressive. It is violent. It feels as if you are being ripped apart by a black hole. That being said, it does flirt with being too much. That launch was the source for a few headaches throughout the day due to the shake it produces. That being said, I’d go as far as saying it is the single best moment I have experienced on a roller coaster.

That launch then leads into the record breaking airtime hill, which is lined with trim brakes on the ascent. Similar to the trim on the cliff, the weight of the train will affect how the train goes over the hill. No matter what the entire train does get floater airtime during the ascent and descent. However a full train will get some floater over the crest as well. That being said, the trims make the airtime feel stronger due to how much braking they provide. It is a strong deceleration that causes riders to lurch forward while also getting airtime, which makes it feel stronger than it actually is. The drop lasts for what feels like forever and the speed gained is amazing. What follows is a high speed twist to the right followed by a speed hill that has more floater airtime over the crest. The train then dives under the entrance at speeds that feel in excess of 100 mph and it smoothly transitions into a giant overbanked turn. One more speed hill and banked turn leads into a trimmed hill over the park entrance and a sharp banked turn into the brakes. For the speed the train takes this segment, it is fantastic, but it does get a bit shaky. It was nothing too bad, especially considering the speed the train is going, but it is noticeable. However, this is the conclusion to what is the largest roller coaster ever constructed. The scale alone is enough to impress, but the elements and forces are so dynamic that it is truly a one of a kind experience that no other ride can replicate. 



It is one of those rides that is hard to believe actually exists. Especially considering that the previous records have been broken either by gimmicks or have not been touched in decades. Is it possible these records could be broken again, maybe. However as it stands, there truly is nothing else like it in the world.


BONUS: Over the course of my visit, I was fortunate to be able to experience two rollbacks back to back on launch three. Both times the ride reacted the same way, it tried to clear the massive hill and got to the top before rolling back to launch three. Once the train settled and it was determined safe to do so, the ride was relaunched with riders on it. To be able to clear the hill, the ride did a quad swing launch to get to speed. Prior to the first launch the train would position itself in the correct spot and then launch in reverse about halfway up the launch track. There is a decent kick going reverse but it is nothing too intense. The train then immediately launches forwards to get enough speed to climb partially up the camelback, but not in the range of the trim brakes. It rolls back again and then engages in a powerful reverse launch up the cliff. There is a strong kick that pushes riders forward into the restraint and it accelerates in a similar manner to the launch up the cliff. It is steady and it throws the train up the vertical drop to the top of the cliff. The drop now acts like a spike with a few seconds of weightlessness and the back car begins to crest the top a little bit, reaching the trim on the cliff. The process of launching over 500 ft backwards is insane to experience as the ground rapidly falls away as the train is thrown upwards. There is genuinely no other experience like it. Then just a second later, the train drops back into the final launch.
The trim is not noticeable as the train drops forwards and then the launch kicks in at full power to send the train up and over the camelback. It feels exactly the same as a normal launch three, that being insanely powerful.

Falcons Flight isn’t just a roller coaster — it’s a reflection of life itself. From its smooth beginnings to its heart-stopping drops, this ride mirrors the ebbs and flows of a journey we all experience. It’s not just a thrill; it’s a story, told at breakneck speed.

The ride starts gently, with smooth turns and floaters that ease you into the experience. Then, the launch hits. Suddenly, you’re on the pinnacle of a cliff, high above the world, literally on top of it. The view is breathtaking — a moment of clarity, of feeling invincible. But just as you realize you’re standing on the edge of the world — aptly named “The Edge of the World” in the outskirts of Riyadh — you drop. A free-fall plunge that grounds you, humbles you, and reminds you of life’s unpredictability.

From rock bottom, the ride surges forward, gaining momentum and rising to staggering heights of over 500 feet. Then, it drops again, pulling you back to earth. The speed is relentless, weaving through head choppers and racing alongside an F1 track. There’s one final airtime hill before the ride slows to a crawl, leaving you breathless and exhilarated. It’s a relentless journey, much like life itself — full of highs, lows, and moments of awe.

But Falcons Flight is more than just a ride. It’s a symbol of ambition and vision, a testament to what’s possible when bold ideas meet determination. Built in Qiddiya City, a groundbreaking development near Riyadh, this coaster represents the future of Saudi Arabia. In a country where the majority of the population is under 40, there’s an undeniable energy and drive to create something extraordinary. Falcons Flight is proof of that ambition.

To those who dismiss this ride with one-star reviews, often without even experiencing it: stop. Open your mind. Visit. Saudi Arabia is a beautiful country with some of the friendliest people you’ll ever meet. This isn’t about politics or preconceived notions — it’s about appreciating a marvel of engineering and the spirit of a nation that dared to dream big.

Falcons Flight is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. There will never be another coaster like it. Perched on a cliff over 600 feet high, it defies imagination. It’s not just a ride; it’s an invitation to the world to see what Saudi Arabia has to offer. For the people of Riyadh, it’s more than a thrill — it’s a symbol of pride, progress, and possibility.

So, to the skeptics: Steel Vengeance had its moment. Falcons Flight is the future. Come ride it. Experience it. And maybe, just maybe, you’ll see the world — and life — a little differently.

The perfect symphony. 

Falcon's Flight is not only the tallest, fastest and longest but also the most perfect layout too. 

It starts gracefully, before giving you a taste of insanity as you launch up the hill. Then, like a falcon circling high above, it plays in perfect, calm silence at the top of the cliff. The cliff drop into the tunnel is other worldly but it only serves as a build up for what comes next. The downhill, 155mph launch; no words can describe. Up and over the hill. The record breaker for the tallest, fastest and longest tilt coaster in the world certainly lives up to that name. Iron Rattler is a wonderful coaster that has a little bit of everything to offer. The layout is massive and dynamic with its elements and the signature tilt element makes a statement standing high above the midway.

Iron Rattler is the marquee attraction of Steam Town and it looks fantastic with its presentation. Pathways are routed to go right against the coaster and every element is visible for guests to watch trains fly by. To fit with the theme, the tilt structure has props built on and within it and it looks great. The queue is well detailed using projections to give it more kinetic energy and the trains look incredible with the drill facade and lights.

The ride starts with a quick climb to the top and onto the tilt track. Tilting at that height is a cool sensation, especially in the back row. The release has a brief moment of airtime, but it feels closer to a sudden freefall like on a drop tower. Positive G’s are plenty in the valley and the first element transitions into solid hangtime. A fluid twist to the left gives a slight lateral push and the double up gives strong airtime, particularly in the front of the train. Perhaps the most unique element of the ride is the double zero-g roll, which is a good element but I wish it was a bit more floaty. It does have a good lateral pull through it and the back car does get a fun amount of whip on the downward roll. A strong airtime hill gives good air throughout the entire train and it enters my favorite element on the ride, the downward barrel roll. The roll starts with a banked turn into it and in the back row it is pulled through very quickly. Almost like it is a tamer version of the downward roll on Iron Gwazi. The last segment of the ride is the best paced on the layout with a twisted double down giving great air on each drop, a banked turn into a sudden ejector airtime drop and a fast roll into the brakes.

Iron Rattler is one of the best layouts to come from the designers at Vekoma and it does not have a single dull moment. I do wish some of the elements had more of a bite, especially the double zero-g roll as if it had the forces like Lech Coaster it would be an exhilarating ride. However, as it stands it is a great compliment to the more intense ride experiences offered by Colossus and Falcons Flight. Everyone got off of the coaster having a great time and it was one of the coasters I noticed guests riding the most in the park. A sign of a well designed experience that truly anyone would enjoy.

I’ve now ridden Europe’s and the U.S. West Coast’s biggest rides under my belt—but I’ve never experienced something this intense in my life! I’d need something like Eejanaika or Intimidator 305 for a fair comparison, but this thing? It’s not even close to X2—it’s absurdly intense! So first conclusion: this is not for everyone. Now that you’ve been warned, let’s get into the details! The first launch is nice and punchy, done in two phases. I’m not the biggest fan of the two-step system, but it’s followed by a solid first brain-melter of a G+ moment. Then we hit the top hat with a very strong and sustained ejector, and as we drop down again—disaster strikes! This is the moment everyone talks about: “Why the trims?” you might ask. Well, without them, you’re just dead. No joke. Even as a seasoned rider, hitting that valley at night folded me in half against the lap bar with those insane forces. That’s never happened to me before! Okay, we’re past the most “sensitive” moment. Now we’re back in the air, still catching airtime, especially on the first hill, leading into a turnaround—not super noteworthy, but solid. Then it’s ejector after ejector, before that gorgeous 180° in front of the entrance, which looks great and leads into one last (slightly weaker) airtime moment before hitting the second launch. From here, the layout shifts focus—less on airtime, more on whip and dueling elements. We enter the Celestial Spin, which is visually striking for the dueling effect, though less intense in terms of raw sensation than, say, a Death Roll or Maus au Saurus Roll. Then comes a massive overbanked turn—not much to report there, except that even up that high you’re still getting solid G-forces. Then comes the EGF turn, which is just incredible, possibly my favorite element of the whole ride! After that, your skull gets crushed in a long helix that climbs slightly toward the end (or the start, depending on the side), kind of a mini I305 warning shot—though to be fair, probably not quite as intense as I305, lol. Then one last airtime moment, not quite as crazy as the first half’s, and finally a last pop of airtime as you hit the brakes. So… what do I think? It’s absolutely excellent: incredibly intense, tons of ejectors, a wide variety of elements, a great length—but yeah… probably too intense for a lot of people. The ejectors don’t go into leg-ripping -2G territory, but the positive Gs are extremely pronounced and relentless throughout! Watch out for some minor rattle on the green side, but nothing major. Conclusion: A world-class coaster, not to be missed. If you can handle the intensity—go ride it NOW

Hold up, its possible to make a roller coaster THIS good??? The first launch gives you a decent punch, then after an airtime hill, you get blasted with an insanely intense second launch. The double inverted top hat gives you some insane thrill as you come up the mountain and do another inversion as you plumet, then the stall brings you some insane forces, enough to make some gray out. Then the skyflier loop is the most fun thing you will even experience, it has you completely unaware which way is up and you never know which way you're facing. Then the ice winder  roll keeps the momentum going with some fun, whippy inversions. Then you get to the fire serpent roll which is surprising whippy and intense, then you get to take a momentary breather while getting some airtime before getting to the 9th, and final inversion. Once you hit the break run, you will be shocked at how amazing the coaster is. I rode it 3 times within 3 hours, and it never failed to surprise me with how fun it was. This is the best roller coaster in the world, no argument.

I felt that my original review for AlpenFury definitely had some recency bias so I’m giving it a fair rewrite.  
     AlpenFury provides a long-overdue addition to the B&M-heavy lineup and blows every other ride in the park out of the water, due to its relentless pacing.
     The launch packs more punch than I expected, and almost every element of the ride landed perfectly for me. I felt the top hat absorbed too much of the momentum the first launch so quickly builds and the coaster does meander a bit after the first drop before the zero G stall. The fire serpent roll was a bit overhyped providing decent forces but just not quite the intensity that’s being universally described by other enthusiasts. The ride is intense but not too intense for new enthusiasts or people who don’t ride coasters often, making it a great ride to bring your friends on. Despite a 5½-hour wait on opening day partially due to a couple of brief downtime issues, the overall ride experience was outstanding.      Capacity felt a bit slow, which isn't surprising: AlpenFury only runs two trains of 18 riders each.
Edit: I do have to say I keep seeing this ride compared to Maverick and personally I  prefer Maverick, as it provides the more intense experience, and longer ride duration. Alpenfury’s launch is rolling, whereas Maverick’s launch occurs with the train almost stopped and is therefore more punchy. Mavericks’s banked turn post-launch also trumps Alpenfury’s top hat with its sheer intensity.
Overall Alpenfury is a phenomenal and much needed addition to Canada’s Wonderland. It’s not a masterpiece nor is it a perfect ride but I’d definitely describe it as a world class coaster.

AlpenFury delivers an excellent mix of ejector airtime, intense inversions, and nonstop pacing. The opening top hat is easily one of the standout elements of the ride, creating a unique sensation that combines hangtime, exposure, and a feeling of weightlessness. From there, the coaster rarely lets up, flowing from one inversion into the next while maintaining strong intensity throughout.

Despite its compact layout, AlpenFury never feels small when you are riding it. The speed, transitions, and constant action make the ride feel much larger than it appears from the outside.

The main drawback is the capacity. Without Fast Lane, wait times can become extremely long due to the coaster’s lower hourly capacity. However, with Fast Lane, the wait is often minimal, allowing riders to experience the coaster multiple times with very little downtime.

Overall, AlpenFury is a thrilling and unique addition to Canada’s Wonderland’s lineup, offering a high-intensity experience filled with memorable elements.

Great Ride, got to ride the first fully loaded train ever (employee ride day) and got the back. I got 3 more rides in rows 1, 5, and 9. I'll start with the worst, row 5. The tilt is mid in this row, as you just rotate and don't tilt up or down, but the drop is great and so is the hang in every row I rode in. The first airtime hill gave pretty good air time in 5, but the rest was what you'd expect from row 5. The front was awesome, but not the best. The tilt is really cool watching the tilt and seeing the track connect. The first airtime hill is best in the front (does nothing in the back suprisingly), and its as expect cool watching the layout come in front of you. Row 9 was basiclly a tuned down version of row 12, so I'll go to 12. 12 was easily the best row. The tilt is really weird going up, and its really cool feeling that. The hang in the back is incredible as you hang in place for like 10 seconds. This is also the reason why it has comfort collars, and the first ride I've been on where I've agreed to them being in place, cause that hang would not be fun with a lap bar. The drop is great, and the layout in the back has a ton of great airtime. The best part of the ride in any row is the crazy triple down into the tunnel. It feels soooo fast in the back, more than the front, and it delivers incredible airtime. The last bunny hills are also awesome. Overall, I'd say this is a clear #5 option in the park. One warning I have for everyone is seating is assigned and row requests are not allowed, you get what you get and you don't throw a fit. For some reason the platform can only single load every row and the back and front do NOT have an extended que, so prepare to get row 5 after wating 4 hours.

This tilt coaster is absolutely insane!!! It starts off with a crazy fast lift hill into a slight left turn that gets you on the tilt track. Something about this lift feels magical with the mermaids laughing and whispering in the speakers behind and it really gets you hyped for the incoming ride. Then after a little bit of sitting on the tilt track you eventually tilt and man this is a really odd sensation. You fall into the vest, and it almost makes you lean forward if you have your hands up. Then you finally drop and go immediately into a left twist at the valley of the drop. At this time the audio goes from mermaids to full early 90’s hard rock that makes the ride way better. After this you go into a pretty decent element where you peak for an airtime hill but twist in and go straight into a heartline roll. This heartline roll gives really good laterals and some decent flojector airtime. After this intense inversion you whip into a half helix that pulls some decent Gs. Followed by the half helix you go into most people's favorite part of the ride, which I agree with, the triple down. On the first dip you violently have a left wave turn that slams you out of your seat giving great ejector. Then as soon as you recover from the first down you go into another one this time banking to the right this time. Finally, you go into a basic drop but this time it goes under a part of the queue. If you ride this ride at night this tunnel gets filled with smoke/fog and it enhances the experience by loads! Anyway, after the triple down you go into a non-inverting loop which is good, BUT I thought it was going to have great laterals and ejector, but it kinda just lacked forces. After this you go into a pretty drawn out turn into a mid, off-axis hill that severely lacks force. Then you flip into the final inversion, another heartline roll! This inversion does everything the first one does but better! If you have the OnRide Picture Pass the camera takes the picture as you are taking this roll that leads to great pictures. Finally, you head into some off axis hills, wave turns, and a drawn-out hill that all pulls great Gs. You slam into the brakes with a full head of steam, I feel like Siren’s could go for another 500ft of track and it would be great. These new-gen Vekoma vests are great and let you get great airtime and they are very, very comfortable. Overall, Siren’s is a great ride with great audio, great airtime, great restraints, and an awesome gimmick! I was also on the second train on the charity event so that's cool!!!

When I first heard this, I was like “Vekoma is making this?” and when I rode it, I still couldn’t believe it. This is a really fun coaster, and the tilt doesn’t feel like a gimmick. The ride is short but it still is really fun, even in the front row, where I was. The ride apparently goes only 58 miles per hour but feels a lot faster. Theming is actually pretty nice, but the queue is in full sun, which sucked.
Ohhh shitings
The music in the background while zooming around the layout is fire

Sirens Curse is a great addition to Cedar Point's lineup, featuring tight elements and surprising airtime with whippy inversions. What's not to like? The tilt is incredible in both the front and back, but I experienced significantly more airtime in rows 4 and 5.
Best coaster at Cedar Point with Maverick just behind and Steel Vengeance just behind Maverick. Smooth, Tilt Coaster, Intensity, Even the audio! Every park needs one or two coasters made by Vekoma.

The tilt sensation in the back is very cool - much more disorienting than something like a dive coaster. And the stomach drop on the release is comparable to some drop towers. After that Siren's Curse's layout is solid but unspectacular - it has a nice mix of moderate forces but the positives are not particularly intense and the sequencing can feel a bit aimless. Overall it's a broadly appealing coaster that blends unique thrills with a smooth and comfortable ride but the model still has room for improvement.
This is so much fun! Smooth, great pacing, cool layout. But it seems to be down a lot. And with riders getting stuck a couple times this year, it's kind of a sore spot.
One if the best rides of all time. That drop is on-par to a drop tower. Insane

Siren's Curse is an amazing ride. The tilt is freaky, and creates some crazy hangtime. The release is sudden. The layout consists of many airtime hills and snappy lateral inversions. I also like the on-board audio, and the theming in the queue and station. The ride is well paced with a very engaging layout. One of the turns near the end also caused some positive G's. The one con of this ride is that it feels short, but it is an absolute rush. 9.5/10

Buttery smooth, yet intense. The first drop is sensational and the remainder of the ride does not disappoint either. I suggest sitting as close to the back as you can, since the drop will be significantly higher and more powerful due to the style of tilt employed on this coaster. Some are saying tilt coasters are a gimmick but I am keen for as many as possible. Also, the onboard music is on fire!
Audio built into the carts and LEDs on the side of the carts and it's fun

God Damn! This ride astonished me. Everything from the hanging to the twists to the theming is beautiful. I was in a bad mood before this and after I was walking out the happiest I had been that whole day. This is a Must Ride.

My new #1 at Cedar Point, just to hang there being hold by the vest waiting in 90 degrees angle for the train to be released was a nice surprise. The onboard audio only makes the experience even better. 23 rides in 3 days, and can’t wait to go back there ASAP
The tilt is the most insane element on any coaster I’ve been on. The layout has great ejector and intensity but is just too short. Overall, great ride.
The tilt is insane one of my favorite coaster elements. The rest of the layout is smooth and fun
You should come to Japan to ride this and Hakugei.
The most intense coaster I've been on and it is not even close. The initial drop is wild and the craziness does not stop until the brake run. Nothing really comes close to this.

Imagine if X2 was bigger, better, and smoother. That's eejanaika. The layout is relentless, the forces are intense, and the pace is much better kept than on its predecessor. It's not smooth, and it can even be a little painful. You really have to be a fan of super intense coasters to enjoy it, but I promise it's worth. This was far and away the best coaster on my recent Japan trip, as Hakugei was running terribly sluggish in the cold.

I'm going to use the rest of this review to pass on my elite ball knowledge gained from my trip. 1) They only let in exactly the right amount of people to the locker area. If you want to guarantee the back row, just stall for as long as possible and waltz to the end of the line when everyone is done. If you're towards the front of the line before being let into the locker area, you can do the opposite to try and guarantee the front. 2) For reasons that will soon be obvious, I cannot condone actually following this second point of advice. If you're feeling brave, try taking off the seat belt that goes around your waist at the crest of the lift hill. You won't get in trouble, I did it twice. X2 lacks this third seat belt, I promise it's redundant. The ride feels RIDICULOUS if you take it off. Try it, but you didn't hear it from me.
It's only missing theming...it's elite
Simply outstanding.  It won’t be for everyone as it is undoubtedly one of the most intense coasters on the planet, but if pushing the boundaries is your thing then Eejanaika delivers and some.

Absolutely incredible the backwards run to the top. I really enjoyed this coaster. It's high, fast, a tad scary, but also fairly smooth. Every corner feels like a surprise. Little to no theming, but it doesn't really need any - the ride speaks for itself. I really enjoyed the twisting inversion. My only comment is its so fast it feels like its over too soon (adding to the thrill) and the wait time was long 80+ minutes on a quiet day.
Run up perfectly positioned to give a different view to the other parks coasters. Lives up to the reviews.

Basically a masterpiece and better than X2. My first ride was absolutely perfect and I loved it. However, my second ride was in the rain in an outside seat, which led to a rather uncomfortable experience. I'm still giving it 5 stars because of how incredibly perfect my first ride was.
Don't know why this coaster is rated so high, it is very uncomfortable. I was shocked by this ride it was intense. Normally I like to reride but this one nope

The first drop takes your breath away.  I like X2's layout better, but Eejanaika doesn't have X2's headbangs and leg slaps.  It's a true feat of engineering that Eejanaika delivers every flip/rotation so smoothly.  I laughed the whole time.  One huge negative - the ride ops go over every safety rule as you sit in your seat.  By late morning, the line was 3 hours.  (Fortunately, I stayed at the resort and got early entry.)  An important note to add:  
AGE-LIMIT RULE - Fuji-Q rules state no one over 54 is allowed on Eejanaika.  Well, I'm over that age.  The ride ops didn't ask me or my friend for proof of age, so it appears the rule is there as more of a recommendation.  However, YMMV.
これを乗り続けると白鯨でも物足りなくなってしまいます。ジェットコースターがエアタイムだけじゃないことを証明している最高傑作です。

This is without a shadow of a doupt one of the best coasters that I've ever ridden. It is out of this world! It's so uniquely insane and intense! I was seated in row 1 and the view over there was really freaky. I love coasters that have lots of airtime and snappy transitions like Toutatis but this was something else. An absolute masterpiece!

このジェットコースターは、乗客をまるで布人形のように激しく振り回します。まさに常軌を逸した凄まじさです！最初の落下は、高さ76メートルから89度という急角度で一気に急降下します。乗車時間はわずか2分間ですが、そのレイアウトは秀逸で、ゼロGロールやブーメランターンといった要素が乗客をあらゆる方向へと翻弄します。純粋な激しさという点では世界最高レベルであり、白鯨と並ぶ日本の傑作と言えるでしょう！それにしても、ええじゃないか…人間を何だと思っているだ！？

Wow. Such a unique and crazy ride. Was lucky enough to be there on a slow day. The first drop is really insane, my body actually didn't like it. Same feeling as being pressed down a drop tower. Still, what a ride, was laughing and shocked the whole time.

The ride inside was nothing too crazy and it was handleable, but when I sat outside it was a completely different ride, I got flung around everywhere and did not know what was happening, it was very crazy but it was pretty fun tho, although my eyes hurt after that.
Very intense, has been my number 1 for nearly 3 years but I’m going on RTH soon which may beat it
Rough, not fun at all. Weird restraints that don't let you breathe. Slow dispatches. The turning is rough, sometimes even punshes you.

Currently my #1, and in my opinion an absolute masterpiece of visceral intensity. The layout is absolutely relentless and the flips disorienting. This ride doesn't let up (not even in the brake run!) and the sustained g-forces are impeccable. While undeniably rough, and rerides hindered by slow operations characteristic of the park, I was able to get 5 runs in, with my back row ride being the absolute best (you can't pick your row unfortunately, so it's luck of the draw). It's the king of the S&S 4D coasters, and it's difficult to imagine a coaster that can top the sheer violence of this ride!
ふつーのコースターに飽きてしまった方にオススメ。人を人として扱わないところが好きです。
Absolute flying washing machine.

Holy hell, absolute insanity in all the best ways. I didn't expect it to be too different from X2 at one of my home parks but let me tell you, this is on a different level. I can't really describe the experience cause I can barely recall other than it was absolutely incredible. Honestly worth the trip to Japan almost by itself.

As with almost all Japanese parks, capacity and ops were not great, but the park wasn't crowded so I got 5 rides!

Eejanaika is an absolute masterpiece and proves that coasters don’t need to be airtime focused to provide incredible ride experiences. The combination of the smooth track and rotations, incredible restraints, and a fast and intense layout results in one of the best coasters in the entire world. The first drop is absolutely brutal and even if you are familiar with the layout and rotations, it always feels absolutely crazy and unique. Eejanaika’s full ride experience is truly breathtaking and something every enthusiast should have on their bucket list.

I really enjoyed this coaster. I am pretty small, so I was able to survive the headbang, but Japan knows how to make some pretty good coasters. I loved this ride, and the next time I'm in Japan, I HAVE to go.

This is it. The one and only Eejanaika! A coaster enthusiasts dream all put together making what is the most out of control experience you will ever experience on a rollercoaster that will leave you questioning why there’re not more of these?! If intensity is what you’re looking for this will likely be in your top 5!
I had the opportunity to ride it on my last travel to Japan, I really enjoyed the “4D” elements Ps 1st review

Katun is one of the most underrated rollercoasters in all of Europe. It is unusually tall and the speed at which you take the inversions on this ride is unreal. The cobra roll hammers you into your seat, while the zero-g-roll gives the complete opposite sensation of weightlessness Obviously the comfort is amazing, as is expected of a B&M invert like this. I really do believe this is the best coaster in the park, and that is not a diss to iSpeed. It's just that good.

This is an absolute titan of an inverted coaster. The scale of these elements give it a slightly slower pace compared to the smaller, more rapid-fire inverts like Nemesis or the Batman clones, but it compensates with a greater sense of speed. The first drop, and the drop off the MCBR are also surprisingly decent airtime moments for a ride of this kind.

It's arguably the best invert in Europe, maybe in the world. Idk why people seem to prefer Black mamba, Oziris or Nemesis (the most disappointing coaster in my life) over it. Of course it lacks airtime but it's still an invert! Rattle is not noticeable (like the one on ispeed) and I don't know why there are SO many people in the reviews saying it's forceless or "ispeed is miles better". Katun is now my favorite ride in Italy even if I like launched coasters more, because Ispeed was rattling too much to be enjoyable, while katun is just amazing in every aspect.
Simply the best inverted coaster I’ve ever ridden!!
Best coaster in italy no doubt!!!
This has to be the best coaster in  italy! one of the most intense in the contry featuring a very long track ans well as breathtaking inversions. the theming needs some maintenance.
It's the best B&M inverted and overall coaster I have ridden! Love the forcefull and smooth layout. The lovely roar is hearable all over the park.
Probably the best inverted coaster in the world. A true masterpiece.

Man alive, Katun is INTENSE. Like, really intense, to the point it was almost too much. I'm not that big on crazy intense rides, hence I've listed it as a positive and a negative. There's no denying though that this is a very good layout, the inversions all try to rip your head off with sheer power, particularly the cobra roll which is bone crushing. The zero g roll was really good too, very whippy and perfect weightlessness. The first drop is also incredible, it feels like you're dropping for miles, particularly in the back, yoy just keep going and going. The park have retrofitted some extra padding to the headrests and restraints, which is welcome as it definitely has a bit of a rattle in places, its an older ride now of course but with all that intensity it isn't ideal. Katun is absolutely a monster of a coaster though, and I can absolutely see how it could be someones favourite invert if you really like the big positives
Very intense, best first drop in an inverted hands down. Fun to ride, the queue is usually not that long because it can board a lot of people at once. First row is the best. Underrated.
Best coaster in Italy IMO, buttery smooth and with a very fun although not showy (good thing) layout. Only con I'd say are the operations: a bit messy and often 1 train only.
The best coaster in the park—and the best inverted coaster I’ve ever tried!

For me, Katun was easily the highlight of Mirabilandia, even my favorite coaster of our coaster tour through Northern Italy:
This massive invert reminds me a bit of Monster at Walygator, but even taller and faster. The sense of speed is relentless and every element is taken with a lot of force - I particularly enjoyed the first two inversions (I absolutely love a good zero-G-roll in general). It is a great ride, but there are also some minor flaws: Katun is the roughest B&M invert I've been on, in some rows, I had a little headbanging. Nothing dramatic, but the rattle detracts from the experience. Additionally, the station building and the surrounding area is nicely themed, but during the layout, there is no decoration. Operations were painfully slow (with only one train running), but it was also hampered by other park guests behaving foolish...
But nevertheless, Katun is an absolute beast of intensity which is worth the way to Mirabilandia!

There is a separate front row queue which allows you to choose, and I approve of this. I choose front. Despite that slightly disappointing feeling of being held back past the pre-drop and the first few metres of the main hill, by the time you hit the bottom you are going FAST. The whole scale of this B&M seems bigger than others. It has less punch around the tight elements than say Montu which I felt was trying to pull my body apart in the cobra roll. But due to the high speed and fantastic interactions with the ground this is a truly excellent ride. Some genuinely scary leg choppers. 


It’s smooth and despite the OTSR I never had any discomfort.

The first drop in the back rows is really top notch. You can’t appreciate the subsequent terrain in the same way, but it’s still an amazingly good ride. But the front row is next level for me. I did notice a scratch on my elbow and it wasn’t until later when I got a second one that I realised it was from the foliage near this ride. Get gardening Mirabilandia!

This coaster will always hold a special place in my heart as the one that made me conquer me fear of rollercoasters. I got to ride it again this year and still love it, however I have to say that some rows are more rattly than others. Still my favorite B&M though.

It was such a great esperience riding this.
Coming from gardaland where I tried blu tornado which was awful this was on another level.
I hope this coaster will last forever because in italy we dont have many good coasters such as this

This is everything you want in an Invert. Height, speed and amazing inversions. The Corkscrew right before the tunnel is outstanding! Only the pace is less because of the humongous elements, but with a lay-out like this isn't a problem at all!
Awesome coaster
That is an insane invert! It's intense, has some great inversions and the pacing is really good, it feels fast.

I LOVE Katun, it was my first ever inverted coaster and it's so much fun! It's a long ride with good pacing, tho it has gotten a bit rough over time (2025). It's also very intense in the back row, it really wants to rip your face off, so I cant really reride it sadly

my first ever inverted coaster and it's still the best!
surprisingly long,intense with a great layout and inversions,jt's a very fun and enjoyable ride.
the theming area where the coaster is located would be awasome if only the maintance would be good as the coaster is

I dont't know why everyone likes this ride that much.  It's intense, wich is caused by the constantly high g-forces, but you get no airtime and no hangtime aswell although there are six inversions. But the saddest point is that i noticed that one year operatimg made a huge difference in terms of the ride's rattling. Last year I did not feel any kind of rattle, but this year I felt a not so nice rattle, wich didn't make the ride unrideable, but unpleasant. And the reliability of this coaster is bad too.

The best ride in Italy in my opinion. There is nothing I could say against it. Incredible inversions, nice first drop and intense positives. Every element is amazing, some of the rolls even have some nice airtime and the ride has some of the best theming in the park on top of that. I loved it a lot so it’s an easy 10/10 for me
Top tier invert. Nobody talks about it, yet it's absolutely awesome. Each inversion is very whippy and the ride as a whole is extremely forceful. The drop is also my favorite one on an invert.

Waited  2 hours the first time i rode it, i was tired hungry, and just sleep deprived (dont car camp, not a good idea) and when that first drop happened, i woke up, and i was horrified, and secretly having the best time of my life
This feels like mini i305
Holy hell.
Maverick is a great coaster

My choice for the closest thing to a perfect roller coaster. There's an innate feel for setup and payoff on this layout that is very special - and a dissonance between the precision with which each element is delivered against the batshit out of control feel of the ride that is intoxicating. The second launch is one of the great dramatic moments on any ride. There are coasters with stronger positives, negatives, or laterals but I've personally never been on one that blends all three so seamlessly and leaves me dying to get on it again the way Maverick does.
If only there was a way to not have trims. And a heartline roll. ...anniversary retrack?
Ride this at night, its a whole different experience
One of the very few roller coasters where it looks a lot more tame then it actually is. You really feel the speed of the ride for the entire time.

This is an excellent compliment to Steel Vengeance.  This is one of the best one-two punches in a specific area of a park, let alone an entire park.  The first drop is so much fun since you launch up the hill and go beyond vertical during the drop.  It has great twists and turns, along with a couple of amazing ejector hills in the first and second half.  I loved the launch to break up the halves halfway through the ride.  It seems deceptive, like the ride is over, then launches you into another intense half.  I definitely prefer the first half to the second.  The launch might be great with a hard banked left turn, but that brake at the top of the hill is such a momentum killer.  I would have also preferred a more unique second half (it seems repetitive to the elements in the first), but it's still a ton of fun.  4.5/5 stars

I absolutely adore this ride. I came in with absolutely no idea what this ride did, and I think that really helped the experience I had with this ride. I came in with high expectations after what I heard of this ride, and it has blown those expectations out of the water. The ride is so intense, but the whips feel so natural at the same time. The second launch was super punchy too, and loved how it went under the station. Also something to mention is that it's glass smooth, more smooth then new B&Ms

My most recent rides on Maverick shocked me. Before, this ride was just outside of my top 15, but now it is easily my favorite Intamin. It blends airtime, intensity, and inversions into a perfect layout. Don't let the ride directly next to it overshadow this awesome coaster.

Maverick is my favorite coaster at Cedar Point. All the elements are fantastic, but it's the non-stop pacing of the entire ride that really makes it so incredible. This is about as perfect as a coaster gets.
Yes, it is a good ride, but is it that good? It is undoubtedly a good ride, but it doesn't live up to all the hype.

If I could describe Maverick in one word, it would be AGGRESSIVE. My very first ever ride on Maverick was at night. And WHAT A RIDE. I was deeply unprepared for what was in store for me. I was laughing maniacally the entire ride out of sheer surprise. You have no idea what is coming next. The whips and change in direction are incredible. But the star of the show is that second launch. Especially at night, nothing can prepare you for a 0 to 70 in 3 seconds launch that IMMEDIATELY banks you left with a SNAP. Intamin was absolutely diabolical for that. Loved Maverick so much. My only criticism is that at 6'5", the shoulder harness hurts something awful after multiple rides.
NIGHT RIDE NIGHT RIDE NIGHT RIDE!!! Just pure, utter fun. There's nothing more to it!

This is in my opinion, the 2nd best coaster at Cedar Point and 2nd best in Ohio, just behind Steel Vengeance. This ride was SO MUCH more intense than I though and I LOVED IT! The 2nd launch in the tunnel was absolutely amazing, and the inversions and snappy turns were some of the best I've ever felt on any ride. This is one if Intamin's best coasters ever! 9/10!
Worth the wait, hope they add the heartline roll!

Maverick is an outstanding ride and currently my #2 rollercoaster.  I love the variety of elements:  the quick turns, the amazing air time hill, the twisted horseshoe roll, the 2nd launch from the tunnel, the Stengel dives.  I also love how the ride isn't that tall and doesn't really look that impressive from the pathways.  It's definitely a big surprise once you ride it.  The only thing that prevented this from being my #1 is that I think it could use a couple more elements.  It's pretty well known that the heartline roll was removed from the ride.  I think that if 2nd half still had a heartline roll and maybe another air time hill, that could have been enough to push it into my #1 spot.  One annoying thing about this ride is that it always seems to have a long line.  I managed to get 2 rides on this early before the line got long.  Unless you ride this one early or close to closing time, it always seemed to have a wait of at least an hour.
The most intense coaster I’ve ridden. This coaster is amazing

In my eyes this is a near perfect ride. Incredibly intense with brilliant pacing. It's one of the smoothest coasters I've ever ridden, which is impressive considering it's age. The only things letting it down are the restraints and capacity. The soft straps are definitely better than the older generation Intamin OTSRs, but they're still bulky and uncomfortable for anyone taller than average.
Yeehaw

I expected this to be good when I rode it.  However, I was not prepared for just how amazing this coaster is.  I have only ridden it twice, both times the same day.  An added bonus to this wonderful ride, is that the rides I experienced were different.  At one of the "launch barns" where you get launched again midcourse, I had two different experiences.  The first ride, we basically came to stop before launching back out to finish the ride.  On the next ride, we didn't slow down through the barn.  We just accelerated seamlessly.  This difference in ride experiences adds a bit of extra flavor to an already very spicy ride.  The pacing is phenomenal.  It has you twisting and turning and flipping constantly all at a really good clip.  It is a very intense ride.  Which for me, translates to smiles.  Even with all of these high speed transitions, it remains remarkable smooth throughout.  Add in the location over the water with all of the canyon structures they built to have you fly by, and you have a recipe for a world class thrill machine.  This ride truly delivers the goods.  Great time for sure.
It’s Js good

Maverick is a speed machine. I love how smooth this coaster is despite the aggressive turns and dips featured throughout. The first drop is fantastic and the layout is compact yet expansive. I also appreciated that the main launch occurs midway through the ride, which I was not expecting. A great surprise.

This is another one of the three coasters I consider absolutely perfect. This ride is not talked about enough for its many wonderful feats. The restraints allow you to receive a ton of room, allowing you to feel the abundant, incredible airtime to its full potential. Weaving through the structure with the orange lights at night has to be one of the most magical experiences on a coaster. (Rating: 10/10)

GhostRider is a great ride. Although I am typically disappointed by my morning rides, I found my last ride to be pretty great. The ride has fun airtime and some wicked lateral moments. The only downside to this fun coaster is the trash capacity, while it has certainly gotten better; it is still far from ideal, but I certainly enjoy my rides on this coaster when it is not 90 minutes.
Worlds best wooden coaster... BY FAR

Ghostrider is definitely the best wooden coaster I've ridden. The first half can be hit or miss depending on how fast it's running, but the fantastic second half always makes up for it with those crazy airtime hills that leave you floating for what feels like forever and those crazy lateral forces that you feel while flying through the structure of the coaster with some of the best pacing out there. The only big downside is the horrible operations that make the line take 2 hours most of the time. Other than that, it's a fantastic wooden coaster and it's ranked among the best of them for a reason.
As a coaster enthusiast with 63 credits this is my favorite coaster just ride in the back at night and you’ll see
The laterals reminds me of getting slammed to the side of a bobsled at high speeds

I used to find this very disappointing and overrated until it gave me the best night ride I have ever had and I totally understand the praise. The crazy layout and airtime is insane especially in the dark and when it has warmed up though it can be weak in the morning. Has some dead spots and I’m not a fan of the slow turnarounds and final helix which kill the pacing.
Just a great woodie. Pacing, layout, laterals, airtime, drops. It’s a damn good coaster.

An absolute masterpiece of a ride. The layout is an out of control blitz of airtime and laterals, all while being the smoothest wooden coaster I've ridden so far. The helix finale is spectacular, it'll fold you over sideways in the best way.
Night rides on a good day, this is my #1 wood. Genius layout for a flat plot of land, just enough great presentation. Wish it was run better.

GhostRider converted me to a roller coaster enthusiast. It was my first big roller coaster outside of my home park, and it showed me how good roller coasters can be. Me and my family have returned to Knotts Berry Farm to ride it every year since we first rode because it's just that good. And, in spring 2026, I finally got a night ride and it shot into my top 10! GhostRider during the day is awesome, but at night it's a complete sensory overload. This will always be one of my favorite roller coasters, it really is something special!

So Fun! Recommended if you are okay with a rattle. For my rides it Rattled insanely and the ejector airtime, mid-course drop, and aggressive second half were so fun. Get to this ride first. Lines get long
WOW! Worth The WAIT! Best coaster in California! So many intense laterals! Top 3 wooden coaster layout of all time. Also happens to be my #1!
Griddle123 has ridden this ride

This is undoubtedly Knott's best coaster. Wooden coasters are supposed to rough, BUT THIS ONE IS ACTUALLY SMOOTH. Even after 10 years of being retracked it STILL feels smooth. It's pure fun, that's all I can say.
the best wooden coaster in the west in my opinion should definitely ride
Amazing ride especially in the dark, insane laterals and some great floater airtime. The queue was way too long glad I had fast track

This is my favorite wooden roller coaster and it’s not even that close (keep in mind have not done voyage, el toro, mystic timbers and haven’t ridden anything outside of the United States) This was my first big coaster as well and one of the two rides that made me an enthusiast. Overall this ride gives more than 14 moments of airtime (cough cough rcdb) and is the best ride at Knotts and the best ride ever in the state. This year it is running the best I have ever seen it run and I think next year it’s somehow going to be even better. Ps: if you ride it and you don’t think it’s that good ride it at night and you will understand.
GhostRider is my all-time favorite coaster.
GhostRider, at night and in the back row. There’s nothing like it. This roller coaster deserves its praise! Hang TF on!
This ride throws you around so much while not being too rough and giving airtime.
A bit rattly but still fairly smooth for a woodie, amazing airtime and lots of fun. Laterals were great as well. Worth the very long wait lol
My favorite coaster of all time! So much fun. Riding in the back row at night is an incredible and intense experience.

Feels like a miracle that this coaster exists in its current form. The second drop down the ravine is stunning - its unique profiling at the top creates shocking airtime on the way down as it dives right into Thunderbolt's structure. It's right there with X2 and Skyrush as my favorite drop on any roller coaster. The swooping turn that follows feels both forceful and graceful simultaneously and then the rest of the layout is wild - even the top RMCs can't quite reach the kind of diabolical ejector that Phantom delivers on its best rides. Kennywood has the best collection of lap bars and this one is essential to maximizing the experience. A true one of one coaster that feels like it could only be created by accident, and a perfect fit as the signature attraction for a park that feels as distinctive as Kennywood.

This ride is the equivalent of a toddler throwing a MASSIVE tantrum. The airtime was fun at the start but it became a little too aggressive towards the end. The lap bar was also ill-fitting and the seatbelt was not enough restraint to keep me comfortably in my seat. Giving it three stars solely because the first two drops are amazing, though. This is the first coaster where I've genuinely thought, 'I would not let my cat on this ride.' (Shout-out to Asher, the cat on my pfp) Edit: I was wrong. After a re-ride in May, I thought it got better. The airtime was less aggressive and the seatbelt fit better. By far a better ride now that I've been on this twice. I do think Steel Curtain is better, though. Still not letting Asher on this one. Edit 2: I re-rode again in July and it dipped in quality, and not in a small way. The first drop wasn't actually that good this time around. The airtime was back to being stupidly aggressive. It felt way shorter than it actually is. The second drop was the only redeeming factor because it was rip-the-leather-off-your-La-Z-Boy scary and fun. I'm in a love-hate relationship with this ride and I don't regret it.
ABSOLUTELY INSASE Coaster! The airtime is EXTREMELY strong, and the pace and speed of it is UNREAL! By far, the 2nd best Coaster in Pennsylvania behind Skyrush. 10/10
This ride is perfect. The speed and the drops are amazing. I wish it was a little bit longer, but other than that, this coaster is underrated.
The crown jewel of Kennywood. The top dog. Simply does not get better than this for me. This ride and its predecessor started my love of coasters. And now it's purple too.
Some of the BEST ejector airtime in the world and is definitely underrated.

Phantom's Revenge is simply a perfect coaster. Its sense of speed is phenomenal; there are so many quality ejector airtime moments on this ride, and don't even get me started on the finale that alone might be the best series of elements in Pennsylvania. It's incredibly smooth and comfortable, as someone who is tall and finds many rides to be a little "tight," Phantom's Revenge always was to accommodate my size. Also, I personally find it hilarious that the restraint is basically a pool noodle.

I was a bit disappointed in my rides on Phantom's Revenge.  The ride is intense and delivers some amazing air time.  I also love the first 2 drops, especially the 2nd one.  The main problem was with the lap bar.  My body kept slamming into it during the ride.  I even tried pulling the seat belt as tight as possible, but that didn't solve the problem.  My only decent ride was when I pressed my thighs tightly against the lap bar and maintained that pressure for the whole ride.  While this seemed to mostly solve the issue, I didn't enjoy having to do that.  Maybe I'm just spoiled by B&M hypers and their very comfortable clamshell restraints.  In any case, the lap bar ruined what should have been an amazing ride.

This ride did absolutely nothing to me. Yeah it's smoother than expected, but it's all fast turns and some airtime hills that last less than a quarter of second. The restraints are not the best in curculations. I don't know I don't get the hype.

I tagged it 'first drop' but really it's the second drop off the clip through Thunderbolt, holy crap is that awesome.  

The rest of the ride is boring and painful.  I don't know what they were thinking removing the inversions in the second half- the new design is more boring and rougher.  A few seconds in and I was just wishing the ride would end.

The first drop is also just weird..  nice twisting drop into....  a completely flat straight section?  Feels like it's just begging for a loop, or at least put a little airtime bump/drop in!  

A very confusing coaster, feels like it was designed by drunk middle managers
One of a kind. Amazing layout and airtime.

Phantom’s Revenge is smooth, big, fast, and a rush. It feels super solid from the track to the cars, there’s no rattle or hint of movement to the track. I love the first half with the slow clack lift hill, swooping first drop, rush of speed on a straightaway up into a hilltop before the largest plunge. It is big and classy and a joy to ride, which is why I saved it for my 100th coaster credit.
The fact that this used to be a rough Arrow looper amazes me. It is so fast and fun with ejector airtime rivaling that of Magnum.
Great ride with an awesome sense of speed in the first half and great airtime in the second half.

Lot to say about this ride. First of all the lap bars are unique and minimalistic and surprisingly the station is designed so you can choose which row to go to. The ride is very smooth and the first drop gives much speed for the ride to zoom up and suddenly fall into a large second drop, intertwining with Thunderbolt as it goes down then up into a graceful turn with wind blowing up onto the train. The second half after that is unpleasant thought as the train goes up and down throwing you up to be caught by the lap  bar.

This ride has one of the most lenient lap bars out there. Due to this, it greatly enhances the airtime. This ride is essentially one-of-a-kind and an incredible coaster, feeling very fast, having great drops, and being surprisingly smooth.

I meannnnnnn it’s an amazing ride Kennywood deserves this one, but would love to either see a new rmc entirely behind black widow and another terrain of that cliff or near the the right side of Jack rabbit
Definitely not as good at steel curtain, too rough but isn't a terrible layout (with the exception of the two doubles). This belongs nowhere near the top 100..probably not even top 500.
By first drop I mean second drop. It's very fun and the lap bars are basically pool noodles
Nothing wrong but steel curtains better
Fun ride but the end is very whiplash inducing
Such a cool backstory for this coaster! Turning a rough old coaster into a airtime Machine, makes this an RMC before RMC!
Maybe a bit overrated but had some of the most violent airtime I’ve ever seen. I think it’s closer between this and steel curtain than I would’ve expected.

Unbeknownst to me, this coaster has a nasty trim brake around the double down, and that was a big disappointment for me, as the airtime for this ride had been hyped up ridiculously. Still, this is an excellent coaster. Minimalist restraints, awesome terrain layout, and a unique experience overall. Awesome second drop, huge sweeping turns, and then intense nonstop ejector airtime until you hit the final brakes. Excellent ride.

Mecalodon is an excellent family coaster with amazing theming. The launches are punchy and the rest of the layout has many amazing airtime hills. The s-bends over the water are also great. The pace is also good because of the launches.
It's wild, it's a thing. Second half was slow, but was still a fun ride.
Pulsar has some cool launches and good airtime moments. The spikes are really nice and the ride is very comfortable.
The launch is amazing and the loop is really intense and because of the darkness very disorientating. The ride is very short but otherwise would the capacity be bad.

Tiki waka is a great family coaster with great theming. The ride has some good drops that give nice airtime and some of the turns give good laterals. It is really smooth but the capacity is bad so the line can be very long.
This ride is a fun coaster that is very long and has great theming. The layout has some nice moments but it is a bit rough.
